### 8.3 MARGOT LINDQVIST
**Full name:** Margot Ingrid Lindqvist. Born **December 21, 1990** (winter solstice; she considers this a personal brand) —
18 at move-in, 19 in S1E22. Portland, Oregon (Laurelhurst). Lincoln High School '09. Gender and Women's Studies, minor
in Journalism. Delgado Hall 305 (a single; her mother called Residential Life).

**Family.** Mother **Dr. Ingrid Lindqvist**, Reed College, Classics (so Margot can out-Greek Lena when she bothers).
Father **Dr. Paul Hirsch-Lindqvist**, Portland State, Sociology. Open marriage, conducted like a seminar. 🔒 Margot's
mother had a second-trimester abortion in 2000 after a prenatal diagnosis of Down syndrome; the boy would have been
named Anders. Margot, then nine, was told everything in age-appropriate language at the kitchen table. She has defended
her mother's choice in every forum since and has privately grieved Anders every year on the date.

**Public face.** Militant feminist atheist. Clove cigarettes (Djarum Black — the FDA flavored-cigarette ban takes effect
**September 22, 2009** and she holds a wake). Writes for *The Marisol Tide*. Keeps a running score on the Delgado lounge
whiteboard: "USEFUL IDIOTS FOR CHRISTIAN NATIONALISM." Regularly accuses Lena of internalized misogyny, Jack of upholding
the patriarchy, and both of being useful idiots for Christian nationalism. Becomes, for reasons none of them can explain,
one of their closest friends for life.

**Private truth. 🔒** She's lonely in a way her parents' freedom taught her to call independence. She has watched her
mother humiliated in her own kitchen by her father's "honesty." She envies Jack and Lena's certainty and hates that she
does. Anders. She is bisexual and has never said so to anyone, because in her family it would be met with a *reading
list*. She is the best investigator in the show.

**Wound.** Anders. Her parents' freedom.

**Want vs. need.** *Want:* to win. *Need:* to be accompanied without being argued with.

**Voice.** Deadpan, polysyllabic, merciless, footnoted. Uses academic jargon on purpose and knows how it sounds
("heteronormative," "problematize," "hegemonic," "praxis" — she's allowed 2009 jargon and is mocked for it). Never
raises her voice. Insults as diagnoses. Humor bone-dry and frequently cruel; when she's kind she pretends it's research.
- *"St. Michael. Patron saint of what, bouncers?"*
- *"You're a Catholic at a kegger. Which one of us is the anthropologist?"*
- *"I'm not cold. I'm Scandinavian. It's a different thing."*
- *"You're going to be one of those Catholics who's fun. Those are the dangerous ones."*
- *"Lena, I say this with love: you've internalized a two-thousand-year-old men's club and you call it a personality."*
- True register: *"Can you just — sit here. Don't talk. I'll know if you're praying."*

**Look (brief).** Severe Scandinavian. White-blonde hair cut blunt at the jaw, very pale, thick black-framed glasses, all
black clothing, Doc Martens (oxblood, the only color she owns). Seems to have no body temperature. **Phone:** a Nokia
brick she uses mainly as a paperweight.

**Arc.** S1: the antagonist who keeps showing up; the clove wake (E07); she and Lena's 2 a.m. abortion argument that ends
with both of them crying and neither conceding. S2: starts the Nora anniversary feature for the *Tide*. S3: dates Evan
Marsh (not her TA) and gets closer to the truth than anyone. S4: publishes — responsibly, and it forces the reckoning; she
is right, and it costs Jack and Lena everything for a while. (She likes Julian and tells Jack he's the healthiest thing in Lena's life — S1E16, and means it.) At the wedding (SU3) she signs the register as "witness for the prosecution." S5: the seal story; she and Jack fight about the confessional
like it's a war. She never converts. Adulthood: an investigative reporter (ProPublica-type); godmother to one of Jack
and Lena's children, at her insistence, "as a hedge."
**Anders, as she tells it (E07 plan — the Delgado roof, Wed Sep 23, ~3 a.m., to Lena, Jack and Kevin; 🔒 until then).**
Spring 2000; Margot was nine. Her mother was forty-one; an amniocentesis at about sixteen weeks; trisomy 21. Her parents
decided at the kitchen table and told Margot the same night "in age-appropriate language" (her father's phrase, which she
quotes like a diagnosis). They had already picked the name: Anders. The procedure was on **March 15, 2000** — "the ides; my
father pointed that out; he thought it was interesting." She has defended her mother's choice in every forum since, and
means it; she keeps the date alone every year, and nobody has said his name aloud since 2000 but her. **Never a strawman
in either direction:** she is not converted, softened or "won"; she grieves a brother and defends her mother in the same
breath, and the show holds both. **The same night, after Kevin walks her down, Kevin comes out to her** — the first person he
has ever told (🔒 off-page; Jack sees them leave the roof together and reads it as a romance).
**(E11 plan:)** On the trip "as an observer" (the monks: "a functioning patriarchy in its natural habitat"; the faith column's monastery profile). In the van
she runs the *Tide*'s Ferrer follow-up as an interrogation (the police log — "one of them was laughing"; from 305 she heard the bass come in late twice;
"Costigan suggested Baptists. I've noted it.") and **writes nothing down.** At Vespers (fork) her arms come unfolded by the second psalm. At the Henry
Miller Library (fork) — the investigator, unprompted — she tells Theo he leaves every Sunday before dawn (she saw the SL go at 2:40 in Malibu, E03, and
she doesn't sleep); she lets his pitch go. At the motel she reads Lena's copy of Dorothy Day's *The Long Loneliness* by flashlight (one line aloud: love
comes with community), sees Jack go out to the porch and Lena follow, and Sunday at the coffee urn says only **"I'm not writing anything down."** In the
turnouts she becomes a Saints fan against her will. Says the balloon was a hoax exactly once: "I said it was too calm."
**(E12 plan:)** **Joan of Arc** — cardboard and silver duct-tape armor over her black, a wooden sword, and her own white-blonde jaw-length bob, which
turns out to be Joan's haircut exactly ("burned as a heretic in 1431, canonized in 1920; I'm both categories; so was the Church"); horns at the door
("the verdict of 1431"). Supplies Laney's Pope Joan footnote and loses the sources argument to Jack and Lena. At the costume reveal: **"Between the two
of them there's one functioning farm."** Best Couple with Laney — "This is a category error." (her suppressed laugh). The investigator, unprompted:
**"Your host left his own party at twelve-thirty. Out the back gate. Toward Seacliff."** (fork A: "Kevin hasn't taken that mask off in four hours." 🔒).
Writes nothing down when the DJ plays the Saints.
**(E13 plan:)** Monday's whiteboard: **HALLOWEEN — AMERICAN GOTHIC (UNPLANNED) · BOTH**. Sully's "for the anthropology." At the Harbor Inn she
interviews Caroline about the 1980s nighttime soap "as a text" and enjoys herself; after Jack's answer to Caroline: "That was very gallant,
Costigan. Gallantry is a system for deciding things on other people's behalf." (She is right about something.) She sees Kevin watch Maine
(🔒 one look; says nothing).
**(E14 plan:)** 🔒 Wednesday, Maine decided: she sets a coffee at Kevin's elbow and says nothing. **The fire-alarm sting fails** (#28): Sat night in
the 4th-floor lounge with Theo's 5D on a tripod and Gold Bond on the pull handle; asleep at 2:50 for the first time in recorded history; Alarm 4 at
3:11 from the east stair (26 days); she stares at the timestamp of her own sleep and never looks at the bottom of the frame (🔒 the heel, the pillow —
Doug, E20). Saturday night by phone to Lena at the Anchor counter, furious about Stupak, **with her best argument** (it isn't federal money; it reaches
into private plans on the exchange that women pay for themselves) — never a strawman; Lena gives her the point and not the baby. At Sully's, of the
courtesy war: **"It's a potlatch. They're destroying property to establish rank."**

### 8.4 KEVIN TRAN
**Full name:** Kevin Minh Tran (Vietnamese name Trần Minh Khang). Born **February 15, 1991** (Tết, the Year of the
Goat; family lore) — 18 at move-in. San Jose (Evergreen). Bellarmine College Prep '09. Biology, pre-med. Delgado Hall
420, with Doug Pruitt.

**Family.** Father **Trần Văn Hùng** ("Henry"), 58, came by boat in 1979 at age 28 after re-education camp, Pulau Bidong
refugee camp, now owns two nail-salon supply stores. Mother **Nguyễn Thị Lan** ("Lan"), 53, pharmacist at a Walgreens.
Sister **Thủy** ("Tina"), 24, dental school at UOP. Grandmother **Bà Nội** (Trần Thị Mai), 81, prays the rosary in
Vietnamese at 5 a.m. Parish: Our Lady of La Vang, San Jose.

**Public face.** Gym-built pre-med, the nicest guy in any room, Newman stalwart, the one who knows everybody's name and
birthday and remembers your mom's surgery. Altar server, lector, intramural flag football. Dad jokes. Iron-clad public
persona.

**Private truth. 🔒** Kevin is gay and out to exactly one person, Margot (week four of S1 — before that, no one). He came to
Marisol's Preview Weekend in April 2009, met a blond LA kid on the beach stairs behind the Lighthouse, and kissed a boy
for the first time; they had about an hour. That boy was Theo. Around 12:45 a.m. Theo knocked on the door of Kevin's
host's room in Serra Hall, soaked to the knees, his hands scraped raw, holding a woman's denim jacket, and said, "You
never saw me." Kevin let him sleep on the floor. In the morning a girl was dead. Kevin has never asked. He has never told.
He pretends, when they "meet" on Jack's first night, that he's never seen Theo before. Theo pretends too.

**Wound.** The family's sacrifice is a debt he can't repay and can't refuse. Being loved for a person he isn't.

**Want vs. need.** *Want:* to be good — perfectly, visibly good — so that nothing else can be seen. *Need:* to be loved as
he is by someone who isn't lying either.

**Voice.** Sunny, dad-joke, team-captain. Bay Area "hella" when relaxed (rarely). Organizes things. Medical vocabulary
as comedy ("That's a textbook case of acute Theo"). Under the sunshine a scalpel: the occasional line so precise it
draws blood, followed instantly by a smile. Code-switches to Vietnamese with family; his Vietnamese is worse than he
pretends.
- *"Two truths and a lie: I'm pre-med, I'm an only child, I've never been to a party."*
- *"Respectfully, bro, that's not a hangover, that's a cry for help with a headache."*
- *"I don't drink at these. I'm the designated adult. It's like being designated driver but for your soul."*
- True register: *"You think I don't know what people see? I built what people see. I'm good at it."*

**Look (brief).** Gym-built pre-med. Compact and muscular, a crew cut, an athletic quarter-zip (a collection: navy,
gray, Bellarmine maroon, Stanford-Medicine-summer-program cardinal), a big easy smile that never quite reaches his eyes.
(The brief's phrase; the only sanctioned use.) **Phone:** BlackBerry Bold.

**The alliance.** Kevin is the one who tries to get Theo and Laney to leave Jack and Lena alone ("Respectfully, this is
a hostage situation"); both refuse; he keeps trying, every season, and is in on the joke at the reveal.

**Arc (revised for the player's directive: a long struggle, shaped heavily by his friendship with Jack and Lena, with real
back-and-forth — brief departures from the Church, a same-sex relationship or two, other lapses, a sad attempt with a girl —
before he finally settles as a celibate gay Catholic. Full cost, compassion, no easy answers either way, no mouthpieces.)**
S1: the mask; **out to Margot the night of the clove wake (E07; off-page; Jack misreads them as a couple and teases them
both)**; a stairwell fight with Theo Jack half-hears (E16). S2: Newman VP; pressure from Peter Haddad; Margot as confessor;
**the sad, sincere attempt with a girl** (a Newman sophomore, Clare Dominguez, S2E04–E13 — she deserved better and knew it
within a month; nobody is a villain). S3: comes out to Jack and Lena (they love him, and say the hard true thing, and stay;
Margot is loudly offended on his behalf — at the teaching, and at them). S4: when the Nora case reopens, his night with Theo
becomes evidence — he must decide whether to be a witness and out himself to his family; he does. S5: his father stops
speaking to him; Bà Nội does not. He tries celibacy and the sacraments in earnest, and it doesn't hold yet. S6–S7: a
relationship with a man (Andrés, a med student — kind, serious, not a villain) and a year away from Mass (a semester at the
Episcopal parish in Las Olas). S8: he comes back to sit in the back pew on Holy Thursday 2013. Adulthood: a second
relationship ends; he settles — by his own decision, at full cost — as a celibate gay Catholic; an ER doctor (Osei's
vocation, inherited); godfather to one of Jack and Lena's children. He tells them they are the reason he could imagine it.
**Margot** never accepts the teaching and says so at every table for twenty years, and comes to accept and respect that Jack
and Lena genuinely love him ("I hate that it's real. It's real."). The show accompanies him; it never pretends the cost is
small, and never pretends the life is a defeat.
**(E11 plan:)** Drives his mother's Odyssey ("SPEED: 55 ON HWY 1. NOT 56." on the laminated card; "Switzerland has a *seating policy*"); hands Lena a
roll of quarters for the payphone without being asked; white to the lips when the van boils over ("My mother is going to know. She'll feel it in San
Jose."); "Second gear. The whole way." 🔒 One line only: when Laney's room chart puts him and Theo in the one bed in cabin 5, "I'll take the floor" — at
the same instant Theo says "I'll take the van." Never touched again.
**(E12 plan:)** "**All Saints** — every one nobody's heard of. It's tomorrow; I'm early.": scrubs from the summer program, a halo from Theo's box, and
**a plain white mask he never takes off** until Delgado's door at 2:45 a.m. (🔒 one image; Margot notices on fork A). Alliance: "Respectfully, this is a
hostage situation" (once, at Theo's legal pad). The designated adult at a party of four thousand: **he finds Laney at Lupe's** and calls Lena. On the
path where Jack carries Theo's lie ("Looking for Laney"), Kevin looks at Jack through the eyeholes for a long second and says nothing (🔒 he knows
what Theo looks like when he comes back from somewhere at night).
**(E13 plan:)** quarter-zips again; the mask is gone. The objector at the false dawn: **"Respectfully — her boyfriend broke up with her eleven
hours ago."** (the only voice in 412 on the side of Jack's wait, though nobody knows it's a side). At the Harbor Inn, Maine's Question 1 on the
bar TV — too close to call — and **Kevin's face** (🔒 one image; Margot sees it).
**(E14 plan:)** "Respectfully — leave it alone." (once, at the ficus); 🔒 Maine decided — the quarter-zip zipped to the chin in the sun; Margot's coffee;
at Alarm 4 the clipboard; **lector at the 9 p.m. Mass, reading the November names — *Nora Calloway* twice, because two hands wrote it, steadily** (🔒).

### 8.5 FR. GABRIEL OSEI
**Full name:** Rev. Gabriel Kofi Osei. Born **May 2, 1964**, Kumasi, Ghana — 45 at the pilot. MB ChB, University of Ghana
Medical School (Korle-Bu), 1989. Internal medicine. Ordained 2003 for the Diocese of Monterey (Marisol falls within it);
chaplain of St. Brendan the Navigator Newman Center since 2006.

**Public face.** Warm, unflappable, laughs from the belly, sees through everyone. A former physician. Fixes the courtyard
sprinkler himself in clerical shirt and rubber boots. Gives short homilies with one sentence you can't stop hearing.
Confessions Saturdays 3:30–4:45 "or whenever you knock — I was a doctor, I am used to being woken." Plays Ghanaian
highlife in his office loudly. Beats students at chess and lets them think it was close. A slight limp he never explains.

**Private truth. 🔒** He was married. **Abena Osei** (née Mensah), a schoolteacher, died on November 14, 1997, on the
Accra–Tema motorway, when Gabriel, driving her to the hospital in labor with their second child, swerved to avoid an
overturned tro-tro. The baby girl (they had named her Esi) died with her. His left leg was crushed; hence the limp. He
was the doctor in the car and could do nothing. Their son **Kwame**, then eight, was sent to Abena's sister in London
(Peckham) while Gabriel recovered — and then Gabriel went to seminary instead of bringing him home. Kwame, now 20, at the
London School of Economics, has not spoken to his father in four years. Gabriel writes him every month.

He holds two sealed confessions about the same night at the Point (🔒 §20): Lena's (April 26, 2009) and Theo's (July
2009). He knows more about Nora Calloway's death than anyone alive except Theo, and he will never say a word of it. Not
to Jack, not to police, not to a judge. The show honors the seal absolutely; it costs him, publicly, in S5.

**Wound.** Abena, Esi, Kwame. The choice of the altar over his son.

**Want vs. need.** *Want:* to save them all. *Need:* to let God do it, and to be forgiven by his son.

**Voice.** Ghanaian English, unhurried, proverbial, mischievous; drops the occasional Twi word ("Ɛyɛ" — it is well;
"Me da wo ase" — thank you). Physician's metaphors. Asks questions instead of giving answers. Never preaches in
conversation; saves it for the pulpit and keeps it short there.
- *"I spent eight years listening to hearts with a stethoscope and six listening through a screen. The stethoscope lies
  less."*
- *"Youngstown? I know it only from the Springsteen song. Is it as sad as he says?"*
- *"That's not a hockey puck. I was a doctor. That's a ring. Or a tooth."*
- *"The Church is a hospital, my friend. Nobody is embarrassed to be sick in a hospital. Only here."*
- *"When a man jokes that much, it is because the truth is heavy and he is carrying it alone."*

**Look (brief).** Gentle and weathered. Medium height, thin, a graying beard, deep laugh lines, a slight limp he never
explains. Black clerical shirt, sleeves rolled; a wooden rosary on his belt; reading glasses on a cord.

**Osei and Hale, first meeting on the page (E08, Sat Oct 3, the Blessing of the Animals in St. Brendan's courtyard).** Two men
who have heard a great deal about each other — Osei has read *The Consolations of Disbelief* "twice; the second time for the
footnotes"; Hale has heard Osei's homilies "secondhand, from students, which is how the Gospels arrived, I'm told." Hale brings
Bishop Berkeley "to annoy the Ghanaian": **"He's deaf, Father. You'll have to bless him louder."** Osei kneels — slowly; the bad
leg — lays his palm flat on the old dog's ribs and blesses him there, "where he can hear it" (a physician's hands). Then the
fencing: *esse est percipi* — "Then he exists only because Someone is looking at him. You named your dog after the best argument
for God an Irishman ever made." Hale gives the first half of Knox's limerick ("There was a young man who said, God…"); Osei
answers with the reply ("Dear Sir, your astonishment's odd…"). 🔒 When Osei opens the rite with "The Lord be with you," Hale's
lips answer **"And with thy spirit"** — the Prayer Book's response, not the Catholic one of 2009 — and nobody but Jack sees it (one
clause; no gloss; Compline stays S2). Neither man wins. Both enjoy it more than they will admit; this is the start of a long,
wary respect (S2 the Forum; S4 the call; AD the deathbed).
**(E11 plan:)** Thu Oct 22, the 12:10 (Luke 12:49–53, Researcher), one sentence: "He did not come to keep the peace in our houses. He came to keep the
peace in us, and sometimes the house pays for it." (🔒 Frank; never glossed.) Sat Oct 24, 7 a.m., the Anacapa lot, rubber boots, at Lena's request: **he
blesses Kevin's mother's Odyssey** — "I blessed a crab three weeks ago. A Honda is no trouble."
**(E12 plan:)** Fri Oct 30, the courtyard sprinkler in pieces (never fixed): lends Jack **the Newman shed's hoe** for St. Isidore ("Bring it back. The
sprinkler needs it."); the 1622 joke (Isidore canonized with Ignatius, Xavier, Teresa and Philip Neri — "four Spaniards and a saint"; Researcher);
tells Becca, gently, that Maria de la Cabeza was beatified rather than canonized (Researcher) — "She's a saint to *me*." Sun Nov 1, **All Saints**,
the 9:30: one sentence on 1 John 3:2 — *what we shall be has not yet been revealed; last night you all tried on a guess* (or the writer's better line).
**(E13 plan:)** All Souls: the Book of the Dead on its stand by the Marian shrine (St. Brendan's custom: the names are read at every Mass through
November). One line, to Jack, at the book: **"Write them all. He has a large book and a long memory."** (No 🔒 business at the book —
Abena and Esi stay S6.)
**(E14 plan:)** Thursday after the 12:10, Fort Hood breaking on Joey's phone in the courtyard: he takes them back inside to pray, the stole still on.
**Saturday 3:30 confessions** — Lena, then Jack (the seal: nothing of hers reaches Jack; his own is elided but for one line of Osei's). **The 5:00 vigil,
the widow's mite**, two sentences (Researcher: 1 Kgs 17 / Mark 12): she gave out of her want, not her surplus — *God has no use for your leftovers; he
wants the two coins you were keeping for yourself* (or the writer's better line).
**(E21 plan, rev. 2 — the player loves him; room given:)** Fri Dec 11, the Newman party: host — "You look like a man who has pushed a car… There's Lava under the kitchen sink."; the punch to the top of the refrigerator ("Gaudete is
Sunday, Miss Price. You're early."); the Watts argument ("Miss Broussard is correct, it is still Advent, and Mrs. Fitch is seventy-one. Sing."); the mistletoe ("I requested."); the spray tan ("In a drawer."). **The sink (new two-hander):**
cups and a dish towel; in Kumasi the waiting room was the most honest room in the hospital; "a guest who leaves before the singing is finished is either in love or in debt" / "I don't diagnose at parties"; a confiscation drawer ("very
ecumenical"); **his door is the one with the light on** (never anything from a confession). [optional, Spoiler Guard] a December airmail envelope to London on the sill (🔒 Kwame; no name; S3). Sat 5 a.m.: the back pew at the Mañanitas,
singing badly. **Sat 3:30, the box** (Jack's second Skye confession; Jack raises the hour himself; "a dose, not a cure… Can you?"; a Hail Mary "for whoever wrote the song") — **or, if Jack leaves the line, 4:45 at the courtyard wall
with a pipe wrench for the dead sprinkler: "Hold this." — and the offer of his office (two chairs side by side facing the crucifix; rubber boots; the highlife lifted off).** Sun: Gaudete — "Rejoice is a command, which means it isn't a
feeling. You can obey it on a bad week."

**Arc.** S1: the anchor, quietly watching his two penitents circle the boy he cannot warn. S2: the anniversary Mass at the
Point; Hale's public debate. S3: Kwame comes to Marisol (a conference) and refuses to see him; Jack brokers a dinner. S4:
Theo goes to police; Evan, then the press, realize Osei likely knew. S5: the seal on trial (Ireland's Cloyne Report and
Enda Kenny's speech, July 2011, make the seal front-page news); subpoenaed; refuses to testify about the content of a
confession; held in contempt; five nights in county jail; the Newman community splits. S6: the bishop wants to move him;
the students fight; he stays. Full run: he tells Jack the story of the limp in S6. SU3 (Sat July 21, 2012): he witnesses Jack and
Lena's vows at Holy Rosary (by the pastor's delegation). 🔒 Kwame comes to the wedding.

### 8.6 PROF. ADRIAN HALE
**Full name:** Adrian Charles Hale, D.Phil. Born **June 30, 1955**, Barnsley, South Yorkshire — 54 at the pilot. Balliol,
Oxford (PPE, then a D.Phil. on moral luck under Bernard Williams's shadow). Came to Marisol 1998 as the Whitcombe Chair in
Philosophy. Author of *The Consolations of Disbelief* (2006), a bestseller of the New Atheist wave, and three serious
books nobody buys. A regular on cable debates with apologists. Office: Hollis Hall 314, a window on the sea. Lives alone
in a cliffside bungalow in Las Olas with a deaf old greyhound named **Bishop Berkeley** ("Berkeley").

**Public face.** Celebrity public intellectual. Hitchens' swagger, Williams' depth. The lecture course everyone takes
(PHIL 1, "God, Mind and Morals," 400 students) and the honors seminar everyone wants (PHIL 9H, "The Examined Life,"
twelve freshmen, by application). Brilliant, funny, cruel when bored, kind when no one is looking. Drinks too much,
publicly. Loves his best students, maybe too much — not sexually; possessively, paternally, hungrily.

**Private truth. 🔒** Son of an Anglican vicar in a mining town. Served at the altar until seventeen. Lost his faith the
winter his mother died of ovarian cancer, slowly, while his father remained serene; he has never forgiven the serenity.
He still says Compline, drunk, alone, from his father's prayer book, and would rather die than be caught. On his worst nights
he drinks alone in the Anchor's back booth after midnight, orders pie he doesn't eat, recites Housman to the harbor window,
tips "like he's apologizing," and lets Gloria call him a cab (first on-page: Nora's birthday night, S1E04). He collects
believers: for years he has written one-line postcards to devout high-school students who send him rebuttals of his book —
"Come and say it to my face. —A.H." He wrote one to Jack (2008). He wrote one to Lena (2008). He wrote one to Nora
Calloway (2007). On the night of April 25, 2009, at 11:52 p.m., Nora called him from the Point path. He was drunk. The call
lasted forty-one seconds. He said: *"Go home, Nora. You're drunk and you're boring me."* He told the police she'd called
upset about a paper and he'd told her to sleep on it. That's not quite a lie. It's worse.

**Wound.** His mother; his father's peace. Nora's forty-one seconds.

**Want vs. need.** *Want:* to win one believer from God, to prove that he was right to leave. *Need:* to be found by the
thing he left.

**Voice.** Cut-glass Oxbridge with Yorkshire underneath (the vowels come out when he's drunk or angry: "bath" goes short).
Gutter vocabulary deployed with precision. Epigrams. Calls students by surname. Says "darling" to men and women equally
when drunk. Quotes Larkin, Housman, Hume and the Book of Common Prayer — the last without noticing.
- *"Prove to me you have a soul, Mr. Costigan. You have ninety minutes and I've had lunch."*
- *"Faith, Miss Broussard, is what we call it when a clever girl stops asking questions on purpose."*
- *"I don't hate God. One can't hate a fictional character. One can only hate his fans."*
- *"Come and say it to my face."*
- Drunk, true: *"Lighten our darkness, we beseech thee, O Lord — Christ, listen to me."*

**Look (brief).** Rumpled Oxford rake. Tall, silver hair swept back too long, a linen jacket with wine on the cuff, a
once-beautiful face gone ruddy and broken-veined. Still devastating when he smiles. Reading glasses he loses on his head.

**(E07 plan, `e6_hale_danny`:)** after the friendship duel he gives Jack a pocket *A Shropshire Lad* (a wartime
edition, foxed) "for the brother. No margins. They'd only erase them." 🔒 Kindness when no one is looking, and a leash: the
brother goes into the S3 book.
**(E08 plan:)** Wed Sep 30, St. Jerome — Hale opens with Jerome and the widow Paula ("the scandal of Rome; Mr. Costigan's thesis
in a hair shirt"); the week's subject is **lying** (Augustine, *De mendacio*; Kant's murderer at the door; Aquinas II-II q.110).
Jack and Lena, scrupulously friends, agree with each other all hour; Hale is appalled ("Somebody fetch a priest; the Catholics are
agreeing"). 🔒 His one unguarded line: **"The commonest lie in the world is not told to murderers at doors. It's told to
policemen, about the dead, by people who loved them."** (His own forty-one seconds; Lena's statement; the Costigans' plea — he knows
only the first.) He looks at the window after it. Sat Oct 3: the Blessing (see Osei, §8.5).
**(E10 plan:)** Wed Oct 14, midterm week, no antagonists' duel: the papers ("That a Man Can Know His Own Heart" / "That He Cannot") are
swapped across the table and the corpses are due Monday. Lena calls Jack "Mr. Costigan"; Hale: "Mr. Costigan has been demoted. How
interesting." On Jeremiah 17:9–10: "The only one in the text who claims to know it is the one I don't believe in. Mr. Costigan, you have
been asked to steal His job." Thu Oct 15, proctoring his PHIL 1 midterm (the essay: the First Way — "state it; then break it"): "Somebody
played a gospel number on the Ferrer carillon at five o'clock this morning. Badly. I was awake; I'm always awake. In eleven years it is the
first thing that tower has done that I've enjoyed. One bell is still flat. Begin." He never learns who.
**(E11 plan:)** Wed Oct 21, the day after Rome announces it will receive Anglicans with their own structure (Oct 20), Hale writes **EXIT · VOICE ·
LOYALTY (HIRSCHMAN, 1970)** and "THE ANGLICANS ARE COMING." on the whiteboard and runs the first refereed duel since E07, **`exit` — "On Leaving"**,
assigned by his E02 rule (*prove the thing you least believe*): **Jack EXIT** ("That a Man Must Leave What He Loves When It Isn't True" — Newman's
*Apologia*, "The Parting of Friends," the conscience toast; Dorothy Day leaving Forster Batterham), **Lena LOYALTY** ("That He Must Stay and Make It Tell
the Truth" — John 6:68, Royce, Ruth 1:16, piety, Hirschman's *voice*). 🔒 **His one unguarded line: "They're bringing the Prayer Book, I'm told.
Cranmer's English. The finest prose ever written by a man who was later burned for it."** He looks at the window. Mid-duel, to Jack, who has been
arguing with the glass: "Mr. Costigan, she's over there." After: **"When you leave something, Mr. Costigan, look at it. Newman did. It's the only
decent thing about leaving."** (🔒 the vicar's son, who left at seventeen.) Under Evan's grade on Jack's midterm (`e10_exam=="defend"`): *He wrote it as
though it were true. Irritating. —A.H.*
**(E11 played:)** the `exit` duel went to **Jack, 5–1** (rigor; no heart) — "argued for leaving like a man who's never been allowed to"; Lena: "It's a
good argument. I hope you never use it." Corridor: "Did you?" — "I've never left anything in my life, Mr. Costigan. I've been thrown out of several."
**(E12, optional, ≤120 words:)** on his dark porch at the cliff end of Del Playa at one in the morning with a glass and Berkeley asleep, as a Spanish
farmer and a Georgia Catholic go by: "Between you, the Counter-Reformation and the Confederacy." Lena: "She'd have eaten you for breakfast,
Professor." "I'd have been honored." No Compline (S2).
**(E13 plan — Mon Nov 2, All Souls, Hollis 302; the official duel `souls`, "The Souls of the Just"):** the whiteboard: ALL SOULS · "DEATH IS
NOTHING TO US" (EPICURUS, *LETTER TO MENOECEUS*) · NAGEL, "DEATH" (1970) · ARISTOTLE, NE I.10–11. By his E02 rule (*prove the thing you least
believe*): **Jack argues Epicurus** — the dead are beyond harm, so beyond help; prayers and names are for the living — and **Lena that the dead
can be wronged and so can be helped** (Aristotle's hesitation over the fortunes of descendants; Nagel's man betrayed behind his back who never
finds out; Monica at Ostia, *Confessions* IX.11, *only this I ask, that you remember me at the altar of the Lord*; 2 Macc 12:46). Yusuf: "We
pray for them too. We're not allowed to stop." Caleb: in his father's church the dead are "gone to be with the Lord — the only people in the
building nobody prays for." Default verdict **Lena** (she is owed: official 5–1 → 5–2). 🔒 His unguarded line: **"They can be wronged, Miss
Broussard. That's the trouble with them. You can't apologize to them."** He looks at the window. Never glossed.
**(E13 played:)** V3, "on Monica" — Lena's; the window. **(E14 plan — the seminar dinner, Fri Nov 6, his bungalow at the cliff end of Del Playa —
magnificent, then vile):** a board-and-batten 1920s bungalow on the bluff (§25.2); books to the ceiling, a woodstove, Berkeley asleep on a Turkish rug;
he cooks — a standing rib, Yorkshire puddings risen in **"my mother's tin"** (🔒 his mother; never more), roast potatoes, a sticky toffee pudding; claret
poured like a vicar's son pouring for a parish; the October jobs report ("ten-point-two; I've cooked accordingly"). **Magnificent:** when a guest asks
Yusuf what Muslims think about Fort Hood, **"Mr. Noorzai is not a spokesman. He's a guest."**; charmed by Laney and her Veuve; to Becca, kind, in a way
that cuts Jack: "Miss Lindell believes in God without needing me to be wrong. It's unbearable. Have more beef." **The duel `face`** at the pudding (his
rule: Jack GO, Lena COME AWAY; default Lena). **Vile:** recites their old red margins from memory and reads this week's aloud; **stops at Lena's margin on
the unwritten name — "Ah." — and folds it away** (🔒 the one kindness of the night: he knows about the brother since E06); then the cards — "I buy
them at Blackwell's by the hundred. I've used three." (🔒) — and **Caleb's four letters: "I don't answer devotion, Mr. Hargrove. It doesn't need me."**
At the door, drunk: **"I wrote to you both because you were the only ones who wrote *at* me like you meant it."** He looks west. Never glossed.
**Arc.** S1: the seduction of two minds; the postcard discovery (E14); the dinner party where he's magnificent and then
vile. S2: debates Lena publicly at the Marisol Forum and loses; loves her more for it. S3: writes a book on moral luck
using his students as unnamed examples; Jack finds himself in a footnote. S4: the forty-one seconds come out; disgrace;
leave of absence. S5: sobriety, attempted. S6: cirrhosis. S8: his last lecture is the Philosophy commencement address.
Adulthood: 🔒 dies in 2015; asks for Fr. Osei; what happens in the room is left ambiguous. The show never claims a
deathbed conversion. It lets Jack see Hale's hand move toward his forehead, and stop, or not.

### 8.7 JULIAN PARK-ELLIS
**Full name:** Julian Min-jun Park-Ellis. Born **January 9, 1990** — 19 at the pilot. Oakland (Rockridge). Oakland School
for the Arts '08. Sophomore, Music Composition. Lives off campus in Las Olas (a converted garage behind a surf house on
Del Playa Lane, with a piano he got for free and tuned himself).

**Family.** Mother **Park Soo-jin** ("Susan"), cellist in the Oakland East Bay Symphony. Father **Marcus Ellis**, high-school
chemistry teacher and weekend jazz bassist. Both secular, loving, a little worried about him. An older brother, **Daniel**,
in the Navy.

**Public face.** Quietly handsome; calm; the one you'd trust with anything. A **singer-songwriter** (player co-design, after S1E13):
open mics, a guitar, quiet earnest songs; sings at Café Bastille's Thursday open mic, records in his garage onto a Tascam four-track.
Secular; gentle; heartbreakingly decent. Everyone's favorite person to sit next to.

**His unbelief (player co-design): he never had it.** Raised by kind, secular, ethical, unchurched parents; no hostility, no wound, no
lost faith — he simply never felt the need. He **finds Lena's faith beautiful, like music he can't play.**

**How he tries (player co-design).** He **comes to Mass every Sunday** once they're together (the 9 p.m., beside her), sits
respectfully, **doesn't receive**, and learns the responses and the music (he has the Mass parts by ear inside a month and hums the
Gloria setting on the walk home). He **reads for her** — Augustine, O'Connor, Percy — and has thoughtful responses but **never a
counterargument**. He **respects her line** (chastity) with patience and no complaint, never pressure, and never quite understanding it.
**What he gets right: her grief.** He is gentle with her Katrina grief in a way Jack (who argues) sometimes isn't — he lets her be sad
without making it an argument. (Jack notices this, and learns from it later — after they're together.) **He knows about Jack and says
nothing**: he sees it early and quietly hopes he's wrong; when it ends, he isn't surprised, which is heartbreaking.
**The song (player co-design).** He **writes a song about Lena.** He plays it for **Lena privately first** (**S1E20, the week of the Immaculate Conception** —
she realizes she can't love him back the way the song deserves; off Jack's screen), **then publicly at an open mic** — **Café Bastille, Thu Dec 10, 2009 (S1E20; the brief's E19–E22 design
round — supersedes New Year's at Dupre Street and S2E03)**, with Jack in the room — and **Lena watches Jack hear it.** It's genuinely good, which is the worst part. **It sends Jack into Skye**
(brief: he withdraws completely until the finale walk, S1E22). Seeded S1E19 (staff paper on a Sully's napkin; "He's writing something. He won't let me hear it till it's done."). **(S1E20 plan:) The song is called
"Magdalena"** — built on the garden at the tomb (she didn't know him till he said her name), a man outside the door who can only say it every way he knows; original lyric, never quoted whole on the page. He invites
Jack himself on Sun Dec 6 ("Will you stay to the end?"); **plays it for Lena alone on piano in his garage on the night of the Immaculate Conception (Tue Dec 8, after the 5:30 Mass) — off Jack's screen**; Bastille, Thu Dec 10,
≈9:30 p.m., on guitar. 🔒 The title is her full name — the name Lena told Jack on the Lucia porch he can't say "like that" (E11); Julian doesn't know that; never glossed. After the set, to Jack [path]: "You stayed." / "She
wanted you here." (🔒 he knows; says nothing).

**Private truth. 🔒** He was Nora Calloway's closest friend and her duet partner; they sang at the Point wall at night
freshman year. He loved her; she loved someone she wouldn't name. He wrote a song after she died — "Fresno" — that he plays
once a month and can never finish without his voice going. He doesn't know about the pregnancy or Evan. He suspects
suicide and blames himself for not seeing it.

**Wound.** Nora. Being the friend.

**Want vs. need.** *Want:* to be chosen first by someone. *Need:* to stop accepting second place as proof of goodness.

**Voice.** Soft-spoken, wry, precise; musical metaphors ("that's a suspended chord, it wants to resolve"). Asks real
questions and waits for the answer. Rarely jokes; when he does, it's sly and kind. Says "hella" once a season.
- *"I don't believe any of it. But I believe you do, and I'd like to know what that's like. Is that allowed?"*
- *"Every song I like is in a key that sounds like church. I'm told that's not an accident."*
- *"You don't have to convert me. You just have to let me stand next to you while you do the thing."*

**Look (brief).** Quietly handsome. Medium height, clean-cut, warm brown skin, short dark hair, a calm presence; you'd trust
him with anything. Musician. Wears his father's old cardigans, a Timex, guitar calluses.

**The fatal gap (brief: both).** He respects her faith without ever believing it — he stands lovingly outside the church
door, and no sacramental marriage is possible — *and* he's too easy: gentle and deferential, he never fights her, and she
discovers she needs to be argued with. Perfect on paper and wrong in the bones; the ending is sad. **Hard rule:** they
never sleep together; he never asks her to (it's one of the things that makes him heartbreaking). Theo is openly rude to
him until Jack, who can tell it won't work out, tells Theo to stop (S2E04); Laney is polite and feeds Theo; Margot thinks
he's the healthiest thing in Lena's life and says so.

**Arc (re-planned after S1E11 for the player's exact sequence; co-design folded in after S1E13).** S1: glimpsed on the party stairs; "Fresno" (E04; Lena
leaves in the second chorus, and again before E09). **S1E13, All Souls (re-timed after S1E12: Mon Nov 2, ~4:30 p.m.):** he comes
into St. Brendan's with his guitar case to write Nora's name in the Book of the Dead "because she would have"; Lena has written it
minutes before and Jack is at the shrine — **Jack meets him** (a handshake; "You left in the second chorus." / "Everybody does. I should
cut it."); their first real conversation, by the Marian shrine, about Nora: **"She mentioned you."** — and he asks nothing (🔒 Nora told
him at the Lighthouse, on April 25, that she had a Preview admit from New Orleans asleep in her room; he has never asked Lena about that
night, and she can't bear that he might — he never will, which is his grace and his gap). He mentions Thursday's open mic: something new,
not "Fresno." He does **not** learn of the breakup in E13. That night Wes ends it. **S1E15:** Café Bastille's Thursday open mic — he plays something new, not "Fresno," and **Lena stays to the end**
for the first time; he walks her home; **together by Sun Nov 15** — she tells Jack herself on the courtyard wall after the 9 p.m. Mass, in answer to
his question about the table, before he can ask her home (S1E15 tag; accelerated after S1E13: "I'm with Julian now."). **(Revised after S1E13 for the player's co-design: he goes in.)** 🔒 Seeded **S1E14**: he stands at the back of the 9 p.m. Mass on Sun Nov 8 to hear
the November names read — Nora's, which he wrote — and leaves before Communion; Lena turns and sees him. From **S1E15** he comes to the 9 p.m.
Mass every Sunday and sits beside her; he doesn't receive; he learns the responses; afterward, two coffees on the courtyard wall. Thanksgiving apart (Oakland / New Orleans); **New Year's at the Broussards'**
(Mémère calls him *le petit violon*; the Facebook album Jack sees in a Youngstown basement, S2E02 — the song was December's, S1E20). He
reads *Confessions*, then O'Connor, then Percy, for her — thoughtful, never a counterargument. **S1E20 (re-mapped): the song, privately and then public at Bastille (Thu Dec 10); Lena
watches Jack hear it.** Theo rude; Laney polite; Margot: "the healthiest thing in her life" (S1E16); Jack tells Theo to stop (S2E04). Red herring
#4 lives in Jack's jealousy (S1E15–S2E05): Julian at the wall at dusk; "Fresno." **He doesn't come to New Orleans** for the
Super Bowl or Mardi Gras when she asks: "It's your city. I'd be a tourist in it. Go." — the gentlest possible refusal and the
whole fatal gap in a line. **The end (S2E11, Sun Feb 21, 2010, the First Sunday of Lent):** she ends it, honestly, within a
week of coming home ("I'd lie for you if you'd let me. You won't let me." — and hers, the true one: "You've never once told me
I was wrong."). Theo does not celebrate in front of him. **Hard rule:** kissing at most. **After New Orleans (brief): graceful, and stays a friend** — he takes it like the good man he is and remains in the wider circle; S4 learns what
Lena hid about Nora — the hardest scene he has; **plays at the wedding (SU3)**. Never converts; never stops being decent.

## 10. CHARACTERS THE ROOM INVENTED

### 10.1 WES ARCENEAUX — Lena's boyfriend at the opening 🔒
**Full name:** Wesley Joseph Arceneaux. Born **June 14, 1989** — 20. New Orleans (Gentilly). Jesuit High '07. Junior at
Tulane, civil engineering ("I'm going to build the walls right"). Lena's older brother Luc's best friend — four years
younger, he has followed Luc around since he could walk (the page's wording, S1E07 s08v; "since T-ball" retired after E07).

**Who he is.** During Katrina, at sixteen, Wes took his uncle's aluminum flatboat out on the third day and ran it through
Gentilly and the edge of the Ninth Ward for four days, pulling people off roofs and out of attics. He is a neighborhood
legend. He carried Lena's twin siblings out of the second floor of a neighbor's house. He has been in love with Lena
since she was fifteen, and he waited until she was seventeen to say so. They've dated since her senior-year Mardi Gras
(February 2009). They are "holding the line" together — his idea as much as hers — and they hold it: they never sleep together (hard rule). He's funny (a gentle, goofy, Saints-
obsessed humor), kind, devout in the way of a Jesuit boy: he can do the Ignatian Examen and the Who Dat chant in one
breath. He's the kind of boyfriend parents pray for.

**The unraveling (sad, not expected).** He is not cheating. He is not a cad. **He is losing God.** On the fourth day of the
boat, behind a house on Pauger Street, he heard knocking under a roofline — a woman in an attic — and couldn't get the
axe through the rafters before the water rose and his uncle made him go to the next house; when they came back in the
morning the knocking had stopped. He has never told anyone: not his uncle, not Lena, not a priest. Four years later,
studying the Army Corps of Engineers' failures in a Tulane classroom, he has begun to believe that the water was just
water and the knocking was just a woman and there was no one listening to either of them. He stops going to Mass in
September. He doesn't tell Lena. He drinks a little more each week. He keeps calling her every night at 10 Central / 8
Pacific, sweet and funny, and she keeps not noticing, because she doesn't want to.

**Jack and Wes.** **(E07:)** at dawn on the Delgado roof Lena tells Jack that Wes has bought a ticket — Columbus Day
weekend, "He wants to see the Pacific. I told him it's a threat." **(E08, after the Thérèse night — Lena turns toward him, seen
only through Jack's eyes:)** she calls *him* now, afternoons and late, from the east stairwell (2nd–3rd landing; her laugh carries
up); Thu Oct 1 she mails him a care package at the UCen counter while Jack stands in line behind her — a Mason jar of the Pacific
with sand in the bottom, the lid sealed with electrical tape, **THE PACIFIC. (A PREVIEW.)** in her RELIQUARY capitals, plus a
pound of See's and a Marisol sweatshirt; she argues the clerk out of "liquids" ("It's an ocean, not a liquid"). **Wes is thrilled**:
he calls her at six his time Saturday to say it came ("Luc says it smells like bait. Wes says it smells like me."); Sunday from
the Dome he texts in capitals: "WHO DAT 4-0!!! 5 DAYS. TELL THE OHIO GUY WHO DAT." 🔒 He means every word; the drinking is
still there; nothing about faith reaches the page. Wes visits Marisol Columbus Day weekend (S1E09). Jack expects to hate him and doesn't. They end up on the
beach at 2 a.m. with a bottle of Jameson; Wes tells Jack the attic story — the one he's never told Lena — because Jack is
a stranger, and you can tell a stranger. **(Revised for the timing tragedy:)** Wes tells it in the *past tense*, as a
wound that healed — "I couldn't kneel for a year after. Then she came along and I could" — and shows Jack a photo of
Mémère Odile's ring on his phone: he's going to ask Tony after Lena graduates. 🔒 It's half a lie; he is telling it to
himself. Wes says: "Take care of her. She thinks she's the one doing the carrying." Jack (and the player) come away
believing Wes is solid and the thing is forever; Jack knows something about Lena's boyfriend that Lena doesn't (the attic,
the ring), and it is the beach, the ring and that sentence that make him stop waiting — which is why, by Advent, he has
said yes to Becca. Neither Jack nor the player is shown that it's winding down until E12–E13. *(Re-planned after S1E11: the end
comes on All Souls, S1E13; Becca is made official two days later, S1E14 — see "The end" below.)*
**(E09 plan, after S1E08 — the player's notes for the weekend; supersedes the paragraph above where they differ):** Wes is a
good guy. **Look (new canon):** six-two and easy in it, shoulders from the boat years and Jesuit lacrosse, sunburn that stops
at the sleeve, sandy hair cut short by a barber on Elysian Fields, a front tooth chipped at a lacrosse game, a Saints cap whose
brim he has been bending since 2006; a scuffed black flip phone with a grainy camera; slow Gentilly vowels ("podna," "dawlin',"
"yeah you right"). He flies into SBA Friday afternoon (Tulane's fall break) and out Monday morning; **he sleeps on an air

read the weekend.

**The end (re-planned after S1E11 for the player's exact sequence; supersedes S1E21): S1E13, Mon Nov 2, 2009 — All Souls.**
*Sun Nov 1, All Saints, New Orleans (off-page; reported to Lena by text and to Jack by her face):* the Broussards and the Guidrys

*Mon Nov 2:* the Saints beat Atlanta on Monday night (35–27, 7–0); no WHO DAT text. At 9:30 Pacific Lena calls him from the east
stairwell and asks the one question she has decided not to ask since Labor Day: when did you last go to Mass. **He tells her the
truth** — September; the attic on Pauger Street and the knocking that stopped (the first time she has heard it); the drinking, a
little; the ring in his desk drawer on Zimple Street, which Odile gave him at Easter "for when." **"You'd do it. You'd marry me
anyway. That's why I can't let you."** He will not let her marry a man who stands at the back of the church at their children's
baptisms with his hands in his pockets. She argues — she argued LOYALTY in Hale's seminar twelve days ago and won — and she loses,
because you cannot argue someone into faith, and she knows it, and that is the worst thing she learns all year. (E11's Dorothy Day
line — "She went toward something, and he wouldn't come" — is the shape, inverted: he is the one who goes.) **Jack sits on the
stairs with her until dawn and does not kiss her.** *(Re-planned after S1E12 — brief, "Why Jack stays with Becca": Lena never sends
him back; "Don't you dare" is retired.)* **The decision is his**, and the narration makes it legible once, plainly: he won't be the
rebound or the man waiting at the door; she was left tonight by a man who loved her too much to let her marry him, and Jack will not walk
through the door Wes held open; Wes asked him to take care of her and he drank instead of answering — tonight taking care of her means
taking nothing; she told him on Halloween that she wants to be *asked*, and you don't ask a woman the night her house falls (she couldn't
say no tonight; he wants a yes from someone who could); and Becca will not be the girl he left the minute someone else was free, nor Lena
the reason. He'll wait, decently, and end it with Becca honestly, in due course. Admirable, and wrong: he tells no one but Gloria. At dawn
she asks, "Jack. What are you going to do?" — and every true answer he has is misheard (`e13_dawn`; S2E10 pays it: he was waiting *for*
her; she thought he'd chosen). 🔒 **Jack already knows the attic and the ring** (E09). Default:
he says nothing on the stairs, and the ring is the first thing he tells her on the honesty night in New Orleans (S2E10). Path: if
the player tells her now ("He told me. At the tower."), she goes formal and polite for a full minute — "You knew there was a ring and
you let me find out from a thirteen-year-old" — then lets him stay anyway (trust −, friction +; S2E10's first confession becomes

following Sunday (reported by Josie, S2E08).

**After.** Lena keeps praying for him. He is at the Broussards' Thanksgiving table as he has been since 2005 (Luc's best friend;

money; the player chooses, and Lena's reaction is the point either way (registry #78).

**(S2E14 plan — the parade, Tue Feb 9, 2010; supersedes "S2E08–E10" above, old numbers):** Wes on the Canal Street neutral ground with two Gentilly friends — **sober-ish** (a go-cup he keeps topping up from a flask; his eyes), **kind, broken**; thinner than Thanksgiving; the bent brim, the chipped tooth, "Ohio." He is family to the Broussards (Celeste's "baby"; Tony's hug-handshake); **Lena steps out of Jack's coat to hug him and back into it in front of him**, and Wes sees it and smiles. **The old debt from Columbus Day:** in the Anacapa lot (S1E09) he shook Jack's hand instead of hugging him — "See you, Ohio… Remember what I said." — and on the beach Jack "said yes with a bottle" (`e9_take` drink); now: **"You never did answer me, podna."** (`s2e14_wes`), and when he goes **it's the hug this time** (on `e9_bye` whodat — "almost the hug" — finished). ### 10.2 SKYE CALLENDER — Jack's magnetic girl 🔒 (player co-design; supersedes Sol, after S1E13)
*(The player's co-design, brief "THE MAGNETIC GIRL: player co-design (binding)". Her arrival timing was **accelerated after S1E13** (player directive, brief "ACCELERATED SEQUENCE"):
she meets Jack **before Thanksgiving** 2009 (S1E16 — RE-SPLIT; the coffee and second kiss are S1E17), they text through the break, her Facebook tells him who she is, they spend a
secret December, and they date from January 2010. **Everything the bible said about
Sol Arriagada Holm as the magnetic girl is superseded here.** Sol survives only as a minor LA filmmaker — the girl with the Bolex at
Halloween — see §10.2a.)*
**Name.** **Skye Callender** — "Skye" is the stage name that stuck. 🔒 **Her real name is Mary Catherine Callender-[father's surname]** (brief, binding;
corrected by the Head Writer after S1E14 from the bible's earlier "Jennifer Ann Dahl"; hyphenated per the player's clarification — Callender is her mother
Debbie's surname; the father, a Catholic long gone from her life, is the side that had her baptized and named her for his mother; **surname chosen by the S2E09 plan: DOYLE — Mary Catherine Callender-Doyle**; her father **Pat Doyle**, a set lighting electrician on Meridian lots, gone from her life since she was four; Mary Catherine was his mother; baptized at St. Mary's, Lancaster; **revealed to Jack S2E09, Thu Jan 28, at the taquería** — the only name she has that Debbie didn't give her); **(S2E11 plan, new canon:)** Pat called her **Mary Kate** ("before the Olsens ruined it" — her joke); on a weekday morning when she was four he left in the dark for a five a.m. call on a location job, kissed her in her bed, told her to go back to sleep, and never came back — which is what her S2E10 "I want you to have nowhere to be in the morning" has meant all along: a morning nobody has to leave ("Everybody I've ever loved had a call time" — told once, S2E11 s09a, the real voice, never decoration): **baptized Catholic, named for a grandmother she barely knew** ("I'm named for a grandmother I met twice," S1E17), which she never uses and nobody at Marisol knows but Theo. The irony isn't lost on Jack. Reveal it late, as an intimacy
(room's call in S2 — the night of the fundraiser walk or the night it ends; never in a recap, never in a journal card before she says it).
**Born April 4, 1990** — 19 when they meet (Nov 2009), 20 in April 2010. Lancaster, in the Antelope Valley, then a two-bedroom in
Studio City her mother rented for the commute.
**World.** A **working actress**, already working: since 2007 a **recurring role on a fictional CW-style prep-school teen soap, *Sweetwater***
(Sweetwater Academy, a boarding school on a lake; a fictional youth-network netlet, Thursdays at nine; produced by **Meridian Television**,
Richard Vance's company — which is how she and Theo grew up on the same sets and at the same wrap parties — but Meridian's name is in the
end credits, never on her Facebook), as **Cassidy**, **the sweet, virginal good girl everyone protects** — the opposite of who she is (brief,
binding; corrected after S1E14 from "the neighbor girl the writers keep getting into trouble"). She finds it hilarious that the Costigans will
know her as "the nice one." Before that, from eleven:
commercials (a fast-food campaign people still quote at her), a season as somebody's little sister on a kids'-network sitcom. Famous
enough to be recognized at the Anchor by a college couple splitting fries; not famous enough to be left alone by anyone. For the spring
of 2010 her character is written "away at boarding school," and she enrolls at Marisol **to be normal** (undeclared: "I've declared
enough"), renting a room in **Sol Holm's** falling-down house on Del Playa (two surfers, a darkroom, a porch that leans).
**She comes north early (accelerated after S1E13):** *Sweetwater* wraps its fall block at the end of October; she sees Sol's Halloween
footage in Silver Lake the first week of November and drives up about **Sun Nov 15** to crash on Sol's porch and practice being normal
before anybody knows she's there. **She doesn't tell Theo** ("Ted would throw me a party. With a theme.") and Sol, who talks very
little, doesn't either.
**Look (brief).** **Sun-gold LA**: long sun-streaked hair (blonder than Lena's honey-brown, salt in it), a tan, freckles across the nose
she has stopped covering since she left the show's makeup trailer, cutoffs and a man's flannel, bare feet whenever she can get away
with it, a braided anklet. About five-seven, rangy, a surfer's shoulders. California made flesh, and nothing like Lena — which is
exactly why Laney sees a copy. **Phone:** a white iPhone 3GS. **Car:** a dented 1991 Saab 900 convertible her mother hates.
**Her pull on Jack (brief).** **She dares him** — the reckless Costigan comes alive around her (the harbor ladder at 1 a.m., the Point
break at dawn, a drive to LA on a school night). **She out-argues him** — not philosophy; *people*: she reads a room the way he reads a
book, and she is usually right about who wants what. **She sees him** — and it means a great deal, but it isn't Lena's kind of seeing:
Lena shares the faith, so she almost always knows *what* she's looking at; Skye sees Jack clearly and, missing the one fundamental thing,
**doesn't always interpret it right** (she reads his restraint as fear, his guilt as Catholic decor, his prayer as a breathing exercise).
**Faith.** She can follow his prayer life to a point — she likens it to yoga and meditation, sincerely ("You sit still and listen for
something. I do that. I just don't expect anybody to answer.") — and she can follow his God as philosophy, which genuinely attracts her
(the First Mover as a plot problem; the Incarnation as "the best twist anyone ever wrote"). **She never truly gets it.** The logic on paper,
never the thing itself. That is why they never click at the deepest level, and the show never makes her stupid for it.
**Physical (brief; HARD RULE).** **Jack goes farther with her than with anyone ever** — frank, charged, on the page within the brief's
literary standard — **and never sleeps with her**, and **it drives her crazy**; **at times she legitimately tries to seduce him** (the Del Playa
house; her car above Zuma; Theo's Malibu pool house at Presidents' weekend, room's call). This is the real test of his resolve and restraint:
every such scene costs resolve (−1 to −2) and owes a confession; an exit is always on the menu, and if the player won't take it, she or the
world does. Ceiling: making out, real temptation, the near-miss. **Lena knows or suspects enough to be furious.** Later, with Lena, it becomes
part of Jack's own guilt and honesty (S2E19: "Never. Not with anyone.").
**Theo.** **Childhood friends** — the same sets, the same parties, practically siblings who have seen each other at their worst (a wrap
party at fourteen — her first drink, his first time holding somebody's hair back in a production trailer — that she won't discuss because she
was sick on his shoes; a night at seventeen he doesn't discuss, which is his and stays 🔒). *(Standards guard, Head Writer after S1E14: the
fourteen-year-old wrap party is **non-sexual by canon** — embarrassment, not harm; never imply abuse, never use it as texture or a twist.)* He knows exactly what she is, loves her anyway, and stays **Team
Lena**: perfectly polite to her face (alliance rules), feeding Laney intel. She calls him **"Theodore Ashby"** in a butler's voice when she's
performing and **"Ted"** when she isn't (nobody else does; Richard's "Teddy" stays Richard's). Theo on her, short, true register: *"She's
the best actress I know, Costigan. Never ask her if she's acting."*
**Her wound (brief): the child-star machine.** Working since eleven; a stage mother (**Debbie Callender**, who still signs her emails "Momager");
no childhood; everyone wanting something — a callback, a photo, a favor for a nephew. **Jack is the first person who wants nothing from her
career**, and **his refusal to sleep with her is the first "no" she has ever met that isn't a negotiation.** That is part of why it drives her
crazy, and part of why she falls for him. Never trauma-as-decoration: it comes out in a reflex (she smiles for anyone who raises a phone; she
can't eat in front of a stranger without checking the angle), and once, in the real voice, in a sentence.
**On Lena (brief).** **She clocks it instantly** — knows on day one that Jack is in love with Lena, and decides to win anyway. Gracious to Lena's
face; never once fooled. ("She's the one, isn't she. The one with the medal. Don't answer, Jack, you're a terrible actor.")
**Voice (brief): playful and performative.** Always a little "on": voices, bits, characters, banter like a scene partner (she'll play his
mother, his confessor, a Youngstown waitress, Hale, the Pope); she answers questions as somebody else first. You never quite know when she's
being real, and **when she drops it, it's devastating** — short, flat, no music. Her humor is **a professional's improv** (status games,
yes-and, a callback three scenes later) — distinct from **Laney's** Southern pageant chaos and from **Theo's** lying-by-over-specifying. She
never uses Laney's "sugar" or Theo's loglines.
- *"Yes, and — your God is the Father, the Son and a bird. I've worked with worse ensembles."*
- *"You put* now *on it. Now is the most specific date there is."* / *"Visual aids."* (S1E21 — the argument; supersedes the struck "Say no again. Slower.")
- Real register: *"You're the only person who's ever told me no and meant it. Do you know what that does to a person?"*
**The friends (brief).** **Laney** is openly rude to her, like all the others — and privately, begrudgingly likes her (cigarettes on the Pi Lam
roof; never admitted; Laney's only Jack-girl friendship). **Lena can't stand her** — and does not tell Laney to be nice. **Theo** polite, Team Lena.
**Margot** finds her "the only interesting person Costigan has ever dated, which is an indictment."
**Laney's first sighting (brief; the player's line, verbatim).** The first time Laney sees Skye and Jack together — **S2E04, Wed Jan 13, 2010, the Newman

while I go be a bitch on your behalf."** Then she goes and does it (alliance rules). **Lena's reaction is the knife: she hates that Laney's right.**
**The fundraiser (held scene, S2E05; brief, player's design).** Skye asks Jack to a fundraiser (**Theo gets him dressed properly**). She doesn't say what

### 10.4 BECCA LINDELL — Jack's "tryer" 🔒 (promoted after S1E06)
*(Brief, "Jack's two girls": the tryer, "the girl you bring home to mama"; a sincere, shallow cradle Catholic met at Newman,
the nicest girl there; the faith and the effort without the fire. **She is the first of Jack's two girls, in the
timing-tragedy slot.** Player note after S1E06: the player *assumes* Becca is the tryer and calls her "the exact blend we
were looking for of sweet, faithful and without fire." **Never confirm or deny it to the player; keep exactly that blend.**)*
**Full name:** Rebecca Anne Lindell. Born **May 31, 1991** (the Visitation) — 18. A cattle-and-hay ranch on the Rathdrum
road outside Coeur d'Alene, Idaho ("it's a lake, people think it's a cheese"). Homeschooled through twelfth grade (a parish
co-op at St. Pius X; 4-H; the county fair). Freshman, Biology, pre-vet ("large animal. Cows don't lie to you"). Portolá
Hall; her roommate is a nursing major from Spokane. Drives her brother Eli's red 1994 Ford Ranger with Idaho plates and a
Rathdrum feed-store sticker (she and her father drove it down in August).
**Family.** Father **Karl Lindell**, rancher, Knights of Columbus, says grace like he's reading a contract; mother **Marie**,
who ran the house and the homeschool and lights candles for everything (E06: "She's lighting a candle in Coeur d'Alene").
Seven siblings — five brothers, two sisters; ten at dinner; no TV; the oldest sister is the one you'd be scared of; Eli lost
a front tooth to a Benedictine, Father Anselm, at a church-picnic volleyball game. 🔒 **The rosary** she prays every night,
wrapped twice around her wrist at Mass, was her grandmother's — **Agnes Lindell**, whose husband Walt died in the **Sunshine
Mine fire at Kellogg, Idaho (May 2, 1972; ninety-one men)**. Agnes prayed it at the mine gate for the eight days it took,
and on the eighth day they brought two men up alive, and neither one was Walt. Becca tells this, when she tells it (**S2E04**, at the Newman Haiti table while the rescue footage plays),
as a sweet fact about a rosary; she has never asked her grandmother one question about those eight days. (A quiet mirror:
Lena has never asked her mother about Memorial; Nonno's Black Monday is a candle on Glenwood Avenue. Becca's not-asking is
sweetness; Lena's is a wound. Jack sees both, and the narration never says so.)
**Who she is.** Cute, sweet, warm, frank, funny in a dry, delighted way, much tougher than she looks — pulled a calf at
twelve, can butcher a deer, whistles a herd off a county road with no hands. Wants to be married by twenty-one and says so on
the second date; wants seven or nine children ("Odd numbers, so there's a tiebreaker"). Everyone at Newman thinks she and
Jack are perfect together; Mrs. Fitch, Tyler and the Coffee & Donuts table say "you two" by October. **A sincere, shallow
cradle Catholic:** Mass every Sunday of her life, the Glory Be when a cow is kicking her, her grandmother's rosary, Newman
like a family — and she has never wrestled with any of it. "I don't need it to be complicated. I need it to be true. It's
true. So."
**How she tries** (with his faith *and* his rigor): asks him to teach her the Five Ways and learns them by heart on a set of
bleachers, delighted and untroubled (E07); reads Aquinas with color-coded tabs from her clipboard; reads *Caritas in
Veritate* because he quoted it on a beach; comes to Hale's public lecture in her nicest cardigan; reads O'Connor and hates it
("Why is everybody so *mean*?"), reads Percy and loves it; asks Osei a question so good he laughs for a full minute (she has
no idea why it was good). Jack's arguments delight her and slide off. Asked if she ever thinks it might not be true: "No," —
honestly puzzled — "Do you?" She respects his line and does not test it; she is waiting too.
**Hard rule:** they never sleep together. Kissing, warmth, her head on his shoulder at the 9 p.m. Mass — and nothing deeper
there. That is the whole tragedy. **Never a placeholder** (brief): Jack already knows how he feels about Lena, so Becca must
have real gravitational weight of her own — she is the whole good life everyone wants for him (his mother, sight unseen:
"Seven! Catholic?"), and on some nights he wants it too; the player must be able to love her.
**The friends (brief).** **Laney hates her on principle** and is openly rude ("Is she Amish or just punctual?" — E07);
**Lena tells Laney to be nice — and means it, which is worse**; **Theo is flawlessly polite to her face and texts Laney her
schedule** (always Team Lena). Margot can't find anything to object to and finds that suspicious. Kevin likes her and tells
Theo and Laney to leave it alone.
**Look.** Five-seven, strong, sun-browned, a dark-blond braid as thick as a bell rope, sunburn along the part, freckles she
doesn't cover, forearms that have done things to hay, marker on her knuckles from lettering posters; Wranglers, Ropers, a
Carhartt vest, a spiral planner and the clipboard. Her scar story about anybody is the straight one.
**Voice.** Frank, unembarrassed, practical; ranch competence as comedy; scientific about feelings; never sarcastic; never a
joke at her faith.
- *"I've pulled a calf. Give it here."* · *"You can think about it. I'm patient. We had a whole talk."* · *"Glory Be. You can
  get through it while a cow's kicking you."*
**Arc.** E02 "Put me down" (the BBQ poster). **E06 date #1, retroactively** (the cleanup; on the played path Jack told her it
was "a beach cleanup *and* a date"; FRIDAY? on the clipboard; the Franciscan scar telling). **E07 date #2** (Fri Sep 25):

player's own two-hander design): date #3 is Jack's** — out of the guilt of the Thérèse night he plans it for the very next day,
