### 10.5 PRIYA RAMAN — the junior RA
**Born October 14, 1988.** Fremont, California. Junior, Biochemistry. Delgado Hall 4th-floor RA (Room 401). Three jobs
(RA, library circulation, organic chem tutor). Overwhelmed; laminated everything; "per my email"; color-coded door tags;
an air horn for emergencies. Parents run a motel in Fremont and believe she's pre-med. 🔒 She's quietly failing organic
chemistry and has changed her major on paper without telling them.

🔒 **Nora connection:** Priya was Nora Calloway's freshman roommate (Delgado 2007–08, Room 222) and her best friend that
year. They drifted sophomore year (Nora moved to Serra Hall with Sloane Kittredge, got secretive). Priya has a box of Nora's
things in the RA storage closet — the Calloways never collected it — including Nora's journal, which Priya has never been
able to open past the first page. Her rule "Nobody goes to the Point after dark" is personal. On Nora's birthday she buys two mylar balloons at the Safeway
(two for one), ties one to the cross before her 8 a.m. orgo lab, in daylight, and keeps the other in the 4th-floor lounge
with a grocery cupcake. Facebook keeps suggesting Nora to her residents (no memorial status exists until late Oct 2009); she
has reported it three times. She knows the Memorare by heart because Nora prayed it in the shower every morning (Priya is
Hindu).

**Voice.** Rapid, bureaucratic, accidentally hilarious, passive-aggressive in Comic Sans. "Per the Residential Life
Handbook." "I'm going to need you to not." When she breaks, she breaks completely, then re-laminates.
- *"Rule one: nobody goes to the Point after dark. That's not a Res Life rule. That's my rule. I will know."*

**Arc.** S1: comic relief who becomes a source (she tells Jack Nora's name, E04; shows him the box, E11). S2: opens the
journal. Later seasons: switches to public health, tells her parents (Diwali episode, S5).
**(E10 plan — the box moves up from E11:)** Tuesday's storm floods the **RA storage closet in the Delgado basement** (beside the laundry; RA
STORAGE — NOT A STUDY ROOM). At 1:40 a.m. Wednesday, studying for her 8 a.m. orgo midterm in the warm laundry room, Priya unlocks it and Jack
helps save the boxes: **CALLOWAY · 222 · HOLD FOR FAMILY**, HOLD underlined twice, the bottom corner soaked. Inside: a Selma High sweatshirt,
CDs, a mug, a photo of two girls laughing in a dorm window (one is Priya), and a black-and-white composition book — **Nora's journal**. She
opens the cover only: *Nora Calloway · Delgado 222 · If found, please return. Reward: I'll sing you something.* She has never gotten past it.
She breaks ("I *tutor* organic chemistry. I'm *failing* organic chemistry.") and re-laminates (BASEMENT FLOODED · DRYERS 1–3 ONLY). **The box
lives in 401 from now on.** Wednesday night she works the Brick's overnight circulation desk; near dawn she "didn't see" Jack and Lena ("The
scanner's been broken since two"). Saturday is Diwali: a battery diya on top of the box (HAPPY DIWALI · ELECTRIC DIYAS ONLY · FIRE CODE). 🔒
Nothing in the box points at Hale, Evan, the jacket or Lena; the April 23 entry waits for S2.

### 10.6 RAFI OCHOA — the floor dealer
**Rafael Ignacio Ochoa.** Born **June 2, 1991**. Marisol townie (the Westside, near the harbor). Freshman, Environmental
Studies, on a Cal Grant and a surf-team spot. Delgado 204 (his roommate never showed; "the ghost of 204"). Discreet weed and
Adderall dealer: a tackle box of "vitamins," delivery by skateboard, calls everyone "boss," quotes his abuela and Marcus
Aurelius (his abuela gave him the *Meditations*). Mellow, polite, scrupulously honest about prices. 🔒 **His father is
Detective Sergeant Ray Ochoa of the Marisol Police Department**, who investigated and closed Nora Calloway's death as an
accident. 🔒 Rafi, then a high-school senior, sold Nora two Xanax bars at the Lighthouse party on April 25, 2009. He hasn't
sold bars since; he says, on Jack's first night, "Not bars, though. I don't do bars anymore." He doesn't know whether the
pills mattered. He's terrified that they did.
**(E06 plan, played path:)** Jack (living route in the pilot) never heard "Not bars" or saw the tackle box; E06 re-plants
both after his father's stop on Ocean Road: *"Weed. Adderall around midterms. Not bars, though. I don't do bars anymore."*
(🔒 Nora's two bars; no gloss.) Rafi skates; La Flaca was "reported abandoned at the harbor in 2007" (Ray's line, true).

**Voice.** Surfer-mellow, courtly, philosophical. "Boss." "No stress." "My abuela says the devil's patient, so be faster."
**Arc.** S1: supply and comedy; offers Jack money-for-errands during the money crisis (E15). S2: his father's case file
becomes a target. S4: his part comes out; his father's reaction is the best scene Ray Ochoa ever gets.

### 10.7 EVAN MARSH — the TA with secrets 🔒
**Born February 11, 1980.** Duluth, Minnesota. PhD candidate in Philosophy (dissertation on Kierkegaard and moral
injury, Hale advising, year seven, stalled). TA for PHIL 1's Thursday 4 p.m. section (Hollis 108) — Jack and Lena's
section. Lapsed Lutheran. Dry, exhausted, precise, kind to struggling students, savage to lazy ones.

**The secret.** He was Nora Calloway's boyfriend from October 2008 to her death. She was in his section; they told no one
(it would have cost him his funding and her her reputation). She was eight weeks pregnant. On April 25 they fought by
text; at 12:05 a.m. she texted him from the Point: *"I'm at the Point. Please come. I'm keeping it. I want to keep it. I
want you to want it."* He read it at 12:20 and drove. At 12:31 his headlights caught a tall blond kid running from the
Point path toward Seacliff Road clutching something dark. He went to the wall, saw nothing, called her phone, heard
nothing, assumed she'd left to punish him, and drove home furious. At dawn surfers found her. He told police he'd been
asleep and seen her text in the morning; he deleted it. He has spent four months hunting for a tall blond boy.

**What he does.** He is not a villain; he is a coward that night who is now trying to be brave in the wrong way. He sees
Theo at the Halloween chaos (S1E12) and goes cold. He begins asking careful questions (S1E19: "Your roommate — was he at
Preview Weekend last April?"). In S2 he becomes dangerous — to Theo, and to himself.

**Look.** Lanky, prematurely gray at the temples, wire glasses, a stained Carhartt jacket, a bike he rides everywhere
because he sold his car in the summer (🔒 he couldn't drive past the Point). Smokes American Spirits.
**Voice.** Minnesota-flat, dry, exact; Kierkegaard quotes; long silences. *"Purity of heart is to will one thing. I've
never managed two."*

**Arc.** S1: the man at the end of the Lighthouse driveway (pilot); the section; the questions. S2: the anniversary
confrontation. S3: dates Margot; she finds the text history he never deleted from his laptop. S4: tells the truth to the
police and to the Calloways — the pregnancy, the text, the blond boy. Clears Nora of the suicide whisper. Loses his PhD.
Later: teaches philosophy at a prison education program in Minnesota; writes Jack once a year.
**(E11 plan, 🔒:)** Thu Oct 22, section: he returns the PHIL 1 midterms (Jack's: "A–. Defended, not broken. —E.M."), then reads Kierkegaard aloud —
*Works of Love*, "The Work of Love in Recollecting One Who Is Dead" (the dead can't repay you; it is the freest love) — and his voice goes on the second
paragraph; he lets section out at 4:31 without a word. Monday Oct 26 is six months. Lena is very still. Nobody on the page knows why.
**(E12 plan, 🔒:)** Sat Oct 31, ~11:55 p.m., walking his bike through the Las Olas crowd on Del Playa in the stained Carhartt, no costume — **he stops
dead under the Ferrante house's floodlights, looks at Theo** (tall, blond, a white dinner jacket, laughing on the porch) **and goes white**: the first
time he has seen the boy from the Point lot in the light. To Jack, passing: "Mr. Costigan." — not looking at him — "**Who is that?**" Jack's answer
(`e12_evan`: "My roommate. Theo. It's his party." / "Jay Gatsby. It's his party." / "Why?") is **the on-page route for E19's question** ("Your roommate
— was he at Preview Weekend last April?"); on `roommate` he has the name too. He rides off west toward Seacliff (🔒 never followed).
**(E12 played: `e12_evan=="gatsby"`)** — he has the costume and the house, **not the name**. E19 routes it: "The man in the white jacket. Halloween.
You know him." → Jack's answer gives "roommate" → "Was he at Preview Weekend last April?" Not on the page in E13.

### 10.8 JACK'S FAMILY — the Costigans of Youngstown
Home: a narrow two-story frame house on **Glenwood Avenue near Brownlee Woods**, South Side, with a detached garage where
Frank keeps a space heater, a radio and a Stroh's fridge. Parish: **St. Brigid of Kildare** (fictional), South Side. Pastor:
**Fr. Dom Bruno** (named E06 plan; sixties, skipped the homily on Ephesians 5 the Sunday before Jack left — Aug 23, 2009).

- **Francis "Frank" Costigan, 51.** GM Lordstown assembly, 26 years, UAW Local 1112. Laid off since the GM bankruptcy
  (June 1, 2009); unemployment and the last of the SUB pay are running out by October. Drives a **1999 Chevy Silverado**
  (forest green, rust over the rear wheel wells, 212,000 miles). Sings Sinatra in the garage. Kennedy Democrat, pro-life,
  union to the marrow. Funny in a gruff, minimal way. Loves his kids ferociously and can't say it. 🔒 **Frank knows Jack
  threw the punch.** He brokered the plea: he went to Danny in the county jail and Danny said "Jackie's got the
  scholarship, Dad," and Frank let him. He has chosen one son's future over the other son's freedom, and he has to look at
  both of them. He drove Jack 2,400 miles because he couldn't afford two plane tickets and because he wanted to see the
  Pacific once before he died. He sleeps in the truck on the way home to save the motel money.
  - *"Close your mouth. You'll catch flies."* · *"Don't waste it."* · *"We don't. Not here. That's done."*
- **Maria Teresa (Rinaldi) Costigan, 49.** Secretary at St. Brigid's school. Devout, fierce, funny, tired. Visits Danny at
  Trumbull Correctional every other Sunday after the 8 a.m. Mass. 🔒 **Does not know** the truth. Believes Danny's version
  (a fight that went wrong). Her grief over Danny is the family's weather.
  - *"Did you eat? Don't lie to me, I can hear it in your voice when you haven't eaten."*
- **Daniel Francis "Danny" Costigan, 22** (b. Feb 2, 1987). 🔒 Serving five years at **Trumbull Correctional Institution**
  (Leavittsburg, Ohio) for felonious assault, pleaded January 2008. Eligible for judicial release consideration in 2011;
  release date 2012. He took the fall for Jack. He is funny, profane, gentle, does push-ups and reads every book Jack sends
  him (Jack sends one a month, used, with his own margin notes erased because the prison won't allow writing — Jack writes
  new notes on a separate sheet). In his letters he calls Jack "Professor." He does not resent Jack. That's the worst
  part for Jack.
  **(E06 plan:) Danny's first letter on the page** (lined paper, block capitals for the address, TRUMBULL CORRECTIONAL
  INSTITUTION and his inmate number on the envelope — Researcher to confirm the return-address format), written **Wed Sep
  16 night after he called the house and Gina said "fine,"** mailed Thursday, in Jack's Delgado box **Saturday**. It crosses
  the Thursday call: *"Tell Gina it ain't hers to carry. I got it."* (🔒 he is carrying Jack's; dramatic irony, never
  glossed) — which is what the system cut off ("tell Gina — "). Also: *"Tell the veil girl thanks for asking my name.
  Nobody out there asks it anymore. They ask Ma how I'm doing like I'm the weather."* Reggie from Portsmouth; the Hopkins
  ("Ma says it's poems. Send it anyway"). Signed **—D.** Danny's written voice: run-on, profane in a clean way, funny,
  generous; no self-pity; one sentence that stops Jack cold per letter.
  **(E08 plan:) Danny's second letter** — his answer to Jack's Sept 21 letter (which gave him Lena's name), in the Delgado box
  **Tue Sep 29, Michaelmas**: opens "Happy St. Mike's, Professor" (🔒 Danny was his confirmation sponsor; never stated); Reggie
  has decided the Pacific smells like "money and fish, which is California"; *Brideshead* is still with the C.O. ("he says it's
  about a house"); Gina told him on the Wednesday call that "the veil girl" has a boyfriend — "Gina says a lot of things. Tell
  Lena hey anyway. Lena. I like knowing it." The sentence that stops Jack cold: **"You sound happy out there. Don't feel bad about

- **Regina "Gina" Costigan, 15** (b. Apr 9, 1994). Sophomore at Ursuline High School. **(E05 canon:)** in sophomore

### 10.9 LENA'S FAMILY — the Broussards of New Orleans
Home: a raised double shotgun converted to a single on **N. Dupre Street, Mid-City**, near Bayou St. John. Took 4½ feet
of water in 2005; rebuilt by Tony and his brothers by hand over two years; the waterline is still visible on the shed.
Parish: **Our Lady of the Holy Rosary** (Esplanade Ave.) — the family pews; Lena's First Communion; the Christmas Eve
crawl. Family business: **Broussard's Seafood**, a market on Banks Street.

- **Antoine "Tony" Broussard, 53.** Owns Broussard's Seafood. Loud, sentimental, a world-class griller and grudge-holder,
  Saints season-ticket holder since 1981 (through the Aints years, with a bag on his head in 1980 — family lore). Cajun
  roots in Breaux Bridge; talks to God like a business partner who owes him money.
  - *"Cher, you call your mama or I'm flying out there and I'm bringing the boudin."*
- **Celeste (Guidry) Broussard, 50.** Registered nurse; in 2005 an ICU nurse at **Memorial Medical Center** (Uptown);
  now at Touro Infirmary. Brisk, funny, ferociously competent, gives orders in a whisper. 🔒 **Her mother, Lucille Guidry
  (Lena's grandmother, "Grandmère"), was a long-term acute care patient on the hospital's seventh floor during Katrina, and
  was among those who died there before evacuation.** Celeste was working in the ICU downstairs. On the fourth day she was
  ordered onto a boat with other staff, and went, believing her mother would be evacuated within hours. She was not.
  Celeste has never told her family what she knew or didn't, what she asked or didn't ask, what she was told. The
  coroner returned Lucille's Miraculous Medal in a plastic bag in February 2006; Celeste gave it to Lena at fifteen
  without a word. Lena has never asked. Sheri Fink's long investigation of the Memorial deaths was published in *The New
  York Times Magazine* in late August 2009 — **the week of the pilot.** Celeste texts Lena: *"Don't read the Times this
  week, cher."* 🔒 *Writers' rule:* the show never asserts what any real person at Memorial did or did not do. The
  Broussards' grief is about **uncertainty, absence and a daughter's choice**. Celeste's own culpability, if any, is the
  choice to leave on the boat. The truth Celeste finally tells (adult seasons): she went back up the stairs before she
  left, and her mother was asleep, and she kissed her and left her, and she has wondered every day since if her mother
  ever woke.
- **Luc Broussard, 24.** Eldest; NOPD officer (joined 2006). Wes's best friend. Quiet, good, under pressure: in 2010 the
  federal Danziger Bridge indictments and other post-Katrina NOPD scandals tear at his department. 🔒 He knew things
  about his precinct's conduct in the storm's aftermath that he never reported — a mirror for Lena (S2–S3).
- **Thérèse "Tess" (Broussard) Fontenot, 22.** Married at 21 to Beau Fontenot, a lineman for Entergy; first baby due
  December 2009 (a girl, **Lucille**, born Dec 19, 2009 — Lena becomes godmother over Christmas break).
- **Remy Broussard, 20.** At LSU; party boy; Tiger Stadium; adores Lena; the family's comic disaster.
- **Jude and Josie Broussard, 13.** Twins. Wes carried them out of a neighbor's second floor in 2005. Jude is quiet; Josie
  is Lena in miniature.
- **Mémère — Odile Broussard, 88.** Tony's mother, Breaux Bridge, speaks Cajun French first, makes the best gumbo in
  Louisiana, thinks Jack is "un bon garçon mais trop maigre."
- **(E11 plan — Tony on the page, by phone, for the first time):** Sun Oct 25, Saints at Miami: Lena calls Dupre Street from the Hermitage hill and **Tony
  puts the phone on speaker beside the kitchen radio (WWL)** for three hours while the call drops at every curve of Highway 1 and Kevin pulls into every
  turnout with a bar. Loud, sentimental, a grudge-holder: "Who's driving? … Is he careful? … Good." **"Is that the Ohio boy? Wes says y'all got a Browns
  fan out there."** To Jack: "Browns? Lord, son. You need us more than we need you." Laney takes the phone ("Put the redhead on!"); Tony adores her on
  contact (S2's Mardi Gras makes it official). Lena buys **Mémère** a fruitcake from the monks. Luc, Remy, Tess and Josie flood her phone about the game.
- **(E14 plan — Mémère on the page, by phone):** Sat Nov 7, 7:12 a.m. Pacific (9:12 in Breaux Bridge, home from the eight o'clock at St. Bernard's —
  Researcher: confirm the parish): **the fruitcake came Friday** ("trop sec," she's eating it anyway, a slice thin enough to read the *Teche News* through);
  she lit a candle for Wesley ("He's a good boy. God's not finished."); she is not sorry she asked at the tomb — **"Quelqu'un devait demander."**; she hears a
  man in the kitchen at seven in the morning and demands to know who; "le garçon de l'Ohio" — **she has heard of him from Wesley at Tony's table** ("Wesley
  says you're skinny."); "Oui, madame." The Browns: "Ah. Pauvre garçon." She tells Lena (in French; Lena translates selectively, and Jack can tell) to eat.
  Untracked; she will remember him (S2E07: she checks his plate). **Wes at Thanksgiving:** Luc's best friend has sat at the Broussards' Thanksgiving table
  every year since 2005, and Celeste has told Lena on the phone he's still coming ("He carried the twins, cher.") — the concrete reason Lena would go "anywhere
  nobody knows his name."
- **(S2E03 plan rev. 1:)** **Lucille Odile is baptized Sun Jan 3, 2010, at Our Lady of the Holy Rosary — in the third quarter of Carolina–New Orleans** (Panthers 23–10, starters rested), as she was born in one; Lena godmother; Tony with a radio in his coat. **The christening gown is Grandmère Lucille's sewing** — made for Luc in 1985, worn by all five, kept in **Mémère's cedar chest in Breaux Bridge**, which is why it survived the storm (the only thing Grandmère made still in the family; Lena ironed it herself). 🔒 **Wes came to the house after, not the church** (Luc asked him to stand in the back; his reason is the one he gave Lena on Nov 2 — never on the page). **Julian learned the Creed for it and didn't say it; held Lena's purse; flew home to Oakland Jan 4 with Mémère's pralines and a holy card** ("come back"); **Mémère calls him *le petit violon*** (Tess's album caption). **Twelfth Night (Jan 6): Lena got the baby in the first king cake** — so the next one is hers; **she flies back Sun Jan 10 with a king cake on her lap**; Laney meets her at SBA at four (Kevin drives). Lucille grabbed Lena's medal at the goodbye and Tess had to open her fingers one at a time. 🔒 That night, in 217, Lena sees the status (§23.1 S2E03).
- **(S2E12 published / S2E13 plan — new canon on Dupre Street):** **Fr. Lucien Hébert**, seventies, pastor of Our Lady of the Holy Rosary since 1984 (fictional): baptized all five Broussard children (and Lucille, Jan 3), gave Lena her First Communion, will give her ashes on Ash Wednesday (S2E17); short homilies, a Breaux Bridge accent, calls Lena "Magdalena" and nobody else does in that church. **The Broussards sit the eight o'clock** — the same two pews on the Gospel side, Mémère on the aisle; **Tony prays aloud there** ("Lord, I wore the bag for You. One and fifteen, I wore the bag. You owe me one."). **Nonc Clovis Broussard**, Tony's younger brother (one of the brothers who put the house back by hand; knows the first verse of everything; named a dog *Aints* in 1980 — the dog was ashamed; the current dog is Aints III). **The Vikings seating:** since the NFC Championship (Jan 24) every Broussard watches from the seat they had that night; **Tony listens from the porch** on WWL radio (the Saints' radio call — never quote the real announcer), because he couldn't watch the overtime; nobody new has a seat. **Luc** is called in for Super Bowl night (NOPD, all hands for the Quarter and Bourbon Street) and works till dawn. **The front room:** the big television, Mémère's daybed and lamp by the window, the couch; the porch swing and Tony's kitchen chair with the radio on the rail.
- **(S2E14 plan — new canon on Dupre Street, Banks Street and Canal; Continuity to confirm after drafting):** **Broussard's Seafood closes Monday and Tuesday of victory week** (Tony's sign in the window: CLOSED · WHO DAT · BACK WEDNESDAY · GOD WILLING) and reopens Wednesday; **Mr. Alcide** (the shucker, forty-one years — existing minor canon) opens oysters there; **Nonc Placide Broussard**, Tony's eldest brother (one of the brothers who put the house back by hand), shrimps out of **Empire, Plaquemines Parish, on the *Miss Odile*** (named for Mémère) — the case's shrimp are his (🔒 the boat Deepwater Horizon ties up, S2E27–E29). **Celeste took Monday Feb 8 off** (her first personal day since 2006; Touro); she makes groceries on Mondays; **the family's Mardi Gras costume is chosen at Monday's red beans: the bag** — gold-painted grocery bags with eyeholes cut by Celeste's sewing scissors (the 1980 bag redeemed: "We wore it in shame. We'll wear it in glory."), sizes assigned by Celeste — **Jack "a large"**, nobody consulted, nobody corrects (worn S2E16; the room may restyle it). **The twins** were in school Monday and let out early Tuesday for the parade [V]; **Jude**'s first full sentence to Jack is about Rosie's brontosaurus ("It's *Apatosaurus* now.") and he keeps the secret for her. **Remy** goes back to Baton Rouge Wednesday morning and returns Friday for Endymion. **Luc** keeps his own apartment (fictional; off Bayou St. John) and eats his mother's plates after shifts; he works the parade at a Canal Street barricade. **The ring:** 🔒 Wes gave Mémère's ring back in its box after Mass the Sunday after All Souls (Nov 8, 2009); **Mémère keeps it in the cedar chest in Breaux Bridge with Grandmère Lucille's christening gown** (Josie tells Jack at the parade; → S5E18). **Grandmère Lucille Guidry** is in the **Guidry family tomb at St. Louis No. 3** (Esplanade, by the bayou); she was a seamstress (pins in her mouth; the christening gown, 1985); **she called Lena "Magdalena"** — the whole name — as Hébert does; **Wes has whitewashed the tomb every All Saints since 2005**, including Nov 1, 2009 (the day Mémère asked "Quand?"). **The bridge:** in 2005–06, the year Lena went to Mass every morning to yell at God, she yelled first from the **Magnolia Bridge** over Bayou St. John ("He got it in stereo."). **The medal's chain:** the clasp weakened when Lucille grabbed it in January and gave in the parade crowd (Tue Feb 9); Jack fastens it at the tomb (Wed).

### 10.10 CALEB HARGROVE — Hale's acolyte (added after S1E01)
Born **March 3, 1991** — 18. Visalia (Tulare County). Homeschooled until tenth grade, then Redwood High '09. Philosophy.
PHIL 9H. Portolá Hall.
**Who he is.** A Pentecostal (Assemblies of God) pastor's son, raised on tongues and the King James ("Selah," "verily," by
reflex). Deconverted at sixteen reading *The Consolations of Disbelief*; now Hale's most devoted reader — forty Post-its, a
signed copy, a Darwin fish on his laptop. Fast, funny, a little desperate, generous like a puppy; does tongues at parties as
a bit and looks sick afterward. 🔒 **Why he left:** at fifteen his father's church collapsed when the treasurer emptied the
building fund; the congregation scattered; his father's faith stayed untouched and serene, and Caleb could not forgive the
serenity (Hale's own wound a generation down; Hale will recognize it and use it). 🔒 He wrote Hale **four letters of
devotion; Hale never answered** — Hale writes only to believers who fight him. Caleb learns in S1E02 that Hale answered
Jack, and in S1E14 that he answered Lena. **Arc (MS):** S1 the boy Hale's book worked on, Jack's comic shadow; S2 Lena beats
Hale at the Forum and something in Caleb cracks; S3 he becomes Laney's study partner for the first actuarial exam (a deck of cards for the breaks; neither tells anyone); S8 (open) the
Easter Vigil — a back pew, gone before the Gloria. Never a strawman: his unbelief is honest grief, and he's right that his
father's church was a con for some of the people in it.
**(E14 plan — #41 turns):** at Hale's dinner, alone, with a bottle of wine he was told not to bring; he learns **Hale answered Lena too** (both of them,
nine pages and twelve; "I've used three") — "I wrote you four letters." / "I know. I keep them. I don't answer devotion, Mr. Hargrove. It doesn't need
me." He puts his napkin down and goes. [fork c] Jack finds him on the Shipwreck Cove stairs: 🔒 **"My dad never answered either. He just *smiled*."**
(the serene father — Hale's own wound a generation down); "Did *she* know? That you both —" "I didn't." He doesn't use the thesaurus line again.
**Voice.** Central Valley twang, rapid, King James cadence used ironically; self-deprecating; "dude" in moments of terror.
- *"He wrote you back? I wrote him four letters. Four. I used a thesaurus on the third one."*

### 10.11 YUSUF NOORZAI — the third believer at the table (added after S1E01)
Born **November 12, 1990** — 18. Fremont, California (Little Kabul). Mission San Jose High '09. Aerospace engineering; PHIL
9H as his honors GE. Cabrillo Hall. Afghan-American, Sunni, devout and unshowy: finds a quiet stairwell for the prayers,
fasts Ramadan (Aug 22 – Sept 19, 2009 — he's fasting through Hale's first seminar), doesn't drink, plays cricket on the
Commons with grad students on Sundays. Dry, kind, precise; calls Jack and Lena "the Catholics"; Margot calls the three of
them "the Abrahamic bloc." Father **Ahmad**, a 1985 refugee by way of Peshawar, works the line at **NUMMI**, the GM–Toyota
plant in Fremont: GM pulled out in June 2009 and Toyota announced in late August it would close the plant in spring 2010
(Researcher to verify). Two sons of auto workers at Hale's table. Mother **Farida** runs a home daycare. Older brother
**Tariq**, 24, is a contract interpreter with the US Army in Helmand. 🔒 Tariq is wounded by an IED in late November 2009;
Yusuf gets the call the week of the West Point speech (S1E19). **Arc (SEA→MS):** S1 a friend at the table; E04 the
health-care night; E19 Tariq; S2 NUMMI closes (April 2010). The only arguments in the show where three people agree on
the first premise. Never a token: his own jokes, his own doubts (angrier at the Taliban than at God, and at America for
leaving the first time).
**Voice.** Bay Area understatement; deadpan; "inshallah" only when he means it; engineering metaphors ("load-bearing,"
"factor of safety"); a running bit about Catholic potlucks.
**(E14 plan:)** Thursday, Fort Hood (the shooter's name and faith on every screen by evening): Jack texts him (Tariq, Helmand) — *Ask me tomorrow.* Friday
at Hale's, quiet, with his mother's dates: "My brother called this morning. He's fine. He said don't watch the news. I watched the news." When a guest
asks what Muslims think, Hale answers for the room ("He's a guest"); Yusuf, after: "Thank you, Professor. I'd like one week where nobody asks." Never a
token; his own joke before the pudding (a Catholic potluck has never once run out of food; "it's the only miracle I've personally verified").
- *"I'm fasting, Professor. My soul is the only part of me that isn't hungry."*

### 10.12 RUDY SALCEDO — the Anchor's line cook (added after S1E01)
Born **March 30, 1966** — 43. Oxnard, then Marisol's Westside. Six years at Soledad (Correctional Training Facility) for
the armed robbery of a liquor store at nineteen (1985–1991; a starter pistol, a pint of Bacardi in him, nobody hurt).
Sober since 1994 (AA, Tuesday nights in St. Brendan's parish hall). Gloria hired him in 1995 when nobody would. Nights on
the line. A rosary tattooed around his left wrist (done inside); Vin Scully on a transistor; Louis L'Amour paperbacks in
his apron; the 9:30 at St. Brendan's, back row (he nods to Ray Ochoa; they don't talk). Gentle, slow, deadpan about the
dish machine ("Hobart. Older than you, meaner than Gloria"). Never volunteers prison, never hides it. His mother rode three
buses from Oxnard every other Sunday for six years. 🔒 **Role:** Jack's mirror for Danny; after E03 Jack can't look at
him for a while. E15: "I know what an errand is, mijo" (Rafi's offer). S8: Danny visits for graduation and he and Rudy talk
at the counter for an hour about nothing. Not a saint: a temper he manages like a stove.
**Voice.** Soft, unhurried, Westside Chicano; "mijo"; never raises it.
- *"First time I washed dishes was at Soledad. Six years. Best job in the building — it's warm, and nobody bothers the dish man."*

    holy and genuinely exhausting. Fist-bumps after Mass. *"Brother. Brother. Let's grab a coffee and talk about your

    2013. Lives in Cabrillo Hall. *"Jack! JACK. You're Italian? Half? Half counts, the good half."*
  - **Becca Lindell** (above).
- **The rival couple — Peter Haddad and Kenzie Rourke.** Juniors. Peter (b. Mar 8, 1989): Orange County Maronite family,
  political science, Newman president, perfect, ambitious (wants to be a congressman), lector. Kenzie (b. Oct 1, 1989):
  Sacramento, nursing, cantor with a gorgeous voice, kind. Newman's "it couple"; they give the Theology of the Body talk
  every fall ("Love Is Patient: Our Chastity Story"). 🔒 **They are not chaste and haven't been since the summer of 2008.**
  Peter is terrified of being found out; Kenzie is tired of lying. Kenzie gets pregnant in S3; Peter's first instinct is
  the clinic, and Kenzie's is the opposite, and the Newman community gets a real-life test of everything it says. They
  marry (S3), divorce (adult seasons). They are the dark mirror of Jack and Lena: a couple whose performance of holiness
  is the problem, not their sin. Not villains: Peter's hypocrisy is fear; his eventual honesty is brave.
  **(E06 plan — the talk, Fri Sep 18, 7:30 p.m., Newman House lounge:)** a PowerPoint on a borrowed projector; 1 Cor 13:4
  on the title slide; photos (the Disneyland one; Kenzie's cousin's wedding); their slideshow song is Jason Mraz & Colbie
  Caillat, "Lucky"; Tyler MCs. They met at a Steubenville youth conference (summer 2007), "chose to wait" (🔒). At the Q&A
  **Margot reads Eph 5:22–24 (RSV) and asks Kenzie whether she plans to submit.** **Kenzie** answers with v. 21 and v. 25 —
  she'll submit to a man exactly as far as he's already laying his life down for her, and she'll know because he'll have been
  doing it every day before she's asked — better than Margot expected; Margot says so. **Peter**: "Practically? When we can't
  agree, I make the call. Prayerfully." Kenzie's face. If Jack asks *"What do you do when you fall?"*, Peter: **"By God's
  grace, we haven't had to find out."** Kenzie looks at her hands (🔒 the lie; she is tired of it). At the BBQ Kenzie tells
  Jack, quietly, "Good question. Nobody asks that one." Peter avoids him.
- **The choir:** led by **Gus Ferreira**, 60s, retired Portuguese-American tuna-fleet captain, organist, a voice like a
  foghorn.
- **The 9 p.m. Sunday Mass** is the college Mass: candles, guitar, standing room. The 11:30 is the "families and
  serious people" Mass; the pilot's collision happens there.

# PART III — THE HIDDEN ARCHITECTURE

## 13. Hidden prior knowledge at the pilot (Knowledge Auditor: read this)

At 6:48 a.m. on August 29, 2009, before the first line of the pilot, these people already know things the player doesn't:

- **Lena** knows: Nora Calloway (her Preview Weekend host, April 24–26, 2009); the Lighthouse house and the path to the
  Point (Nora walked her past it on Friday night, April 24); Nora was pregnant (the test in the trash); that she herself
  removed and discarded the test; that she told police she slept through; that around 12:45 a.m. she heard a boy crying
  in the Serra Hall corridor and a door shut, and didn't look. Fr. Osei (she confessed to him April 26). Mrs. Fitch (met
  at the Preview brunch). Hale (postcard, 2008). She does **not** know Theo, Kevin, Evan, Julian (she knows *of* Julian
  — Nora mentioned "my friend Jules who writes songs"), or Jack.
- **Theo** knows: what he did; Kevin (the beach stairs, the floor of Kevin's host's room); Fr. Osei (his confession, July
  2009); the Lighthouse; the Point; Nora's name (from the news). He has never seen Lena (she was asleep in Serra; he never
  saw her). He has Nora's jacket in a duffel in his closet.
- **Kevin** knows: Theo, and what Theo looked like at 12:45 a.m. He does not know what happened. He knows Nora's name
  from the news and the Newman memorial Mass. He has seen Lena once (the Preview Weekend Newman brunch, across the room)
  and might recognize her. He knows Fr. Osei (Preview brunch; a summer email).
- **Fr. Osei** knows: Lena (her confession); Theo (his confession); Kevin (brunch); Nora (his parishioner and soprano).
  He knows, from the two confessions, more than anyone. He can use none of it, and he will not even let it change how he
  speaks to them in a way that would betray the seal.
- **Hale** knows: Jack (his nine-page letter, 2008); Lena (her twelve-page letter, 2008 — longer, he notes); Nora (his
  student; the forty-one seconds). He has never seen Jack or Lena's faces. He knows their names are on his PHIL 9H roster.
- **Evan** knows: Nora; the pregnancy; the text; the blond boy (not his name or face clearly).
- **Priya** knows: Nora (freshman roommate); the box.
- **Rafi** knows: he sold Nora two bars that night.
- **Julian** knows: Nora; the wall at the Point where they sang.
- **Mrs. Fitch** knows: Nora; Lena (Preview brunch: "the New Orleans girl who asked for the mantilla basket").
- **Sloane** knows: Nora; that Nora was "seeing someone older"; that Nora left the party around 10:50 p.m. upset.
- **Margot, Laney, Jack**: know none of these people and nothing about Nora.

## 15. The elision rule (how close third keeps Jack's secret honestly)

Jack is the POV and the player *is* Jack, so the narration must never lie about what Jack did. It may **elide**: it can
decline to narrate a memory. Jack thinks about Danny constantly; the narration says so. It shows Jack flinching from the
scar story, smoking when Danny's name comes up, sending money orders to a "D. Kostelnik" (S1E05, a detail with no
explanation), writing letters he doesn't send. It never says "Danny did it" in Jack's voice; it never says "Jack did it"
until the reveal. When the truth comes out (S2E22), every earlier scene must read as honest in retrospect: the player
should feel *Jack was carrying this the whole time and I was carrying it with him without knowing.*
- Allowed: "Jack doesn't think about that night. He's good at it."
- Not allowed: "Jack has never hurt anyone."

## 16. The eyebrow scar — canon of the tellings

Jack tells the story differently every time. Track every telling in `continuity.md`. Never repeat a version with the same
person. The **truth** (🔒; revised for the brief's hard rule — no sexual element): November 23, 2007, a bonfire in the lot
behind the dead Republic Steel works in Struthers; Mikey Kostelnik, 18, drunk, Carly Benedetto's ex-boyfriend of two
weeks, had already backhanded her once in front of everyone and had her by the wrist and the hair, dragging her toward
his pickup to drive her home himself, drunk, while she screamed that she wasn't going (🔒 the drunk driver Jack stopped —
a rhyme with Laney's Kaylee and Hale's two drivers, never stated); Jack, 16, pulled him off; Mikey swung first, wearing his
Struthers High class ring, and split Jack's left eyebrow; Jack hit him once, with everything; Mikey went down backward and
his head struck the cinderblock fire ring. Danny, 20, arrived at the run, took one look, took Jack's bloody hand and wiped
it on his own shirt, and when the Struthers police came said, "It was me."

## 17. JACK'S SECRET (full)

**What happened:** §16. Mikey Kostelnik lived. He has a traumatic brain injury. Struthers PD found Danny with blood on his
shirt and Jack's scholarship-track future on the bench in the back of the cruiser. Danny had a prior (a 2006 bar fight,
misdemeanor assault) and was on probation; the Mahoning County prosecutor charged felonious assault; Danny took a plea
for five years in January 2008. At the station at 4 a.m., Jack, sixteen, tried once to tell a detective the truth; Frank
walked in and took him out of the room by the back of his neck. On the bench in the hall, Jack prayed for the first time
in his life like someone was there. He has been praying like that ever since. **His faith was born the night he became a
coward.** That's the knot.

**Why it matters to the show:** Jack spends seasons judging Theo's silence — and Lena's — while living inside his own. The
central mystery is a mirror: everyone who loves Theo will be asked what Jack's family already chose. Hale's specialty is
*moral luck* (Williams, Nagel): the idea that we are judged for outcomes we didn't control. Jack threw one punch in
defense of a girl; Mikey hit a cinderblock. Theo grabbed a girl to save her; she fell. Hale's seminar will put the
question to Jack in the abstract in S1E05 and he will argue it like his life depends on it, and the player won't know
why yet.

**The money orders.** Jack sends $20–$60 monthly to Donna Kostelnik, unsigned. Shown without explanation from S1E05.

**The clock.** 🔒 Jack is aware, vaguely and with dread, that there are time limits on prosecutions, and that if he does
nothing long enough, nothing can be done. *Writers: never specify the law on the page. The dread is moral, not legal.*
The show's position: he will tell, and the telling (S7, Fall 2012, to Mikey's mother first, then to the Mahoning County
prosecutor) costs him; what the law does about it is less important than what Donna Kostelnik does — 🔒 she slams the
door, and then, in S8, she comes to Danny's welcome-home Mass.

**Danny's release:** judicial release granted November 2011 (S5) — or the full term to January 2013, depending on whether
Jack has told the truth by then (S5 path flag). Danny at Jack's graduation, May 2013. Danny as godfather to Jack's first
child. **(Re-planned after S1E11:)** Lena knows the truth before the proposal (S5 at the latest; the player may tell her from S3).
Danny stands up at the wedding (July 21, 2012) only if he is out; if not, Jack and Lena drive to Trumbull's visiting room the
week they're home, in the suit and the dress (room's call) — the path's price, paid in a cinderblock room.

## 18. LENA'S SECRETS (full)

**A. The Preview Weekend (tied to the central mystery).**
- April 24, 2009 (Friday): Lena, 17, arrives for Marisol Preview Weekend. St. Brendan's runs a hosting program for Catholic
  admits; her host is **Nora Calloway** (Serra Hall 3B; Sloane was away for the night at the Pi Lam formal in Santa
  Barbara). Nora is luminous, funny, kind, a soprano; they stay up talking about Catherine of Siena and boys. Nora walks
  her past the Lighthouse to the Point at sunset on Friday and shows her the wall: "This is where I come to yell at God."
  Lena falls a little in love with the idea of becoming her.
  🔒 **(Added after S1E13, for E14's postcards:)** over Nora's desk in Serra 3B, pinned with a thumbtack, is **Hale's 2007 postcard** — the
  Radcliffe Camera, *Come and say it to my face. —A.H.* Lena, who has the same card in her missal at home, laughs out loud; Nora laughs too: "He only
  writes the ones who mean it. I'm taking his seminar. I said it to his face *twice*." (Nora takes the card down Saturday night; it goes into her
  jacket pocket — §20.5.) **So when Hale says at his table that he has "used three," Lena knows exactly who the third was** — and that is the medal
  (thinking) Jack sees and can't read (E14). She never says so; the narration never connects it.
- April 25 (Saturday): Nora is distracted all day; disappears for an hour after lunch (she bought the test at Walgreens,
  2:14 p.m.). Newman admit dinner 6–8 p.m. At 10:30 p.m. Nora goes to "a party for an hour"; asks Lena to come; Lena
  declines (she's seventeen, tired, and a good girl in a strange town). Nora returns at 11:15, shaking, goes into the
  bathroom; Lena, pretending to sleep, hears her crying and praying the Memorare. At 11:40 Nora kneels by Lena's air
  mattress and whispers: *"Cover for me, Magdalena. If anyone asks, I'm in the shower."* Leaves.
- 11:45 p.m.: Lena gets up for water and sees the test in the bathroom trash. Two lines.
- ~12:45 a.m.: Lena hears a boy crying in the corridor — a broken, gasping sound — then a door down the hall open and shut.
  She doesn't look. She's covering.
- April 26, 7:40 a.m.: the Serra RA knocks: there's been an accident. Before police arrive, Lena takes the test out of the
  trash, wraps it in a Newman bulletin, walks it to the dumpster behind Serra Hall, and comes back. To Det. Ochoa she says
  she was asleep by eleven and Nora was "fine. A little sad. Normal sad." She touches her grandmother's medal the whole
  time.
- April 26, 2:00 p.m.: she goes to St. Brendan's and makes her confession to Fr. Osei: she lied to the police and she
  threw away something that belonged to a dead girl. He absolves her and tells her, gently and firmly, that she should
  tell the police the truth. She doesn't. She tells herself she's protecting a dead girl's name and a family in Fresno. 🔒
  The irony she doesn't know: the autopsy already told the police about the pregnancy. Her sin hid nothing. Her guilt is
  real anyway.
- She turns down Notre Dame (partial aid) for Marisol (Regents' Scholarship, full tuition) and tells everyone it was the
  money. It was also Nora: "I owe her four years."
- She never told anyone about the boy crying in the corridor. She has thought about him every night.

**B. Grandmère and Memorial (family rupture).** See §10.9. Lena knows her grandmother died at Memorial during Katrina; she
knows her mother was working in the building and left on a boat on the fourth day; she has never asked her mother a single
question about it. She has read every public article about the Memorial deaths and hates herself for it. Celeste's text
on August 30, 2009 (*"Don't read the Times this week, cher."*) is the first time her mother has acknowledged that there is
anything to read.

**C. Wes.** She knows something's wrong. She has noticed he hasn't mentioned Mass since Labor Day. She's decided not to
notice. **(Re-planned after S1E11:)** On All Souls (S1E13) she asks, and he tells her, and ends it (§10.1).

**D. The postcard.** Hale wrote her the same line he wrote Jack. She came, in part, to say it to his face.

## 20. THE CENTRAL MYSTERY — "THE POINT" 🔒

The player chose "surprise me completely." This is the spine that will entangle the ensemble from the pilot through at
least S5, with consequences through the full run.

### 20.1 The surface (what Marisol believes)
At about 6:10 a.m. on **Sunday, April 26, 2009** (the Third Sunday of Easter), two surfers paddling out at the Point break
found the body of **Nora Grace Calloway**, 19, a sophomore, on the rocks below the old Point Marisol Light. The coroner
found a BAC of 0.09 and a therapeutic level of alprazolam. Her phone was in her jeans, destroyed. Marisol PD (Det. Sgt.
Ray Ochoa) ruled it an accidental fall: she was known to sit on the seaward side of the low wall at night. The campus held
a vigil. St. Brendan's held a memorial Mass. A white wooden cross stands at the wall, and every Sunday before dawn
someone leaves fresh flowers there; nobody knows who. Privately, many — including her parents' parish in Selma, the
detective, Julian, and later Margot — believe it was suicide.

### 20.2 Who she was
Nora Grace Calloway, born **September 8, 1989** (the Nativity of Mary) in Selma, California. Father Tom, a raisin farmer;
mother Rosa (Gutiérrez), a school-district bookkeeper; two younger brothers (Mateo, 15; Sam, 12). Philosophy major, Music
minor, Newman choir soprano. Funny, generous, intense, devout, doubting, brave. Freshman year in Delgado 222 with Priya;
sophomore year in Serra 3B with Sloane. She wore a Levi's jean jacket with a **Fresno Fair pin** on the collar and an
embroidered **Our Lady of Guadalupe patch** sewn on the back by her grandmother. She sang with Julian at the Point wall.
She sent Hale a rebuttal in high school and got his postcard. She took his seminar. She fell in love with his TA.

### 20.3 The truth of the night (timeline)
- **Oct 2008–Apr 2009:** Nora and Evan Marsh, secretly together.
- **Sat Apr 25, 2:14 p.m.:** Walgreens on Mission Street: pregnancy test. Positive (about 8 weeks).
- **6:00–8:00 p.m.:** Newman admit dinner (Nora hosts Lena).
- **~8:30 p.m.:** Nora texts Evan the news. He calls; they fight — he panics, says "we can't," says "there are options."
- **10:30 p.m.:** Nora goes to the Lighthouse party (the last house on Seacliff Road, rented by senior surfers). Julian is
  there with his guitar; they sing one song on the stairs ("Skinny Love"). Rafi Ochoa, a high-school senior then, is
  selling. Nora buys two Xanax bars from him: she hasn't slept in a week. She takes one with a beer. Sloane sees her leave
  at ~10:50, crying.
- **Also at the Lighthouse:** Theo Vance, 18, an admit, crashing with an LA friend's older brother who lives there. Around
  10:45 he goes down the bluff stairs to the beach to smoke and meets **Kevin Tran**, 18, an admit, who wandered out of
  the party because he couldn't breathe. They talk for an hour. They kiss. Kevin leaves ~11:50 for his host's room in
  Serra Hall, shaking with joy and terror. Theo stays, does two lines of cocaine alone on the stairs, and walks out along
  the bluff toward the light.
- **11:15 p.m.:** Nora back at Serra; the bathroom; the Memorare. **11:40:** "Cover for me, Magdalena." **11:45:** Lena sees
  the test.
- **11:52 p.m.:** On the Point path, Nora calls Hale. Forty-one seconds. *"Go home, Nora. You're drunk and you're boring
  me."*
- **12:05 a.m.:** Nora texts Evan: *"I'm at the Point. Please come. I'm keeping it. I want to keep it. I want you to want
  it."* She sits on the seaward side of the wall, legs over the drop, as she has done a hundred times, and prays aloud.
- **~12:25 a.m.:** Theo, high, comes up the path in the dark and sees a girl on the outside of the wall, talking to
  someone who isn't there. He thinks she's about to jump. He runs at her and grabs her from behind by the jacket. She
  startles, twists, her hand slips off the wall; the jacket pulls off her shoulders as she goes; he's left holding it. She
  doesn't scream. He hears her hit. The last words he heard her say were *"…never was it known that anyone who fled to thy
  protection…"*
- **~12:27–12:31:** Theo, in shock, runs. Down the Point path toward Seacliff Road, the jacket clutched to his chest.
- **12:20:** Evan reads the text and drives. **12:31:** at the Point lot his headlights catch a tall blond boy running
  toward Seacliff Road holding something dark. Evan goes to the wall; it's black; he calls her phone (it's under her, in
  the surf, already dead); he waits ten minutes, decides she's left to punish him, drives home. He deletes the text the
  next morning. He keeps a screenshot on his laptop he took at 12:21 to "show her later how scared he'd been." It's still
  there.
- **~12:45 a.m.:** Theo walks to Serra Hall — the only place on campus he knows anyone — and knocks on Kevin's host's door
  (Serra 3F, two doors from Nora's room), soaked to the knees from crossing the creek mouth, palms scraped raw from the
  path, holding the jacket. He's crying. *"You never saw me."* Kevin lets him in; he sleeps on the floor; he's gone at
  dawn. **This is the crying boy Lena heard.**
- **6:10 a.m.:** surfers find her.

### 20.4 The layers of guilt (no villains)
Every person who touched that night believes, privately, that they killed Nora Calloway:
- **Theo** — he did, by trying to save her. The truest guilt and the least culpable intent.
- **Evan** — he said "there are options," didn't answer at 12:05, saw the boy, drove away, lied.
- **Hale** — forty-one seconds.
- **Lena** — she covered for her; she didn't stop her; she hid the test; she didn't look at the crying boy.
- **Rafi** — the Xanax.
- **Kevin** — he let Theo in and never asked.
- **Julian** — he didn't see she was drowning.
- **Sloane** — she let her walk out of the party crying.
- **Priya** — they drifted.
- **Ray Ochoa** — he closed it as an accident while believing it was suicide, out of mercy, and that mercy kept the truth
  buried.

The show's answer, delivered over seasons and never as a speech: everyone did a small wrong thing, the fall was an
accident, and Nora **was not trying to die** — she had chosen to keep her child and was praying the Memorare on the wall
where she always prayed. The proof is two things only a guilty man and a coward kept: Evan's screenshot of the text, and
Theo's memory of the prayer. The truth heals one person completely — Rosa Calloway, her mother, who has believed for two
years that her daughter killed herself and her grandchild. In S5, Rosa receives Communion for the first time since April
2009. That's the payoff the whole mystery is built for.

### 20.5 Physical evidence and clues
- **The jean jacket** (Theo's closet, in a black Prada duffel on the top shelf). Levi's, women's small, Fresno Fair pin
  on the collar, Guadalupe patch on the back. Inside pocket: **Hale's 2007 postcard to Nora** (Radcliffe Camera; "Come and
  say it to my face. —A.H."), folded soft; a Walgreens receipt (Apr 25, 2:14 p.m.: First Response, $16.99); a St. Brendan's
  choir schedule. Police report notes "victim reportedly wearing a denim jacket; not recovered; presumed lost to the sea."
- **Phone records:** 11:52 p.m. call to Hale (41 sec); 12:05 a.m. text to Evan Marsh. Ochoa interviewed both. Hale said she
  was upset about a paper. Evan said he was asleep and saw the text in the morning. Content of the text never retrieved.
- **Evan's laptop:** the 12:21 screenshot.
- **The cross and the Sunday flowers:** Theo. Every Sunday before dawn. Supermarket roses in winter; jasmine from Las Olas
  fences in summer.
- **Nora's journal** (Priya's box): last entry April 23: *"If I tell him and he says no, I'll still say yes. Lord, to whom
  shall we go."* (John 6:68.) Priya opens it in S2.
- **Julian's song "Fresno":** a line, *"you said the wall was where you yelled at God / I never heard him yell back"* —
  and a verse about her jacket.
- **The postcards:** Jack's, Lena's, Nora's. Same line, same handwriting, same Radcliffe Camera image. Hale's habit.
- **Lena's memory:** the boy crying in the corridor at Serra Hall; a door two down the hall.
- **Kevin's Preview Weekend host:** Serra 3F, two doors from 3B. In the housing records Margot pulls (S3).
- **Evan's sighting:** tall, blond, running, carrying something dark.
- **The Lighthouse:** the senior surfers rotate out; in Fall 2009 it's rented by a new crew who throw the season-opening
  party (the pilot). A photo from April 25 on a Facebook album ("LIGHTHOUSE LAST HURRAH 4/25") shows Theo in the
  background, by the stairs, at 10:41 p.m. Margot finds it in S3.

### 20.6 Red herrings (fair, each true about something)
1. **Hale did it** (S2): the postcard in the jacket points at him; his drinking, his possessiveness, his lie about the
   call. He didn't push her; he did fail her.
2. **Suicide** (S1–S2): the pregnancy, the Xanax, the crying, "cover for me," the town's whisper. Wrong — and the most
   cruel wrong.
3. **Evan pushed her** (S2–S3): he was there; he lied; he's unstable. He didn't.
4. **Julian** (S2, briefly; Jack's jealousy makes him want it): he loved her, he wrote the song, he knows the wall. No.
5. **Sloane / Pi Lam hazing** (S1E12, Laney's arc): a rumor the sorority made pledges walk the wall; false, though the
   rumor is real and leads to the Halloween scare.
6. **Rafi's pills killed her** (S2): the Xanax made her unsteady. Partly true; not the cause.

Osei gave it to Lena after the Gaudete Mass — 🔒 the priest who holds Theo's confession under the seal handing on a letter about the jacket; nothing on the page). **Fri–Sat night, the Point (s15), inside the walk:** Lena goes past the last house for the first time all semester; Nora on the wall, looking back over her shoulder, laughing — Our Lady on her back, the red Ferris wheel on the collar; "It was my weekend. The Saturday." (new to Jack); **"I don't know what she was wearing. I was asleep."** — her hand to the medal (🔒 the police lie; recorded, never read; S2E05's lie-tell note makes it legible). **Jack has held that jacket — one sentence: his hands, the shelf, the knot in the thread, somebody taking it out of his hands; no Theo, no Prague, no Evan, no Halloween, no conclusion; never on a card.** No smash to black — the season ends on Skye's buzz (brief); Jack carries the silence to the roof and the airport and tells no one. Theo leaves Friday for LA; over Christmas he moves the duffel (as below).
- **E22 (season cliffhanger):** On the last night before break, Lena shows Jack a photo on her laptop: Nora at the Point
  wall, laughing, in her jean jacket — the Guadalupe patch, the Fresno Fair pin. "They never found it. Her mom asked me in
  a letter if I remembered what she was wearing." Jack has seen that jacket. Smash to black.

**S2 (Spring 2010):** Over Christmas Theo moves the duffel (his mother's pool house in La Cañada). **(S2E12 plan rev. 1, hidden canon:)** the real **La Cañada Flintridge debris flows of early Sat Feb 6, 2010** (public record: a burst of rain on the Station Fire burn above the city; mud through the Paradise Valley neighborhood at the top of Ocean View Boulevard; dozens of homes damaged, hundreds evacuated; no deaths) reach Caroline's street: **her house stands; mud fills the pool and comes in under the pool-house doors to the sills, and the county tags the pool house unsafe to enter (fictional) until March.** Nobody goes in; Theo, on the phone from San Antonio, tells her for the second time not to. **This is why the duffel stays put until Easter** — Theo drives down for it himself in Holy Week and it is back on the 412 shelf after Easter (the "S2E16" below is the OLD 22-episode number = **new S2E25** by §23's crosswalk; the S2E11 log's "by S2E16" means the same). Jack hears only Theo's half ("Mom. Don't go in it. Let them — don't."); no connection on the page. **S2E04 (Tue Jan 12; re-mapped from "S2E03"):** Jack checks the
closet — gone (and, Tuesday night, finds the Facebook group *In Memory of Nora Calloway* — Julian, Priya and Lena are members; Theo is not; its wall is grief, never clues — no post about the flowers, the cross or the jacket's loss; [`joined_nora_group`] the News Feed carries it to Theo 🔒). He investigates in silence, alone, while his life fills with Skye, the Saints and New Orleans; Margot starts the
anniversary feature (S2E12) and, later, he with her. On the trip, one beat only: Luc, NOPD, at the Broussards' kitchen table,
on how cops close a case they feel sorry for (🔒 Ray Ochoa's mercy, unnamed). **(Specified by `outlines/s2e14.md` rev. 1 — S2E14 s09, Wed Feb 10, 1:10 a.m.:)** Luc, off sixteen hours on Canal, eats the plate his mother left in the oven: first the night's — a man of seventy-one dead of his heart on his feet in his Saints jacket, "natural causes," which is true and is all it will ever say, and his daughter will tell it for forty years ("he died at the parade"); then, because Jack is a stranger and you can tell a stranger (Wes's S1E09 reason, unglossed), **the one he can't put down: Gentilly, spring 2006, a man back in his gutted house, the gas left on; the note, or not; the sergeant wrote it "accidental" so the widow could have the funeral Mass at St. Raphael's and the policy would pay — "Nobody lied. He just didn't write down what nobody could prove." — "You write some of them the way the family can live with."** 🔒 It is Ray Ochoa's mercy (§20.4) without his name, and a mirror of Jack's own 4 a.m. in Struthers (§17) without Danny's; **Jack's narration infers nothing and connects nothing** (no Point, no Ochoa, no Nora, no cross, no Struthers); the player may. Luc's own 🔒 weight (what he didn't report after the storm, §10.9) stays under it. Then the eyebrow (§16). This is the trip's one mystery beat. **S2E16:** the duffel is back on the shelf after
Easter; Jack opens it and finds Hale's postcard to Nora in the jacket's inside pocket → the Hale suspicion (red herring #1),
sharpened because Lena has just beaten Hale at the Forum (S2E13). **S2E17:** Priya opens the journal (the April 23 entry). **S2E18,
the anniversary (Sun Apr 25 – Mon Apr 26, 2010, Good Shepherd Sunday):** Evan confronts Theo at the cross before dawn with the
flowers in his hand; Jack, following Theo for the first time, intervenes; Evan knows now. **S2E22:** Theo tells Jack the truth on
the wall. Jack, in exchange — because it's the only thing he can offer — tells Theo about Danny. (The player learns both truths in
the same scene.) **Jack is Lena's boyfriend by then, and now he carries a secret that isn't his.**

**S3 (Fall 2010):** Jack holds Theo's secret while Theo holds himself together in public — and holds it from Lena, his girlfriend;
Margot dates Evan and finds the screenshot; Lena confides about the test (E18, Thanksgiving in New Orleans, the kitchen at 1 a.m.)
— to Jack, who can't tell her what he knows. Kevin comes out to Jack and Lena.

**S4 (Spring 2011):** Jack and Lena together, with the secret between them. Margot's reporting closes in. Evan goes to the
Calloways. Kevin decides to testify. **April 24, 2011, Easter Sunday:** Theo goes to Mass with Jack. **April 26, 2011:** Theo walks
into Marisol PD with the jacket and Ray Ochoa takes his statement. The same week Lena's own part comes out (the host, the test,
the crying boy in the Serra corridor — it was Theo), and Lena learns Jack knew for a year. **The rupture (S4E21–E22)** — a
separation, never a breakup with anyone else in it (brief: no more other relationships), that holds all summer.

**S5 (Fall 2011):** consequences. The DA's decision (the grab was a rescue attempt; the flight is the problem; drug
possession; a misdemeanor plea and community service — the law shrugs, and the shrug is its own horror for Theo). The
press realizes Fr. Osei may have known; the seal on trial; Osei jailed for contempt. Rosa Calloway receives Communion. Jack and
Lena, after Wes's funeral, rebuild on the far side of all of it.

**Full run:** the case's after-life — Theo's film, Evan's prison teaching, Ray Ochoa's retirement, the cross at the
Point removed by the county in 2014 and replaced by a bench with a plaque that Theo pays for anonymously: *"Never was it
known."*

## 22. SEASON 1 — FALL 2009 (22 episodes, Aug 29 – Dec 18, 2009)

*Liturgical year B through Christ the King (Nov 22); Year C from the First Sunday of Advent (Nov 29). Classes begin Mon
Aug 31; Labor Day Sept 7; Thanksgiving break Nov 25–29; finals Dec 14–18.*

**E01 · "Lip Service"** · Sat Aug 29 – Sun Aug 30 · 22nd Sunday OT (Mark 7). Ted Kennedy's funeral Mass in Boston; the
Station Fire above La Cañada; Frank sees the Pacific. Move-in, Theo, the floor meeting; the Lighthouse party; the back
porch; Mass at St. Brendan's; the first duel; Hale in a diner booth; the stairwell call ("Wes"); sand on Theo's feet.

**E02 · "The Examined Life"** · Mon Aug 31 – Fri Sep 4 · St. Gregory the Great (Thu Sept 3; weekday Gospel Luke 5:1–11,
"Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man"); Ramadan; full moon Fri Sept 4. *(Re-planned after S1E01; full plan in
`outlines/s1e02.md`.)* Cold open: the first 3 a.m. fire alarm, the whole floor on the lawn; Theo meets Lena ("I like her.
She's mean"). Hale's PHIL 9H: "Prove to me you have a soul" — a four-move duel **against Hale**, Lena as rival and ally
(Ryle's ghost; 🔒 Phineas Gage; Lena vs. Jack on form vs. interior; the genetic debunking); Hale pairs Jack and Lena as
**designated antagonists** for the semester (weekly papers, annotated in each other's margins). New at the table: Caleb
Hargrove, Yusuf Noorzai. Margot meets Lena in PHIL 1 and says "useful idiots" aloud. Gloria hires Jack ("Four out of ten?
Hon, you're hired"); Rudy Salcedo; Rafi lends him La Flaca. Frank home ("How's the pelican?"); Traficant; the letter to
Danny (elided). Osei: "the box or the board" (fork). Daily Mass; Kevin's lunch (a smooth lie about Theo). Evan's Thursday
section — the driveway man. Lena names Wes to Jack's face; the second cigarette ("I'm going to need a container").
Facebook: In a Relationship; 🔒 Nora's candle; 🔒 Wes awake at 3:58 a.m. Laney's Pi Lam open house (fork: with Lena / with
Margot and Kevin). The full-moon beach; Lena teaches the Who Dat. Theo's 450SL and the pitch: "Full moon, Costigan. LA is
three hours. Get in the car." (`e2_la`). Becca invites Jack to the Sept 19 BBQ.

**E03 · "Labor"** · Sat Sep 5 – Mon Sep 7 (Labor Day) · 23rd Sunday OT (Is 35; **James 2:1-5**, the rich man with
the gold ring; Mark 7:31-37, *Ephphatha*). *(Re-planned after S1E02 for the played path — `e2_la=="broke"`; full plan in
`outlines/s1e03.md`.)* **Player note: Lena lighter and funnier — a breather after E02's ache, so the next ache (E04,
Nora's birthday) lands harder.** The episode is a comedy weekend with one knife, and the knife is Jack's, not Lena's.
Theo's nine a.m. ambush with a full tank turns into a **convoy** (the SL; Kevin's mother's Odyssey with Kevin, Margot,
Laney in the Mooney hoodie, and Lena, who "isn't going"); Jack can afford his share of gas (he tells them about the
Anchor — Lena's first she's heard of it). Fork: ride in the SL with Theo or the van with everyone. **Pea Soup Andersen's,
Buellton: the Reliquary tin** (an Altoids tin from the gift shop; the mints poured into Kevin's palm; Saturday's
cigarette sealed in; Sharpie on the lid). Malibu: Station Fire ash on the deck chairs ("Don't touch the deck chairs.
That's the mountains."); the fridge nobody may eat from; the Oscar in the powder room. Lena makes groceries and cooks
(a roux is a vow; Jack stirs while Wes calls on time and she laughs on the deck); **Jack pays Theo his pie** (peach,
Lena's mother's crust) and Theo asks whether God takes IOUs. Rock Band. Sunday: the 8 a.m. at Our Lady of Malibu — James 2
in a Malibu church — Lena coaching Laney through her first Mass in whispers; Theo outside with coffees ("a supporter, not
a member"); Nonna on the phone about First Friday. Fork: **the Getty Villa with Lena (and Margot, who out-Greeks her)**
or the pool with Theo, Laney and Kevin (Poppy on the first ring). **Richard Vance's six minutes** (Margot times him:
6:14): magnetic and awful; mistakes Jack at the sink for help and tips him a hundred. **The labor duel** on the deck that
night, Margot moderating: the just wage, the right of association (*Rerum Novarum*; *Caritas in Veritate* §25), the UAW,
the bailout, *Laborem Exercens* ("work is for man") — and Frank, laid off since June, said aloud to her for the first
time. **She wins it** (2–1). Monday, Labor Day, 7:12 a.m.: *"This is a prepaid call from — Danny — an inmate at Trumbull
Correctional Institution."* Theo in the kitchen; Danny funny and gentle and asking what the ocean looks like; Theo
handles it beautifully and keeps it. Then Lena on the beach stairs, the tin's first deposit, and a cold swim she dares
him into without knowing why he needed it. The drive home: Obama at the AFL-CIO picnic in Cincinnati on the radio;
Gina: dad's in the garage with the radio. Tag: Theo, in the dark: "What's he reading?"

**E04 · "Nativity"** · Tue Sep 8 – Sat Sep 12 · Nativity of Mary (Sept 8) — 🔒 Nora's birthday. *(Re-planned after S1E03
for the played path and the player's notes — the harder turn after the breather; ensemble setpieces as punctuation, not
every week; **a long Jack/Lena two-hander as the emotional centerpiece**. Full plan in `outlines/s1e04.md`.)* Row M empty
(PHIL 1, Hale on Epicurus); the 12:10 Nativity Mass (Osei on the genealogy: "God is not ashamed of his family"); "Happy

free night); **Hale drunk in the back booth, Housman, "Go home, Mr. Costigan"** (🔒). Priya's cupcake: Nora becomes a person.
Wednesday: Hale's clean jacket; Locke and Reid's brave officer; the paper swap ("(Costigan)"; his paper "That God Is the One
Who Pays"); **"You lie!"** in the 4th-floor lounge (a room scene, not a setpiece) — Margot's whiteboard debuts; Jack hears the

("Nobody yells at an empty room"); counting freight cars on the Delgado steps; "Thank you, Jack"; "Goodnight, Magdalena"
(gated). Friday 9/11: Theo drives Jack to Driftwood to ship the Waugh to Trumbull (the replacement Everyman, "Not on the tab";

**Wes calls at 2:04 a.m. Central from a party** — "He sounded happy." Lena's resolve 8 → 5 (4 at the song). No duel.

bluff bench, **a prepaid call from Trumbull with Lena beside him** — "Hi, Danny" (path) — cut off by the system mid-sentence:
"Tell Gina — ." Tag: the 2:10 freight on the Delgado steps; Lena texts a number. Lena's resolve 5 → 7.

**E06 · "Welcome"** · Fri Sep 18 – Sun Sep 20 (tag Sun ~11:50 p.m.) · 25th Sunday OT Year B (Wis 2:12, 17-20; Ps 54;

🔒 E07); **Margot reads Eph 5:22–24 and asks Kenzie whether she plans to submit**; Kenzie's v. 21/v. 25 answer is better than

twice.** The Anchor (Rudy: "You wrote him?" "He wrote back."). **Ocean Road, 1:31 a.m.: "License and registration."** — Ray
Ochoa's bit for his son; "Pop."; the bag he doesn't open (🔒); a bike light from his trunk; Rafi after: "Not bars, though."
**THE TWO-HANDER** (~4,300, Sun 1:52–3:55 a.m.; nobody else after the porch): the Pi Lam barn party (Laney carried upstairs by

"Why Marisol?" "Money." (medal 🔒) / "You know why I came" (🔒 the card); the Lagoon bench where people go to break up —

**Fork:** Sully's with Lena and Dale (2–0; "Next week, kid" paid) or Eid with Yusuf (Tariq calls from Helmand). **Sunday 9 p.m.
Mass:** Osei — "On the road they argued about who was the greatest. In the house He asked them what they'd been talking about,

**E08 · "The Little Way"** · Tue Sep 29 – Sun Oct 4 · Michaelmas (Tue; Jack's confirmation saint); St. Jerome (Wed); **St.

ten — Jack erasing the Hopkins for Trumbull; Lena with two baskets; awkward, painful, polite ("How's Becca?" "Great." "How's
Wes?" "Great." "Nine days."); **she erases *Show Lena* herself** ("Friends help."). Midnight is her feast: he gives her a used

laughs before she can stop it** ("Come up with a better answer before somebody else asks you, Youngstown. That is the worst thing
you can say about a person in this situation.") **and can't hide her relief; he sees it.** At two, Becca is praying for him (her
promise). They walk back guilty; at the Delgado elevator, ~4 a.m.: **"That was a terrible thing to be glad about."** Laney, 4:41:
she came in and went straight to her knees, "not asking. (asking)"; Theo: "Did it come clean?" **From the guilt:** Thursday Jack
ships the Hopkins and Hale's Housman, stands behind Lena at the UCen counter while she argues a jar of the Pacific into the mail

Jack in Youngstown: Frank recalled for the Cruze launch at Lordstown (the line restarts — a rare good thing; Researcher: keep to the public 2010 record); a scrapyard job and CYO coaching; Danny; Nonna's lucid and bad days; Carly Benedetto; holding Theo's
truth, and Theo funny on the phone at 3 a.m. and never saying why (now Jack knows why). Lena in New Orleans: the oil, the shrimp boats tied up, her uncle's despair; Luc and the Danziger indictments (July 2010). **The Fourth of July in New Orleans** —
Jack on the Greyhound, meeting the Broussards as Lena's boyfriend, officially; Tony and Jack fishing where you still can; Celeste and Jack in the kitchen. **Meanwhile, Theo on Glenwood Avenue for the Fourth anyway** (brief, "Theo in Youngstown, standing":
the default is the Fourth; when Jack's in New Orleans the Costigans may invite Theo regardless) — Frank's grill, Nonna's twenty, Gina's Flip camera, Danny's call, and Theo reporting it all to Jack in New Orleans at length (comic; warm; the parka in July
as a bit). **August: Lena in Youngstown** (the Assumption, Aug 15) — Nonna ("La ragazza!"), Frank's garage, separate rooms and the basement couch (comic and charged), and **Danny in the visiting room, in person**; Maria and Lena at the sink at last; the
family that was all the way out on Skye, all the way in on Lena. The well capped (July 15). **Living the liturgical year begins here, the 2010 way** (brief; S3+): Jack reads his way in — Weiser's *Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs* (1958), Maria
