### 23.5 S5 — Spring 2011 [old "Season 4"] (the best and worst season)
Together, with a secret between them. Super Bowl XLV party (Feb 6, 2011) as an ensemble setpiece (no longer the reveal). Restraint
harder; one extreme-path window only (§24.3). Nonna's funeral (if Lent). Margot's reporting closes in; Evan goes to the Calloways;
Kevin decides to testify. **S5E17 (~Sat Apr 9, 2011 — a year after the Vigil): "THE CONVERSATION"** (brief; player's design; Lena
initiates; a centerpiece two-hander — registry #85): late in the spring semester, so happy and so loved that she can't bear to find out too
late, **she asks for a conversation — only a conversation, she's scared enough of that, and he'd better not do anything else yet or she'll
tell his mother on him.** Jack is taken aback. Deep and wide-ranging: **the long-awaited Ephesians 5 / marital submission discussion**
(superseding the old Spring-2012 placement, old "S6E09" = S8E09; every brief requirement applies — Eph 5:21–33, mutual subjection, *Mulieris Dignitatem* §24, the Theology
of the Body audiences, *Casti Connubii*, headship as service vs. authority, both sides intelligent and personal and surprising, their families'
wounds — §24.5); **marriage** itself; **kids** (how many; always open to life; how to raise them); **contraception and NFP**; what each of them
wants to do with their life; **where** (New Orleans or Ohio — the argument that will outlive them). **Not perfect agreement by any stretch;
they agree on what matters.** Afterward **Jack just holds her** while she's relieved and still shaking. The comic Ephesians-avoidance bit pays
off here. 🔒 The knife the player feels and they don't: she asked for honesty about everything that matters, and he is carrying Theo's
secret — it lands in the rupture three weeks later. **Easter Sunday, Apr 24, 2011:** Theo goes to Mass with Jack. **Apr 26:** Theo surrenders. Lena's own part
comes out the same week (the host, the test, the crying boy — Julian learns it too); she learns Jack knew for a year; Hale's
forty-one seconds come out. **The rupture (E21–E22):** at the Point — the first time Lena goes to the wall — she gives him back the
tin. **(Re-planned after S1E13 for the brief's "both summers before marriage, they trade visits":** the rupture is a separation, not a
breakup with anyone else in it, and it does **not** cancel the summer: it holds through June and breaks in July — §23.6.)

### 23.6 S6 — Summer 2011 (5 episodes) [old "SU2"]: apart, then the visits (re-planned after S1E13)
No one else, for either of them (brief). **The brief binds both summers before marriage to traded visits**, so the rupture bends: **S6E01–E02
(June): apart.** Becca marries her Veritas missionary in Coeur d'Alene, at twenty (Jack invited; goes, or sends a gift — path). Jack in
Youngstown: **a come-and-see weekend at the Pontifical College Josephinum in Columbus** — the priesthood flirtation, once, and real, *during*
the separation (#79); Danny's judicial-release hearing set for the fall. **S6E03 (July): Lena comes to Youngstown anyway** — the visit planned a
year ago; she keeps her word ("I said I'd come. I don't break those."), sleeps in Gina's room, and the repair begins at the Glenwood table and in
Frank's garage, explicit about forgiveness and unfinished (high `rel.lena.trust`: the visit *is* the repair; low: it's stiff and polite and the
repair waits for August). The Cloyne Report (July 13) and Enda Kenny's speech (July 20) make the seal front-page news. **S6E05 (late August):
Jack's visit to New Orleans** — the Katrina anniversary weekend; Dupre Street; **Aug 29, 2011: Wes dies** (accidental overdose, §19 — reconsider
before writing); Luc's call to the house at 3 a.m.; **Lena wakes Jack on the den couch**, and he is already there.

### 23.7 S7 — Fall 2011 [old "Season 5"] (juniors; repair, restraint at its height, the proposal)
Wes's funeral (E01) in New Orleans — the hinge (Jack is already in the city). **Repair, deepened**, explicit about forgiveness: both confess what
they hid; **the no-contraception line (S7E03, default; brief — Lena initiates; scary for her to say; registry #87):** right after the night of the
funeral, the first night that truly tempts them (danger window #2), she says it — **they never get condoms or birth control; they're not making it
easier to sin, and not stacking sins on top of each other; if they ever give in, they give in with the full consequences — if they engage in the
marital act before they're married, they don't get to deny its fruit.** It is **not permission**, for either of them. She wants them to give each
other themselves fully for the first time as husband and wife, without any guilt in the way. (It raises the stakes of every later danger window: any
premarital crossing carries a real possibility of pregnancy, and the room honors that consequence if it comes.) **Jack tells Lena
the truth about Danny** (if he hasn't — at the latest here). **Restraint at its height** (grief, love, adulthood; the danger windows,
§24.3). The seal on trial: Osei subpoenaed; contempt; five nights in county jail; Margot vs. Jack, a war. Theo's plea. Barron's
*Catholicism* on PBS (from Oct 2011): Jack every week in the Newman lounge; Lena comes for Chartres and stays. Danny's judicial
release (Nov 2011, path). Rosa Calloway receives Communion (E21). Skye back with a film (a friend). **Thanksgiving 2011 in New
Orleans** (junior year flips the holidays): **Jack asks Tony's blessing** (Odile's ring, room's call — #78). **S7E22 (Gaudete week, Dec 2011):
the proposal — the player's design (brief, binding):** Jack gets Lena into an argument while they're walking; she's too invested to notice where
they're going; **they arrive at the Lighthouse back porch, where they first met**, and she realizes it just as **he goes down on one knee and
proposes as his closing argument** — an argument duel that ends in a proposal (#75). **Christmas 2011 in Youngstown** (S8E01; Danny home if
judicial release came in November).

**"The line he'll regret" — the echo with Lena** (brief; #91; provisional placement here, the restraint arc at its height): Jack tells her the sentence he said to Skye ("it's a no right now") — Lena understands how close he came, and how much he held.

### 23.8 S8 — Spring 2012 [old "Season 6"] (juniors; engaged)
**Pre-Cana** at St. Brendan's with Osei (out of jail; the bishop wants to move him; the students fight; he stays); Osei tells Jack the
story of the limp — Abena, Esi, the motorway — the week Jack is choosing vows. **Wedding planning:** where (Holy Rosary vs. St.
Brigid's vs. St. Brendan's — the families' fight; New Orleans wins, because it's the bride's parish and because Frank says, "Let me
see the Gulf"); money (Tony insists; Frank's pride); a senior-year apartment in Las Olas. **The NFP plan (S8E05; brief — Lena initiates, scary for her):** she wants to **use NFP to avoid pregnancy at least through the end of school**,
and after that to **try intentionally when he is** — discernment, timing and openness to life in play; Jack's honest answer is the room's to write;
they may not fully agree (registry #86). **S8E09 "Subject" (re-planned):** choosing their readings — they choose Ephesians 5 *because* of the S5
conversation (Osei: "You may also choose Tobit. Nobody has ever fought about Tobit." — "We already fought about this one, Father."); the payoff,
not the argument (§24.5). The HHS mandate (announced Jan 20, 2012) — Lena and Jack on the same side, Margot against, Kevin in the middle;
it rattles Lena's left lean. **Super Tuesday, Mar 6, 2012:** the Ohio primary — Jack's absentee ballot (Santorum, room's pick), Frank
on the phone; Lena's material on Gingrich's marriages. Hale's cirrhosis. Kevin and Andrés. A danger window (§24.3).

### 23.9 S9 — Summer 2012 [old "SU3"]: the wedding
The Fortnight for Freedom (June 21 – July 4); the Supreme Court upholds the ACA (June 28). **The rehearsal dinner (Fri July 20):**
Celeste's confession at last (she went back up the stairs; her mother was asleep; she kissed her and left her) — #16. **The wedding:
Sat July 21, 2012, Our Lady of the Holy Rosary, Esplanade Avenue** — the eve of Lena's twenty-first birthday and the feast of St. Mary
Magdalene; Osei witnessing (by delegation); Theo best man (or Danny, if Danny is home — both stand up); Laney maid of honor; Julian
playing; Margot "witness for the prosecution"; Kevin; Hale in a back pew ("And with thy spirit"); Becca, pregnant; Gloria's pie,
shipped; Kwame (🔒). The wedding night written with the full weight of the wait — or as what it is, if the line broke earlier (§24.3).
**Paul Ryan named Romney's running mate (Aug 11, 2012):** the subsidiarity-vs.-solidarity duel, as newlyweds, in a hot apartment.

### 23.10 S10 — Fall 2012 [old "Season 7"] (seniors; married, living together)
The Las Olas apartment; the first married fights (dishes; his cigarettes; her mother on the phone); married life as comedy and as
sacrament. **The Biden–Ryan VP debate watch party (Oct 11, 2012)** — two Catholics on abortion; the Fishbowl. **Election night (Nov
6):** **Jack votes Romney** and is the most hated man at the party (Margot, the campus, firmly Obama); **Lena reluctantly votes Obama**
after agonizing on the page (third party and a write-in both considered) — their first presidential election as a married couple.
**Jack tells Donna Kostelnik the truth; then the Mahoning County prosecutor** — with Lena beside him ("defense"). Danny's full term
ends January 2013 if he wasn't released.

### 23.11 S11 — Spring 2013 [old "Season 8"] (seniors; the last semester)
**Feb 11, 2013: Benedict XVI resigns** — it lands hard on Jack; Lena, surprised by how much it hurts him, sits up with him; they
argue at 3 a.m. about whether a pope may simply stop (Celestine V). **Mar 13: Francis** — Lena adores him on sight (the peripheries,
the bus, the shoes); Jack likes him and is uneasy, and the durable argument begins. Holy Thursday (Mar 28): Kevin in the back pew.
**Easter Vigil (Mar 30):** Laney received, Lena her sponsor; Theo confirmed, Jack his sponsor (path). Hale's last lecture as
commencement speaker. Danny home (the welcome-home Mass; Donna Kostelnik comes). **Graduation (May 2013).** (A child on the way is
possible — path and room; never announced before the Vigil.)

### 23.12 Adulthood (AD)
2013–: New Orleans first — Lena at Tulane Law, then the Orleans Public Defenders; Jack teaching theology at a Catholic high school
in the city (room's call; Jesuit, Wes's school, is the knife). Hale's death (2015; he asks for Osei). Children (Danny godfather to the
first; Margot godmother "as a hedge"; Kevin godfather to another). Then home: Lordstown closes (March 2019) and Theo's film; Frank's
last day; Jack at Cardinal Mooney and a volunteer at Trumbull; Lena at the Ohio Public Defender in Youngstown — the move a marriage-
scale argument the show takes seriously. *Laudato Si'* (June 2015): Lena's joy. Barron made auxiliary bishop of Los Angeles (2015). The
Francis argument, durable and affectionate and sometimes heated (real public events only). **Nov 8, 2016:** probably the last time
Jack votes Republican and the last time Lena votes Democrat — both mad at each other, madder at themselves; after, both politically
homeless. The Trump years are hard on Jack (immigration); Lena grows dissatisfied with Barron and Jack defends him (Winona-Rochester,
2022). **Dobbs (June 24, 2022):** joy for both, then ash. **May 8, 2025: Leo XIV** — complete agreement, joy and relief.

### 23.13 SUPERSEDED — the 22-episode Season 2 map (old §23.1–§23.2; kept for the record; replaced by the S2E01 re-map, 2026-10-23 — do NOT plan from it)
#### (old) 23.1 Winter break — the Youngstown Christmas (S2E01–E02; brief: follow Jack home; registry #64)
Lena is in New Orleans (the default); a visit is off the table — she is with Julian, and Jack is (secretly) going to be dating Skye
(availability windows). Long calls, a mailed gift, a Facebook message at midnight Mass. Skye over the break on the RAZR and the family
Dell (accelerated sequence, step 8: they've agreed to date in January); **the Costigans find her Facebook** (#84).

**S2E01 · "Midnight"** · Sat Dec 19 – Fri Dec 25, 2009 · Fourth Sunday of Advent (the Visitation, Luke 1:39–45); Christmas. The
Greyhound east (Theo offered the flight; Jack refused it — Thanksgiving's two tickets are already on the tab); the tin in his
pocket, counted at Flagstaff. **Sat Dec 19: the Saints' first loss (Dallas 24–17)** on a bus-station TV in Gallup — Lena's one-word
text; the same day **Tess's baby, Lucille, is born** (a photo; Lena will be godmother) and Benedict declares John Paul II and Pius XII
Venerable (Jack reads it on the RAZR; Lena: "Pius is going to be a whole thing."). Glenwood Avenue: Nonna home since Thanksgiving
and worse; Frank in the garage; Gina; Rosie. **Christmas Eve:** the Senate passes health care at 7 a.m. (Frank: "Merry Christmas.");
at 4 p.m. on the kitchen TV, Midnight Mass from St. Peter's — **a woman vaults the barrier and knocks Benedict down** (real: Dec 24,
2009; he is unhurt and celebrates the Mass) — Jack on his feet; Lena's text inside a minute: *Is he alright? Are you?* (she knows
what Benedict is to him); Midnight Mass at St. Brigid's (Fr. Dom Bruno); 12:58 a.m. Eastern, Lena's Facebook post from Holy Rosary;
**3:02 a.m. Eastern, Skye** (*merry christmas, ohio. describe the snow globe. be specific.* — they've been writing since Thanksgiving).
**Christmas week: Gina finds *Sweetwater* on the Dell** in four minutes — Nonna by rosary and dark Calabrese, Gina mortified and thrilled,
Maria and Frank worried about "that kind of girl," all of them asking about Lena; Danny, on the Christmas call, thinks it's hilarious (#84). Christmas Day: the
underwear bomber on the news; Danny's Christmas call (fifteen minutes; the system cuts him off mid-joke); **Lena's Christmas-night call from Dupre Street — the empty chair at Réveillon, and, for the first time, "My mama worked at Memorial." Nothing more** (moved from S1E18 by the player's E18 design round: Thanksgiving's call is lighter than Christmas's); Maria, at the sink, about the
girl on the computer: "Is she *Catholic*, at least?" (Idaho's end was told at Thanksgiving; Gina's "doing a shift" line moved to S1E18.)

**S2E02 · "Epiphany"** · Sat Dec 26, 2009 – Sun Jan 3, 2010 · Holy Family (Sun Dec 27); Mary, Mother of God (Fri Jan 1); Epiphany
(Sun Jan 3: the Magi "departed for their country by another way"). **Trumbull on Holy Family Sunday** (Maria, Gina, Jack; Frank in
the truck, then in): Danny (he heard about the crab girl at Thanksgiving, S1E18; what Gina told him on the Christmas call is fresher): "So. The TV one." — and he laughs till the officer looks over The Saints lose to Tampa in overtime (Dec 27) and at Carolina (Jan 3) —
Lena: "They're resting." **Carly Benedetto** at a YSU New Year's party (🔒 she knows; she asks after "Mikey's mom," and Jack goes
white; the elision holds). New Year's Eve: Skye on Facebook chat at midnight Pacific / 3 a.m. Ohio from the Dell in the basement;
**the Facebook album "Lucille's Baptism" — Julian at the Broussards' table** (he flew in for New Year's; Mémère calls him *le petit
violon*); Skye's window blinks. **Dec 28–30: Theo runs into Skye in LA** (a Christmas party in the hills) and is extremely odd, even for him; **Skye calls Jack** to
say so (the Dell, the basement, the furnace) — and the larger part of the call is **how Jack learns Theo has known her since they were eleven — the same
Meridian sets, practically siblings — and that Theo suspects them** (brief). Theo and Laney come back from the break well-prepared. **THE TWO-HANDER BY PHONE** (Sat Jan 2, ~2 hours, Dupre Street to the Glenwood Avenue basement, the
cordless dying twice): the baby; the font; Wes not at the baptism (🔒); "How's California?" (Lena, lightly; the only time she asks); Nonna; Danny; nothing said that
matters and everything heard; Lena: **"Come back, Youngstown."** Epiphany: home by another way. Theo's miles fly him back ("Not on the
tab."). Tag (Sun Jan 10, the Baptism of the Lord): the Anacapa lot, the dented Saab with a surfboard sticking out of the back seat — and a
cardboard sign in the windshield, in eyeliner: OFFICIALLY.

#### (old) 23.2 Season 2 — Spring 2010 (classes Mon Jan 11 – finals May 10–14)
*Title theme: "Do you also wish to go away?"* Liturgical Year C: Ordinary Time to Feb 16; Lent from Ash Wednesday (Feb 17);
Easter Apr 4; Pentecost May 23 (Ascension transferred to Sunday May 16 in California). **Two-handers** every other episode (E02,
E04, E06→E08, E10, E12, E14, E15, E16, E18, E20, E22; after E15 a "two-hander" is simply the couple's long scene). **Ensemble
setpieces:** E03 (Sully's), **E07–E10 (New Orleans)**, E13 (the Forum), **E17 (Floatopia — the alliance reveal)**, E22 (the last
night). Hale's spring seminar (PHIL 109H, "The Novel as Moral Argument") keeps them designated antagonists.

**S2E03 · "Cana"** · Mon Jan 11 – Sun Jan 17 · Second Sunday OT C (John 2:1–11, the wedding at Cana — "They have no wine"). Spring
classes; Theo rushes Sigma Rho (Brooks his big). **Haiti (Tue Jan 12):** Lena runs the Newman CRS collection like a field hospital;
Jack works the table beside Becca (friends now, awkward and kind); **Skye works the table beside him in a borrowed Newman apron** and raises
more money than anybody, in voices — not for the faith — **the "whole thing" she promised: Jack and Skye are officially dating** (accelerated
sequence, step 9). **Laney's first sighting, verbatim (#89): "Oh my God, he found a California you. Excuse me, while I go be a bitch on your
behalf."** — and she goes and does it; Lena already knows — **she found out Sunday night from the Facebook status** ("In a Relationship with Skye Callender," posted
under the OFFICIALLY tag; off Jack's screen): she had privately decided over Christmas to end it with Julian; she veered between devastated, furious and
sick; **Laney physically took the laptop away**, then went through the pictures herself and got mad too (brief; hurt chain link 3 — Lena does not leave
Julian). Jack sees only pieces (Laney's cold fury, Lena's sudden formality); the full story waits for New Orleans. At the table Lena hates that Laney's
right. **Overheard fragments** (S2E03–E06, planted so they click in S2E10): "…she'd *decided*, Theo…" / "…over Christmas…" / "…the laptop's in my
closet…" / "…don't you dare tell him…" — they stop when he walks in; Jack never infers the meaning early. Saturday dawn, the Point break (she teaches him to surf; he is bad at it; 🔒 from the water she points out "somebody leaves
flowers up there every week"). Laney, rude on contact; privately curious. Jack: "I've seen your work, Price." (#69). Theo, at last, out loud:
"She's the best actress I know, Costigan. Never ask her if she's acting." (from here he feeds Laney as usual). **Sat Jan 16, Sully's: the Saints 45–14 over Arizona** (the ensemble setpiece): Lena with
Julian, Jack with Skye; **Lena hates every minute** and is perfect to Skye, which is worse; she tells Laney to be nice to everyone but
Skye. Jack checks the closet: **the black duffel is gone** (#2).

**S2E04 · "Overtime"** · Mon Jan 18 – Sun Jan 24 · MLK Day; Scott Brown wins Massachusetts (Tue Jan 19); Citizens United (Thu Jan
21); the March for Life (Fri Jan 22) and the West Coast Walk for Life in San Francisco (Sat Jan 23: the Newman van; both of them;
not Skye, not Julian). **Jack tells Theo to stop on Julian** — it's turning mean, and it isn't going to work out, and they all know
it but Julian (brief). **Sun Jan 24: the NFC Championship — Saints 31–28 over the Vikings in overtime** (Hartley's kick); the
Fishbowl; Lena on a table; New Orleans is going to its first Super Bowl. **THE TWO-HANDER** (after; the Delgado steps → the Anchor →
the 2:10 freight): giddy, then quiet; **Lena invites everyone to New Orleans** — the Super Bowl at Dupre Street, then stay for Mardi
Gras ("Mama says bring the redhead. Daddy says bring the Ohio boy, he needs us."); Theo has the tickets bought before she finishes;
Jack can't afford it and can't miss a week — and says yes anyway (fork: how; the cost is real — Gloria, Hale, the deposit; #33).

**S2E05 · "Love Is Patient"** · Mon Jan 25 – Sun Jan 31 · the iPad (Wed Jan 27); the State of the Union (Wed Jan 27); Pi Lam's
winter formal (Sat Jan 30: Brooks; Laney leaves early in Theo's car); Fourth Sunday OT C (1 Cor 13, "Love is patient, love is
kind" — Peter and Kenzie's slide, read at Mass the Sunday after). **Proxy fight #1** (§24.6): Hale's seminar on Greene's *The End of
the Affair* — vicious; the real reason never spoken; Laney, to Theo: "Sugar, that was not about a *book*." Kevin and Clare Dominguez
(the sad, sincere attempt, S2E04–E13; she deserved better and knew it within a month). Skye at the 9 p.m. Mass, "like a sound bath," and
means it kindly; Lena, three rows ahead, does not turn around.

**S2E06 · "The Darkroom"** · Mon Feb 1 – Thu Feb 4 · Candlemas (Tue Feb 2; Danny turns 23 — his letter). **Skye's near-miss**
(the Del Playa house — Sol's darkroom under the red safelight, or her room; she tries, in earnest; she stops it, or he does — resolve sets *how*, never *whether*; a confession owed).
Julian tells Lena he won't come to New Orleans: **"It's your city. I'd be a tourist in it. Go."** (Jack hears it from Laney; 🔒
alliance intelligence.) Skye leaves for Vancouver to shoot a pilot ("Come to Vancouver."). The two-hander shifts to E08.

**S2E07 · "Who Dat"** · Fri Feb 5 – Sun Feb 7 · Fifth Sunday OT C (Luke 5:1–11 — "Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man,"
E02's weekday Gospel come round again). Fly to New Orleans (Theo's tickets; Jack's paid back in Anchor singles over a year — #54).
**Dupre Street:** the raised shotgun, the waterline on the shed; Tony, Celeste, Luc, Remy, Tess and baby Lucille, the twins,
Mémère; Celeste adopts Laney on sight; Tony takes Jack's measure with boiled crawfish (early season) and a Sazerac. **Sat Feb 6:
Mitch Landrieu is elected mayor outright** — the kitchen table: Tony, Luc, Lena, Jack; the race note under it, and Jack hears it
(#47). **Sun Feb 7: Super Bowl XLIV** — the watch party at Dupre Street; the onside kick to open the second half; Porter's
pick-six; **Saints 31, Colts 17**; the city erupts — Mid-City, then the Quarter, strangers kissing strangers, Tony crying on a
stranger's car; it ends on Esplanade at 4 a.m. with Lena asleep against Jack on the neutral ground and Laney asleep against
Lena.

**S2E08 · "Lombardi Gras"** · Mon Feb 8 – Thu Feb 11 · The week the city can't go back to work; **the victory parade, Tue Feb 9**
(cold; enormous). Lena's city; the market on Banks Street; **Wes at the parade** — sober-ish, kind, broken; "See you, Ohio," paid
back on the neutral ground; Josie reports the ring went back to Mémère (🔒). Jack misses classes and pays (Gloria by phone; Hale's
email: "Go. Write me something about it. Nothing about football."). **THE TWO-HANDER** (Wed night): Lena shows Jack her city at
night — Bayou St. John, the waterline, St. Louis No. 3 and Grandmère's tomb, still white from All Saints; the medal; they talk about
everything except Julian and Skye, and it is the loudest thing either of them has ever not said.

**S2E09 · "Bacchus"** · Fri Feb 12 – Mon Feb 15 (Presidents' Day) · The Vancouver Olympics open (Fri); Endymion (Sat); **Bacchus
(Sun Feb 14) — Drew Brees reigns** [verify]; Valentine's Day; **Laney's 19th birthday** (Celeste's cake; Tony's toast; Laney cries
at a family table for the first time since Kaylee); Sixth Sunday OT C (Luke 6, the Beatitudes and the woes — "Woe to you who laugh
now"). Kevin and Margot fly in (Margot "for the *Tide*'s anthropology": "a matriarchy disguised as a parade"). **Tết** — the Year of
the Tiger, Feb 14, and Kevin's birthday on the 15th: he takes them to **Mary Queen of Vietnam in New Orleans East** (red envelopes;
Bà Nội on the phone from San Jose; 🔒 Kevin's face at a family table that isn't his). **Proxy fight #2** (§24.6) that night, in the
Broussards' kitchen, on Valentine's Day, with Skye in Vancouver and Julian in Oakland — ostensibly the city (the police; Danziger; Luc
in the room): Laney: "Sugar, that was not about the police." **Lundi Gras (Mon), the levee at Spanish Plaza, Rex arriving by
river:** Wes, to Jack only — **"Don't wait on nobody, podna. I waited on God four years."**

**S2E10 · "Fat Tuesday"** · Tue Feb 16 – Wed Feb 17 · Zulu at dawn (Laney catches a coconut); Rex; the Marigny walking krewes;
the Broussards in costume. **THE TWO-HANDER — the honesty** (the brief's design; re-plan step 7): at midnight, when the mounted
police sweep Bourbon Street and it becomes Lent — **after four days of being all over each other without noticing** (brief, "physical
register": his arm around her at the watch party, her arms around his waist on a parade route, her head on his shoulder in the car, hands
found in a crowd; Theo, Laney, Margot and Kevin notice everything) — they come **within a hair's breadth of kissing**, stop, and **without
letting go of each other** they are **completely honest about what they want** — Jack tells her about the ring (Wes showed it to him on the
beach in October; he kept it; it is why he stayed away) and **the real reason he didn't come for her after Wes (brief, binding): he
wouldn't swoop in while she was hurting from something that big, and he didn't think he'd be able to keep himself from doing it if he were
single too — Becca was a guardrail against himself** (the E13 dawn's last, private reason — "Becca is the fence he can see" — said aloud at
last); he owns Skye and his own hurt that she didn't wait; **the hurt chain said aloud
(#81)** — on All Souls he was waiting *for* her (his `e13_dawn` answer quoted back: "I said I'd wait." / "I thought you'd chosen her."),
she went to Julian because she thought he had, he went to Skye because she didn't wait; she tells him she stayed with Julian because she was
so angry about Skye; and they agree they are **not starting this with either of them as "the other"
something in someone else's story** — "When nobody has to be the other anything" (her roof line, kept); the proxy war gets named and
laughed at, painfully. **Lena is the one who finally pulls away.** **No kiss** (that's the point; restraint is the fire). **The crew (brief):
Jack, Lena, Theo, Laney, Margot, Kevin — the dates (Skye, Julian) do not come.** **Ash Wednesday at Holy Rosary, hungover:** "Remember that you are dust"; ashes from the pastor who
baptized her; the flight home.

**S2E11 · "Ashes"** · Thu Feb 18 – Sun Feb 28 · First Sunday of Lent (Feb 21; Luke 4, the desert); Second Sunday (Feb 28, the
Transfiguration). **Both free within a week**, each ending their own story honestly: **Lena ends it with Julian** (Sun Feb 21: "You've
never once told me I was wrong.") and **Jack ends it with Skye** (Tue Feb 23, the Del Playa porch, back from Vancouver: "I just thought I'd be better than her at something.
Explain to me, slowly, why it took you a parade."). **Fri Feb 26, the east stairs: Jack asks. Lena says "No." with a perfectly straight face** — Theo and
Laney, on the landing above, hear only that and flee to 412 to hold a wake with the champagne they bought (false dawn #3,
inverted) — **then she cracks up**, and tells him to **do it properly**: "Ask me to dinner, Costigan. Then ask me again. Then ask
me." She announces she has given up kissing for Lent ("in principle"). (The Chile-quake call is retired with Sol's old role.)

**S2E12 · "Properly"** · Mon Mar 1 – Sun Mar 7 · Third Sunday of Lent (Luke 13, the fig tree given one more year). **Date #1** (Sat
Mar 6), Jack's plan, alone ("Don't." — to Laney, before she opens her mouth; #69); nothing he did with Becca or Skye (room's call:
the Anchor after close, Gloria's last pie and Rudy's kitchen; or the Mission in San Luis Obispo and a Lenten fish fry). Margot starts
the anniversary feature for the *Tide* (#12). Two-hander.

**S2E13 · "The Forum"** · Mon Mar 8 – Sun Mar 14 · Laetare Sunday (Luke 15, the prodigal son; rose vestments again). **Lena debates
Hale at the Marisol Forum and wins** (the ensemble setpiece; Caleb cracks — #41; Hale loves her more for it). Kevin and Clare end.
Jack's money (the deposit; #33).

**S2E14 · "St. Joseph"** · Mon Mar 15 – Sun Mar 21 · **Fri Mar 19, St. Joseph — Jack's 19th birthday: date #2, hers** — a St.
Joseph's altar in the Delgado kitchen (New Orleans: fava beans, breads shaped like tools and crosses, the lucky bean for his
wallet); a solemnity, so meat on a Lenten Friday ("That's how much I like you, Costigan."). **Sun Mar 21:** the House passes health
care after the Stupak executive-order deal — both furious, for different reasons (Lena betrayed by her party; Jack: "Told you.");
the Gospel that morning is the woman caught in adultery ("Neither do I condemn you"). Two-hander.

**S2E15 · "Vigil"** · Mon Mar 22 – Sun Apr 4 · the health-care law signed (Tue Mar 23); **date #3** (Thu Mar 25, the Annunciation);
Palm Sunday (Mar 28); NUMMI's last car (Thu Apr 1 — Holy Thursday; Yusuf's father; #42); Good Friday; **the Easter Vigil (Sat Apr 3)**:
the new fire in the courtyard brazier, the Exsultet, Laney at her first Vigil; after, by the fire: "Now ask me." — **he asks properly;
she says yes; the first kiss** (Lent is over). Easter morning: *Magdalena Broussard is in a relationship with Jack Costigan* — Laney's
scream audible from Pi Lam. **Official before summer** (re-plan step 7).

**S2E16 · "Divine Mercy"** · Mon Apr 5 – Sun Apr 11 · Second Sunday of Easter (Thomas). The first week as a couple — argument and

## 24. THE ROMANCE ROADMAP — restraint is the fire

*(Re-planned after S1E11 for the player's MAJOR RE-PLAN, exact sequence and long-range timeline. Superseded plans — the S3E22
first kiss, Gideon, the S4E03 reveal, Andrew, the S7E09 Ephesians, the AD wedding — are retired; see the revision log.)*

### 24.1 Shape
- **S1 (Fall 2009):** rivals → friends → the two people who stay. She's taken; he's honorable; the heat is all proximity and
  argument. Restraint scenes: E10 (the Brick at dawn), **E19** (the laundry room on St. Nicholas night — *her* fidelity, Jack free; moved from E20 by the S1E19 pass). **No kiss.** The
  timing tragedy runs twice, mirrored: **Wes ends it (E13) and Becca is made official two days later (E14)** — Jack won't be the rebound (his decision; Lena reads it as him
choosing Becca — the hurt chain);
  then **Lena is with Julian (E15) by the time Jack is free (E15–E16)**. **Julian's song (E20) sends Jack into Skye until the finale.** Finale (E22): the empty-campus walk —
  every place from the semester; both nearly say it (brief, E19–E22 design round). Every reason for hope; a real sting.
- **Winter break and S2, January–February 2010: apart in other arms.** Jack + Skye (the fire without the faith; the darkroom
  near-miss); Lena + Julian (faith-respect without fire — and kept, empty, out of fury at Skye: she does exactly what Jack did with
  Becca). Jealousy as POV, both ways. **Proxy fights #1 (S2E09 — Greene, and the Facebook-status grievance) and #2 (S2E12 — the drive, the worst).** New Orleans (S2E12–E17) breaks it open. *(S2 numbers re-mapped by the S2E01 pass — §23.)*
- **S2, February–May 2010: together.** The honesty without letting go, Mardi Gras night (S2E16); both free within a week (S2E18); "No." — she
  cracks up — "Do it properly." (S2E19); three Lenten dates — **the first kiss at the end of date #1, and Lena kisses him (S2E21; brief —
  supersedes the Easter Vigil kiss and "given up kissing for Lent")**; **official at the Easter Vigil (S2E24)** — a yes without an asterisk; the honeymoon weeks;
  the alliance reveal (S2E26); the proxy fights named and the fear answered (S2E28); and, on the last night, the first secret between them — Theo's (S2E30).
- **SU1:** long distance as a couple; each family meets the other's beloved.
- **S3 (sophomore fall):** a couple; restraint becomes a thing they choose out loud; "I love you" (default Thanksgiving in
  Youngstown — holidays alternate, brief); the test told (Maria's kitchen, 1 a.m.); Christmas in New Orleans (S4E01–E02); Jack's held secret.
- **S4 (sophomore spring):** the best and worst season; **"the conversation" (E17; Lena initiates; Ephesians 5, marriage, kids, NFP,
  where — brief)**; then the rupture (E21–E22).
- **SU2:** apart in June (the Josephinum); **the traded visits** — Lena in Youngstown in July (the repair begins), Jack in New Orleans in
  late August (Wes's death).
- **S5 (junior fall):** the funeral; repair, deepened; **the no-contraception line (E03; Lena)**; restraint at its height (the danger windows);
  Thanksgiving in New Orleans (Tony's blessing); **the proposal (E22, the Lighthouse back porch, a duel that ends on one knee)**.
- **S6 (junior spring):** engaged; Christmas in Youngstown (E01); Pre-Cana; **the NFP plan (E05; Lena)**; the readings — Ephesians 5 chosen
  (E09); wedding planning.
- **SU3:** **the wedding (July 21, 2012)**.
- **S7–S8 (senior year):** married, living together; the election; the popes; graduation.
- **AD:** marriage — the show does not end at the wedding; married love is the hardest saying.
- **After they're together (brief, "the show's shift"; folded in after S1E13):** from S2E15 the plot turns from will-they/won't-they to
  **the mystery beats**, **the intrusions of ordinary relationship life, college and family**, **the effects of real-world events**, and **the
  growth of their relationship** — *them learning each other in the world*. Restraint, the dangerous night, the proposal and the wedding remain
  the relationship spine across sophomore and junior years; every season plan from S3 on should be checked against this shift.
- **S1 cadence (player's standing rule after S1E04):** an **extended Jack/Lena two-hander roughly every other episode** — E04 (the
  harbor), E06 (the long way home), *E07 (the roof at dawn, ~1,800)*, E08 (the Thérèse night — the player's design), E10 (the Brick →
  the Ferrer Tower → dawn — the player's design), **E12** (Halloween: the hour that happens twice), **E13** (the stairwell till dawn —
  shifted up by one: Wes's end), **E14** (the postcards; the Thanksgiving invitation), **E16** (the night Becca ends — "Ask me again in a week," returned; accelerated after S1E13), *E18 — none* (the player's E18 design round: in touch, not as deeply as Christmas;
  the Thanksgiving call is a short phone scene — shifted by one), **E19** (the St. Nicholas night — restraint #2, her fidelity; moved from E20 by the S1E19 pass), *E20–E21 — none* (the withdrawal into Skye after Julian's song, by the player's design), **E22** (the empty-campus walk).
  **Ensemble setpieces as punctuation:** E03 (convoy), E05 (Sully's), E08 (the Blessing), E09 (the Wes weekend), E11 (Big Sur), **E12
  (Halloween)**, **E14 (Hale's dinner)**, **E17/E18 (the airport; Youngstown)** (E17 also carries the Skye meeting at the Halloran house — an extended set piece per the brief, but a two-person one, not an ensemble setpiece), **E21 (the Newman Christmas party** — moved from E22 by the brief's E19–E22 design round). Lena central every
  week regardless.
- **The S1 rhythm after E08 (player's design):** every big near is followed by a retreat — scrupulous, polite, painful — that fails
  faster each time, into *guilty fun*: their best hours together cost Becca and Wes something neither is told. Jack's guilt is the S1
  engine; keep it alive whenever Becca is in a scene (her goodness is the knife, never her foolishness). **Re-planned after S1E12 (the hurt chain,
  clarified):** there is **no retreat after E13 and no distance** — Jack and Lena stay as close as ever and keep getting closer and more
  honest; what keeps them apart is the unspoken hurt each one's relationship choices cause the other (Jack's wait read as choosing Becca →
  Julian; Lena not waiting → Skye; Skye → Lena's fury and Julian kept), never said aloud until New Orleans (S2E10).
- **After S1E10 (player's reading, binding):** the E10 dawn put expiration dates on both relationships, and **Jack pushes through anyway
  because of the ring**. From E11 the retreat is **deliberate** — Jack's (for a ring he can't mention), joined after "Magdalena" by
  Lena's own — and the player *practices* it. It still never takes for long (E11: the porch at 3 a.m. → the comeback that afternoon),
  but both keep their people in deed. The pattern reads: **they can behave; they can't stop.** It holds in deed until the ring itself
  ends Wes (E13); after that Jack's reason for staying with Becca is no longer the ring but **the wait** (brief, "Why Jack stays with Becca";
  S1E13): he won't be the rebound or the man at the door; he won't make Becca the girl he left the minute someone else was free, or Lena
  the reason; he'll end it honestly *in due course* — and "due course" lasts exactly as long as it takes him to imagine Becca in his
  mother's kitchen (E18). Admirable and wrong at once: by then Lena, who read the wait as a choice, is Julian's.

### 24.3 The dangerous nights (only possible when `resolve.jack<=3 && resolve.lena<=3`)
Re-planned for the long-range timeline: **junior year is the height** (brief); sophomore year is restraint *becoming* a thing.
1. **S4E12** (Nonna's funeral, Youngstown, the Costigan basement, after the wake's whiskey). Lena written at 4: **default not
   reachable** — only if Jack's resolve has cratered *and* the writers drop Lena's in-episode.
2. **S5E02** (the night after Wes's funeral, New Orleans; grief and reconciliation in the same forty-eight hours). Lena at 3.
3. **S5E19** (Thanksgiving 2011, Dupre Street, the night Tony gives his blessing). Lena at 3–4.
4. **S6E12** (engaged; spring break; the apartment they've signed for). Lena at 3. The likeliest.
5. **SU3** (the week before the wedding). Lena at 4.
**Hard rule (brief):** every dangerous night is between Jack and Lena. With anyone else (Becca, Skye, anyone) the ceiling is the
near-miss, regardless of resolve (§24.8). If it happens: frank, literary, specific, tender and frightening; then the morning, the
guilt, the confession lines at St. Brendan's on Saturday at 3:30 (both, separately, neither knowing), the rupture and the repair —
as an engaged couple, Pre-Cana in a week. It never destroys them (brief: giving in brings serious guilt, rupture and repair). It
changes them. If it never happens, the wedding night (SU3) is written with the full weight of the wait, and the show is honest that
waiting had costs too.

### 24.4 How the meters bend the route (never break endgame)
- **Endgame is fixed:** they marry (SU3, 2012). What the player shapes is *how*, *at what cost*, and *who they are when they get
  there*.
- **High `rel.lena.trust`** shortens the S4 rupture (the July visit to Youngstown *is* the repair; S5 deepens it; the proposal may come at
  Thanksgiving). **Low trust** lengthens it: July is stiff and polite, the repair waits for New Orleans in August and runs to S5's midseason, and the
  proposal slides to the Christmas break (S6E01) — the wedding date holds. **Both summer visits happen on every path** (brief).
- **High `rel.lena.heat` with low `rel.lena.trust`**: the relationship becomes about the line, not the person; S5–S6 run feverish;
  the windows open wider.
- **High `rel.lena.friction`**: more duels, sharper; Lena wins more. Friction is not bad — some friction is how they love.
- **`soul.grace`** governs whether Jack goes to confession after a fall, and how fast; **`soul.honesty`** governs when he tells Lena
  the truth about Theo (high honesty → he tells her before Theo surrenders and loses her anyway, but the repair is faster) *and* about
  Danny (from S3 on a high-honesty path; S5 at the latest); **`soul.restraint`** governs the danger windows and how close Skye gets.
- **Lena's other relationships** (Wes to S1E13; Julian S1E15–S2E11) run regardless of the player; Jack's choices color them (a
  jealous Jack makes Julian's arc sadder; a generous Jack becomes Julian's friend, and Julian's ending is cleaner).
- **Jack's other relationships:** **Becca** (S1E06–E16, accelerated; fixed in shape — the player shapes how warm, how honest and how it ends,
  not whether); **Skye** (met S1E16; the Starlite S1E17; the secret December S1E19–E22 — mild by the directive; dating S2E03–S2E11; the player can keep December at
  flirtation and a kiss — then January is lonelier and Lena's fury has less to feed on — but she arrives and the pull is real). Neither ever goes past the near-miss. **After S2E11, no other relationships for
  either of them** (brief).

### 24.5 The Ephesians 5 conversation (reserved; brief directive)
- **When (re-planned after S1E13 — the player's correction, binding):** **S4E17, "the conversation"** — late in the spring semester of
  sophomore year (~Apr 9, 2011), about a year after the Easter Vigil; **Lena initiates** (the brief's design: §23.5, #85). It is part of a wider
  conversation — marriage, kids, contraception and NFP, what they want to do, where — and can play as a full duel inside it. **Not perfect
  agreement; they agree on what matters; afterward Jack just holds her.** The old S6E09 "Subject" placement is superseded: in S6, at Pre-Cana,
  they *choose* Ephesians 5:2a, 21–33 as their second reading (Osei: "You may also choose Tobit. Nobody has ever fought about Tobit." — "We already
  fought about this one, Father.").
- **Until then, the running bit (brief, "What's working"):** they visibly, comically keep avoiding it — the chastity talk (S1E06, "Not
  tonight"), the Ferrer stairs (S1E10), Peter and Kenzie's wedding (S3E17), the first week of April 2011 ("Not until I say so, Costigan") — and it pays off in
  the conversation itself (S4E17), where she brings it up first.
- **Seeds:** S1E06 Margot reads Eph 5:22–24 at the chastity talk Q&A; the Sunday before the pilot (Aug 23, 2009) had Eph 5:21–32 as
  the second reading, so both heard it at home the week they left — a callback either can spring; S3E17 the wedding reading.
- **Texts:** Eph 5:21–33 ("Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ"; "Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the
  church and gave himself up for her"); *Mulieris Dignitatem* §24 (mutual subjection); John Paul II's Theology of the Body audiences on
  Ephesians 5 (1982); *Casti Connubii* (1930); headship as service and sacrifice vs. as authority.
- **What each of them hears (don't assume sides):** 🔒 Jack's father exercised headship once that mattered — he decided, alone, that
  Danny would carry Jack's cross (and by S6 Lena knows it). Jack may argue against authority-headship from inside that wound, or defend
  it as the terrible cost of being the one who decides. 🔒 Lena's mother followed orders onto a boat and left her own mother upstairs (she
  will hear the whole of it four months later, at the rehearsal dinner); at home Tony's loud headship is warm theater and Celeste runs
  everything in a whisper. Lena may argue mutual subjection as the only safe kind, or argue that she wants a man who will carry a
  decision so she never has to be the woman on the stairs. Both intelligent, personal, surprising. Margot's critique is setup only; the
  conversation is theirs.

### 24.6 The proxy fights (reserved; brief)
The organizer is dropped, so the fights now live in **Jack's magnetic-girl period** (official S2E03–S2E11; Lena learns of Skye only in January — the December was secret): Lena is
infuriated by Skye and can't say so (she is with Julian; she went to Julian first; she said "not now" on the roof). A **serious fight that is 100% about
the other person being with someone else, and neither can say it.** Vicious, specific, personal; the subtext obvious to the player and
to Theo, Laney and Margot (who exchange looks and say nothing — alliance discipline); the real reason **never spoken** by either
during the period. Play as argument duels where *winning the stated argument is the wrong thing to win* (a Press/Personal win costs
trust and raises friction; a Concede is the only move that helps, and it doesn't feel like it).
1. **S2E08 (Wed Jan 27, 2010; Hale's PHIL 109H session moved to his bungalow; the State of the Union on his television — `outlines/s2e08.md` rev. 1 supersedes the details below: Lena prosecutes Sarah's silence, Jack defends it; the status line spoken; "She let him think it was a man"):** ostensibly Greene's *The End of the Affair*
   (literature as moral test: is Sarah's sanctity real or a writer's alibi for adultery?) — Lena savages the book, Jack defends it; it
   turns into how he's "changing" (the 9 p.m. Mass because he was in the water at dawn — "Since when do you go to the *late* one,
   Costigan?") and whether she's dating a man who agrees with her because she can't stand to lose. Laney: "Sugar, that was not about a
   *book*." Margot: "Well."
2. **(Superseded as #2 by §23.2 — proxy fight #2 is the drive, S2E12; this kitchen version may survive as a NOLA skirmish, room's call.) (Sun Feb 14, 2010 — Valentine's, Bacchus, Laney's birthday; the Broussards' kitchen):** ostensibly the city — the police
   (Danziger; Luc in the room), the Super Bowl as bread and circuses, whether Jack gets to love a place he's known for a week. He calls
   her "a tourist in the class war" in her own kitchen; she calls him "a company man for the company that laid off his father." Frank is
   used as a weapon. Both say the cruelest true thing they know. Laney: "Sugar, that was not about the police."
**The closest it comes (brief; Lena's voice, not verbatim — in fight #1 by default, #2 if the room prefers):** in the middle of the larger fight about
something else, Lena yells some version of **"If we're such *good friends*, how come I had to find out about your girlfriend from a Facebook status, when
we talked every single day for weeks leading up to it?"** — the grievance, never the reason. **Jack has no good answer** (telling her would have meant
saying why it mattered). The fight veers back to its ostensible subject; neither names the real one.
**Rehearsal (S1E10 — not a proxy fight; there was no magnetic partner yet):** the duel `cor` ("On the Heart") at 4 a.m. on the Brick's
eighth floor — the muscle these fights use.
**Payoff:** **S2E19**, once they're together, one of them finally names what the fights were (default Lena: "It was never Greene. It was
never the police."); path may hand the line to Jack. **And for the rest of their lives Lena brings Skye up as a running joke — the
cheapest fallback argument she owns** (brief; #80).

### 24.7 The secret alliance and its reveal (brief)
Theo and Laney, mirrored, from S1E07: **Laney** openly rude to all Jack's girls (Becca; Skye — whom she privately likes), privately
feeding Theo; Lena tells her to be nice to all but Skye; **Theo** polite to Jack's girls, privately Team Lena; **Theo** openly rude to
Lena's man after Wes (Julian), Jack mostly letting him and then stopping him (S2E04); **Laney** polite to Julian, privately Team Jack.
**Kevin** objects every season; **Margot** likes Julian. Their maneuvering is visible (seating charts, a borrowed car that won't start,
a party invitation that reaches only one of them, a "lost" phone, a reservation under COSTIGAN) and **never acknowledged aloud**.
**Reveal: S2E17 "Floatopia"** (Sat Apr 17, 2010; the first ensemble setpiece after they're official at the Easter Vigil): champagne on a
raft, the toast, and: "We know." / "Everyone knows." / "People outside of California know." / "It was obvious after five minutes."
(player's lines; keep them verbatim).
**The false dawns (brief running bit; registry #68).** Every time Jack or Lena gets out of a relationship, Theo and Laney are absolutely
pumped — and then deeply bummed. It escalates: **#1 S1E13–E14** (Wes ends it; Martinelli's; then Becca is official — the Martinelli's
goes into a ficus), **#2 S1E15–E16** (Becca ends before Thanksgiving — S1E15; a table for two at the Harbor Inn under COSTIGAN; dead Friday with Julian's soup), **#3 S2E11,
inverted** (they hear only the "No." and hold a wake with the real champagne — and then she cracks up). Paid off at S2E17, when the
champagne is finally for something.
**Never ask Laney for girl advice (registry #69).** S1E09 the poem and the knee; callbacks E16 ("No."), S2E03 ("I've seen your work,
Price"), S2E12 ("Don't."); Laney confirms the sabotage at the reveal: "The knee was *art*, sugar."
**Overtime (E09):** as before — the flat, the SL, "bedbugs," the seating chart, the Madonna Inn, the Newlywed Game, the tin. With **Wes**
neither of them was rude; Theo liked him, which made it worse.

### 24.9 Availability windows (brief structural rule; registry #70)
Whenever Jack or Lena leaves a relationship while the other is free, they would realistically just get together; neither could start
something new with someone else while the other is openly available. So **every breakup with a "nice" partner coincides with a
concrete reason they don't get together right then.** **The magnetic period is the exception:** while Jack is with Skye, Lena can be
genuinely angry at him, and the anger (plus the proxy fights) keeps her in the empty Julian relationship.

| Jack & Lena | S4E21–E22 (the rupture) | — | the lie (she learns Jack knew for a year) | — |

Every future relationship, in any season, gets a row here before it is written. (After S2E11 there are none — brief.)

# PART IV — THE WORLD

## 25. California State University at Marisol

**Where.** A fictional town of 38,000 (plus 24,000 students) on California's Central Coast, on a marine terrace where the
coast bends west, roughly between San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara. Highway 1 / US-101 runs inland of town; the Amtrak
Pacific Surfliner and the Coast Starlight run along the bluff (the 2:10 a.m. freight horn is the show's clock). Nearest
real airport: Santa Barbara (SBA), fifty-five minutes south; LAX is three hours by car or a Surfliner-and-FlyAway
odyssey. San Francisco: five hours north.

**Climate and light.** Late summer: fog in the morning ("the marine layer"), burning off by eleven; 70s by afternoon; fog
back by dusk; 55–58°F at night. September and October are the warmest, clearest months (Indian summer, Santa Ana days
when the wind turns and the air smells like hot sage and fire). November rains begin. Winter: green hills, storms,
big surf. Monarch butterflies overwinter in the eucalyptus Grove from late October to February.

**Reputation.** Elite public flagship: top-15 public university, Nobel laureates in physics and economics, a ferocious
honors college, a party reputation it hates and earns. Intensely secular and progressive. About 7% of students identify as
practicing Catholics; Newman's Sunday attendance is about 600 across five Masses.

### 25.1 Campus geography (north to south, east to west)
- **The Lagoon** (north edge): a brackish lagoon with a footpath, egrets, and a bench where people go to break up.
- **The Anacapa residential complex** (northeast, on the lagoon): four freshman halls — **Delgado**, Cabrillo, Portolá, and
  Serra (Serra houses sophomores and Preview Weekend overflow).
- **The Commons Lawn** (center): the quad. Big lawn, Frisbees, sunbathers, protest tables, the **Ferrer Tower** (a 1966
  carillon tower that plays the Westminster chimes off-key on the quarter hour and "Hotel California" on the last day of
  finals by tradition).
  - **Ferrer Tower (E10 canon):** ~130 ft of 1966 board-formed concrete; a steel door at the base (warped by the Oct 13 storm; Facilities'
    caution tape; a new padlock by Saturday); **a hundred and sixty steps** in a square shaft with a cold steel rail and window slits; at the
    top a glassed **playing cabin** with a wooden-baton keyboard and pedalboard (laminate: AUTOMATIC SYSTEM ENGAGED 7 AM–10 PM · DO NOT OPERATE
    CLAVIER) under the open bell chamber; the bells cast in Holland, 1965 (Researcher: a plausible count ≥23). **The great bell's inscription:
    VIVOS VOCO · MORTUOS PLANGO · FULGURA FRANGO** ("I call the living, I mourn the dead, I break the lightning"). **One bell flat** — on the third
    of the scale; Lena: a blue note. From the cabin: Delgado's grid, the Lagoon, the hills east, and west past the Grove the dead light on the
    Point. Chimes 7 a.m.–10 p.m.
- **Hollis Hall** (west side of the Commons): the only 1920s building, Spanish Revival, red tile, a cloister walk with
  bougainvillea; Philosophy, Classics, Religious Studies. **Hale's office: Hollis 314** (third floor, a window on the sea,
  a carpet with a wine stain shaped like Italy). Seminar room **Hollis 302** (PHIL 9H; long oak table, twelve chairs,
  a radiator that knocks). **Hollis 108** (Evan's section; a basement room with one window at ankle height).
- **Sandoval Hall 1** (east of the Commons): a 1971 lecture hall, 400 orange flip-down seats, a stage, a wireless mic Hale
  refuses to clip on. PHIL 1 lectures Tue/Thu 9:30–10:45.
- **Anacapa Commons** (the freshman dining hall, between Delgado and Serra): salad bar, a waffle iron with a line, Kevin's
  protein ratios.
- **Pacifica Library** ("the Brick"; south side of the Commons): eight-story brutalist tower; the 8th floor is silent
  study with a view of the Channel Islands on clear days; the 24-hour study room in the basement during finals.
- **Sciences** (east): the Chem building where Kevin lives in his head; the **Marine Lab** on the beach below the east
  bluff with the touch tank (Becca borrows a hermit crab from it, E08).
- **The Student Union** ("the UCen"): a Panda Express, a Jamba Juice, the *Marisol Tide* newsroom upstairs (Margot).
- **Campus Point** (south): the beach below the bluff; a surf break for beginners; the bluff-top bench where Jack smokes.
- **The Grove** (west, between campus and Las Olas): a eucalyptus forest; the bike path cuts through it; monarchs in
  winter; at night the trees creak and drop bark like shed skin.
- **The creek mouth** (added E06 plan): the Lagoon's outlet creek runs under the Grove and crosses the beach below it,
  between the Las Olas bluff stairs and Campus Point; shin-deep and cold, wider after rain; at night you hear it before you
  see it. The beach route from Las Olas to campus has to wade it. (🔒 Theo crossed it, soaked to the knees, on his way from
  the Point to Serra Hall, ~12:40 a.m. April 26, 2009.) A lifeguard tower (closed after Labor Day) stands on the sand at
  Campus Point; the Marine Lab stairs climb the bluff beside it.

### 25.2 Las Olas (the student town, west of the Grove)
A square mile of bluff-top rentals, duplexes and surf houses — dense, filthy, gorgeous, loud. Bikes everywhere. Couches on
roofs. Jasmine and trash cans. The ocean at the end of every street.
- **Seacliff Road** runs along the bluff edge to the Point. **Greek row** is its eastern half: Pi Lambda Chi (white
  colonial, black shutters, the best porch), Kappa Alpha Delta, Sigma Rho (the lacrosse house), Alpha Tau Kappa. West of the
  Greek houses Seacliff becomes surf rentals.
- **The Lighthouse** is the last house on Seacliff Road before the Point: a shingled 1950s two-story with a deck and a
  back porch that looks north to the Point and the old light, rented each year by a new crew of senior surfers; named for
  the view. A chain-link fence at the back of the lot; a gap where the fence post rotted; beyond it, a dirt path along the
  bluff to the Point.
- **Del Playa Lane** (Julian's garage studio; Sol Holm's falling-down house with the darkroom — Skye rents a room from Jan 2010; Hale's bungalow at the far end on the cliff).
  **Hale's bungalow (E14 canon):** the last lot on the cliff end of Del Playa — a 1920s board-and-batten bungalow gone silver, a porch with the canvas
  chair (E12), a deck cantilevered over the bluff on old pilings; inside, books to the ceiling on every wall that isn't window, a woodstove, a Turkish
  rug with Berkeley on it, a dining table made from a door; west, the sea; north-west across the dark, the Point and its dead light (🔒 he looks; never
  glossed); a Blackwell's paper bag of Radcliffe Camera postcards in the desk drawer (🔒 "used three"); his mother's Yorkshire-pudding tin (🔒).
- **Shipwreck Cove**: a beach reached by wooden stairs from the end of Del Playa; bonfire beach; the ribs of a 1920s
  schooner at low tide.

### 25.3 Marisol Point
The westernmost headland: a grassy bluff seventy feet above a reef break (the Point break — expert surfers only), with
the **old Point Marisol Light** (a squat white 1890s Coast Guard light, decommissioned 1967, now a locked shell with a
county sign) and a **low stone wall** (knee-high on the land side, a sheer drop on the sea side). A small dirt lot off the
end of Seacliff Road. The **white wooden cross** at the wall, with Nora's name burned into the crossbar. Fresh flowers every
Sunday. Ice plant, wind, the sound of sea lions from the rocks.

### 25.4 St. Brendan the Navigator Newman Center
Across Ocean Road from campus, at the edge of the Grove. A 1962 A-frame church whose ceiling is a ship's hull turned upside
down (St. Brendan sailed the Atlantic in a leather boat; the architect took it literally) — Douglas-fir ribs, blue
dalle-de-verre glass, a hanging crucifix carved from driftwood. A Marian shrine in the side aisle with a votive rack and,
beneath it, **a small brass plate: NORA GRACE CALLOWAY · 1989–2009 · "LORD, TO WHOM SHALL WE GO?"** A courtyard with an
olive tree, a temperamental sprinkler and folding tables for Coffee & Donuts after the 9:30 and 11:30. The Newman house
(offices, lounge with a 1994 couch, kitchen, the library of donated books, a ping-pong table with a broken net). Osei's
office: highlife, chess board, a framed photo face-down in the drawer. The confessional: a converted coat closet with a
screen and a kneeler and a chair, so you can choose.
- **Mass schedule:** Sat Vigil 5:00 p.m.; Sun 9:30, 11:30, 5:00 and 9:00 p.m. (the college Mass, candlelit); weekdays
  12:10 p.m. **Confession:** Sat 3:30–4:45; Wed 8:00 p.m.; "whenever you knock."

### 25.5 Delgado Hall
1967 concrete, five stories, a grid of narrow windows facing the Lagoon, co-ed by room (alternating doors; men's and
women's bathrooms at each end of each floor). Home to 310 freshmen.
- **Ground floor:** lobby with a front desk (a sleepy desk attendant named Marcus), mailboxes, the **Fishbowl** (the glass-
  walled main lounge with a TV, a broken foosball table, couches that have seen things).
- **Basement:** laundry (eight washers, three working), vending machines, a piano no one admits to playing.
- **2nd floor:** **217 — Lena & Laney** (east wing, window on the Lagoon). **204 — Rafi** (roommate never showed).
- **3rd floor:** **305 — Margot** (single).
- **4th floor:** **412 — Jack & Theo** (west wing, window toward the Grove and, on clear nights, the Point light's dead
  silhouette). **420 — Kevin & Doug.** **401 — Priya (RA).** The 4th-floor lounge (smaller, with a whiteboard — Margot
  annexes it).
- **5th floor:** a door to the roof marked ALARM WILL SOUND (the alarm was disabled in 1998 with a popsicle stick; every
  class passes the secret down).
- **The east stairwell:** concrete, echoing, one window on each landing that opens six inches; best cell reception in the
  building; where people smoke illegally and make phone calls they don't want their roommates to hear. **The 2nd–3rd floor
  landing is Lena's call spot.** Jack, on the 4th floor, uses the same stairwell. Sound carries.
- **The 3 a.m. fire alarm:** about every ten days; everyone stands on the lawn in towels.

### 25.6 Town (Marisol proper, three miles east along Mission Street)
- **Mission Street:** the main drag — palms, Spanish tile, a Borders that's dying, a Blockbuster that's dying faster.
- **Old Mission Nuestra Señora del Mar** (fictional, 1790s adobe): Christmas Midnight Mass, Holy Week, weddings.
- **The Anchor** (the kitchen goes dark one Thursday night a year in September for the hood cleaners — coffee and pie only;
  S1E04): a 24-hour diner on the harbor wharf; Formica, red vinyl booths, a counter with spinning stools, a pie
  case, a jukebox with Sinatra, Otis, Patsy Cline, the Eagles, and inexplicably one Mariah Carey. Gloria Mendes runs the
  night shift; Rudy Salcedo works the line. Jack washes dishes there from S1E02 (Tue/Thu/Sat, 7 p.m.–1 a.m.; the Hobart
  dish machine). The 11 bus stops at 12:30 a.m.; Jack rides home three miles on La Flaca. Pie of the day on a chalkboard; Jack rates them (marionberry 4/10,
  "Dad would complain"; olallieberry 9/10).
- **Café Bastille:** indie coffee on Mission; mismatched chairs, French posters, Thursday open mic (Julian), a barista with
  a Che tattoo who argues with Lena about Che.
- **The Wharf Rat:** a dive bar on the wharf; fishermen, grad students, Hale in the back booth; doesn't card if Gloria
  vouches; a dartboard with a photo of Dick Cheney on it from 2004 that no one has taken down.
- **Sully's:** sports bar on Mission; fake IDs; Saints games (Lena demands it); Browns games (Jack in mourning). **(E05
  canon:)** one big projection screen and five tube TVs; the Sunday-morning crowd is transplants (a Packers table, a Steelers
  table, two Raiders guys who fight each other); Bloody Mary bar at 10 a.m.; no Abita ("Is that a cheese?"); a bell over the
  bar the owner rings for touchdowns until Lena makes him regret it; Dale at the end of the bar.
- **Lupe's:** a taco truck that parks at the Las Olas end of Seacliff from 10 p.m. to 3 a.m.; carnitas, horchata, absolution.
- **Driftwood Books:** used bookstore with two cats (Boethius and Mrs. Danvers); Jack's paperbacks come from here, $2–$4.
  The owner (sixties, glasses on a beaded chain, unnamed) ships books to prisons "as the seller" for families — Jack's
  monthly book to Trumbull goes through her from S1E04; his margin notes go separately by letter.
- **Giorgio's:** pizza by the slice; Jack's culinary despair ("this isn't pizza, this is a cracker with ambitions").
- **The Walgreens on Mission Street.** (🔒 2:14 p.m., April 25, 2009.)
- **Marisol Police Department:** a stucco building on Anacapa Street.
- **Marisol Harbor:** fishing boats, sea lions on the docks, a fish market, the Coast Guard station.

### 25.7 Big Sur (added E11 plan; real places, real road — the Researcher verifies details)
Highway 1 north from San Simeon (the Hearst zebras graze by the road; the elephant seals at Piedras Blancas) to **Ragged Point** (the road narrows onto the
face of the Santa Lucias; cell signal dies), **Gorda** (a store and the most expensive gas in America), **Lucia** (a hamlet on the cliff; the road up to the
**New Camaldoli Hermitage** — Camaldolese Benedictines in white, ~1,300 ft over the sea, a chapel, a bookstore with the monks' brandy-soaked date-nut
fruitcake), **Julia Pfeiffer Burns** (**McWay Falls** onto its beach), the **Henry Miller Library**, **Nepenthe** (the terrace 800 ft up; the Welles–Hayworth
land), **Pfeiffer Beach** (the unsigned canyon road; purple sand; the keyhole rock), Big Sur village, and **Bixby Bridge** (1932; Kerouac's canyon below).
**Fictional:** the **Santa Lucia Motor Court**, a mile south of Lucia — six cabins on a shelf of the mountain, a burned-out NO on the VACANCY sign, a payphone
under a bare bulb, Verna, and one working heater (cabin 4). Condors wear numbered wing tags; everything else is a turkey vulture.

## 26. RUNNING JOKES, MOTIFS, RECURRING OBJECTS

- **The eyebrow scar.** A new story every time (§16). Track tellings. Truth reserved.
- **The Marlboros and the Reliquary.** Lena confiscates every cigarette she catches him with — takes it from his mouth or
  hand, stubs it out, and drops it into an Altoids tin she calls "the Reliquary." She keeps count, out loud. (Pilot: the
  first one goes in her cardigan pocket; the tin appears in E03.) 🔒 At the wedding, she gives him the tin: 211 cigarettes,
  each labeled with a date in her handwriting. **The tin (S1E03):** a red-and-white peppermint Altoids tin bought at the
  gift shop of Pea Soup Andersen's in Buellton on the 101, Sat Sep 5; she pours the mints into Kevin's palm and seals in
  Saturday's cigarette; on the lid in Sharpie, in her courtroom capitals, RELIQUARY, and inside, on a slip of Andersen's
  receipt paper, "No. 1 · 8/29/09 · the Lighthouse." Each later deposit gets its own slip. It lives in her cardigan pocket
  or her boot.
- **The paperback in the back pocket.** A different book most episodes; the narration always names it; Lena reads his
  margins when he isn't looking; his margins argue with the author ("NO." "Coward." "Okay, fine." "Show Lena"). Pilot:
  Walker Percy, *The Moviegoer* (1961, Vintage, spine cracked white, $3 from a Youngstown library sale) — Hale's postcard as
  bookmark. Rotation ideas: Chesterton, *Orthodoxy*; Camus, *The Plague*; O'Connor, *A Good Man Is Hard to Find*; Greene,
  *The Power and the Glory*; Dostoevsky, *The Brothers Karamazov* (too fat for a pocket — it becomes a joke); Hopkins,
  *Poems and Prose*; Pascal, *Pensées*; Kierkegaard, *Fear and Trembling*; Waugh, *Brideshead*; Hale's own book (Jack
  reading it at Mass by accident is an E08 gag). **Played/planned:** E01 *The Moviegoer*; E02 *Spe Salvi*; E03 *Brideshead*
  (→ Danny, E04); **E04 Hopkins, *Poems and Prose*** (Penguin, Gardner; a Mooney library discard) — pencil *Show Lena* beside
  "Thou art indeed just, Lord." **E05 Flannery O'Connor, *A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories*** (a Harvest paperback
  from the milk crate, a Mooney senior-English castoff); the Benedict holy card moves into it; the Hopkins stays on the desk
  until it goes to Danny in October. The Misfit's "I can't make what all I done wrong fit what all I gone through in
  punishment" is available to Jack in the duel (🔒 Danny). Seeds E12's O'Connor duel and Lena's Halloween costume.
- **The Miraculous Medal.** Lena touches it when thinking **or lying**. The player knows this from their own brief; Jack
  doesn't, until he notices the lie-tell in S2E05 (journal note). Before that, the narration simply records each touch
  without comment. Writers: every medal-touch must be consistent (only when she is genuinely thinking hard or lying) — it is
  a fair-play clue system the player can read before Jack can.
- **The St. Michael medal.** Jack's from his confirmation (Danny was his sponsor — 🔒). He holds it when he prays the St.
  Michael prayer. In S4 he gives it to Theo the night before Theo surrenders.
- **The postcard.** "Come and say it to my face. —A.H." Radcliffe Camera, Oxford. Jack's (2008), Lena's (2008), Nora's
  (2007).
- **The jean jacket.** Fresno Fair pin. Guadalupe patch.
- **The Memorare.** Nora's last prayer; Lena's prayer; Nonna's prayer; Theo knows it without knowing how (he heard it once).
- **John 6:68.** "Lord, to whom shall we go?" On Nora's plaque; in her journal; the last line of the series finale.
- **Bread.** The Anchor's toast; Nonna's bread; Lena's mother's French bread for po'boys; the host. The show's secret
  metaphor; never named in narration.
- **The fog.** Arrives at dusk like a tide. Things happen in it.
- **The 2:10 a.m. freight horn.** Jack counts the cars when he can't sleep.
- **The monarchs.** They arrive at All Souls. They cluster for warmth. Nobody who sees them for the first time talks.
- **Margot's whiteboard.** "USEFUL IDIOTS FOR CHRISTIAN NATIONALISM" — a running tally (J vs. L), later expanded ("PATRIARCHY
  UPHELD THIS WEEK," "INTERNALIZED MISOGYNY: LENA, UNREPENTANT"), with Jack and Lena adding their own categories ("MARGOT:
  FEELINGS DETECTED").
- **"Theodore."** Theo is only called this when he's in trouble. When Jack calls him "Theodore" for the first time with
  real anger, it lands like a slap.
- **Laney's pageant wave**, deployed at funerals and police officers.
- **Priya's laminated notes.** A new laminated sign every episode ("THE MICROWAVE IS NOT A PLACE OF WORSHIP." "PER MY
  EMAIL: NO.").
- **Kevin's quarter-zips.** Color-coded to his mood; when he wears a plain T-shirt something is very wrong.
- **Fr. Osei's sprinkler.** He's always fixing it. It's never fixed. (🔒 In the series finale, it's finally fixed — by Theo.)
- **Hale's wine-cuff.** The linen jacket with the stain. When he shows up in a clean jacket, he's in trouble.
- **The 3 a.m. fire alarm** (S1; Doug, sleepwalking).
- **The Anchor pie ratings.** Jack's chalkboard rankings, which Gloria posts by the register.
- **Gina's texts.** All lowercase, no punctuation, devastating: "nonna asked if u have a girlfriend i said yes shes a nun".
- **Jack's flip phone**: the cracked hinge; the T9; the screen that only lights at an angle.
- **The paired papers.** From S1E02, Hale's designated antagonists: every week Jack and Lena swap two-page papers and
  annotate each other in red. Her margins: "NO." "Cite me." His: "This is the best paragraph I've read this year. I hate
  it." The margins are where they say what they can't say out loud. (Payoff: E14, E22.)
- **La Flaca.** Rafi's rusted single-speed beach cruiser with coaster brakes, lent to Jack "till Christmas" (S1E02): "Not
  stolen. Abandoned. My abuela says there's about a week's difference."
- **The Benedict holy card.** Jack's bookmark in *Spe Salvi* (S1E02); it migrates from book to book all season.
- **The Odyssey's back glass.** E03–E04 the Saints countdown in La Vang car-wash polish; from E05 it carries the record
  ("1–0," and so on), updated by Lena the morning after each game; Kevin pretends to object. It reads 13–0 by Gaudete.
- **The fleur-de-lis.** Lena paints one in gold on Jack's cheekbone at the opener (E05, Laney's eyeliner); he forgets to
  wash it off before Mass. On game days afterward she checks his face like a sacristan checking a candle.
- **Lena's boots.** Brown Justins, resoled twice. When she's wearing Keds, she's happy. When she's barefoot, something's
  wrong. (E06: barefoot on the Pi Lam steps with the boots beside her, and she carries them the whole long way home.)
- **Hale's books.** From E06 Jack carries Hale's own copy of Bernard Williams, *Moral Luck* (Cambridge paperback, Hale's
  Oxford pencil in the margins — "No." "Bernard, really." — a man who argued with his teacher the way Jack argues with his
  authors). "Bring it back with your margins in it." 🔒 Hale is courting him; the book is a leash as much as a gift.
- **Ray's light.** The clip-on bike light from Ray Ochoa's trunk (E06), on La Flaca's handlebar from then on.
- **Danny's letters.** Lined paper, block-capital addresses, "Professor," signed "—D." Jack keeps them in the milk crate
  inside the Hopkins until the Hopkins ships, then inside whatever replaces it.
- **The paperback, E07:** Augustine, *Confessions* (Penguin Classics, Pine-Coffin), CARDINAL MOONEY H.S. LIBRARY — DISCARD,
  bought for a dime ("Augustine for a dime" — Lena, E04); Jack's margins thickest in Book IV (the friend who died). Hale's
  Williams moves to the desk (one pencil *No.* so far — owed back with margins); the Benedict holy card moves into Augustine.
- **The roof door.** Delgado's fifth floor: EMERGENCY EXIT ONLY · ALARM WILL SOUND, and under it, in a Sharpie gone brown,
  *(it won't)*; a popsicle stick in the strike since 1998. The roof: tar and gravel, the elevator housing, two HVAC boxes, a
  parapet to the hip; the Lagoon one way, the hills the other. **E07 (the equinox) and E22 (a week before the solstice) are
  its two big nights** — equal night, longest night (arc #65).
- **Margot's whiteboard, E07:** "TUESDAY — NO SCORE. (BEREAVEMENT.)" — the first time she suspends the tally. Never explained.
- **Hale's Housman for Danny** (E07, `e6_hale_danny`): a wartime pocket *A Shropshire Lad*, foxed, no margins — "They'd only
  erase them." 🔒 kindness and leash.
- **Gloria's people-ratings, E07:** Margot, sight unseen, from Jack's description: "Rhubarb. Tart, and nobody can decide if
  it's a fruit." (It's a vegetable. That's the point.)
- **The paperback, E08: Thérèse of Lisieux, *Story of a Soul*** (ICS Publications, John Clarke's translation — Researcher to confirm
  the edition and page wording), $3 off the Driftwood cart **Tuesday Sep 29** — the afternoon he hears her tell Mrs. Fitch "She's my
  middle name" — read Tuesday night after the Anchor and Wednesday morning **in pencil** (his margins
  are always pencil — the prison taught him erasable). Margins: *Easy for you.* beside the elevator ("too little to climb the rough
  stairway of perfection"); *NO.*; *She'd have hated Hale.*; *Okay, fine.* beside the trial of faith and the table of sinners; and,
  beside her two missionary "brothers," *Can a man and a woman be friends? Ask L.* He gives it to Lena at midnight on her feast;
  she will not let him erase a word ("Don't you dare"); on the duel's HEART path she writes back under *Easy for you.*: *Empty
  hands. —L.* (the Act of Oblation). **She keeps it.** After E08 Jack carries Hale's Williams again (margins still owed).
- **The Hopkins, erased.** Before it ships to Trumbull (Thu Oct 1, through Driftwood, with Hale's Housman), every margin comes out
  with the Pink Pearl — and **Lena erases *Show Lena* herself**, in the laundry room, in the freeze: "There. He can have it." (The
  small generous devastating gesture of E08; spend no other.) Danny's first letter, which lived inside it in the milk crate, moves
  into the Williams.
- **The Delgado laundry room** (basement): eight washers, three working; the dryers buzz like a game-show loss; the piano nobody
  admits to playing; Priya's laminate: LAUNDRY ROOM HOURS 7 A.M.–11 P.M. (THIS MEANS YOU.). Nonna's card in Jack's basket: *Whites
  in HOT. Darks in COLD. MEDALS OFF.* (E01) — Lena reads it and nearly laughs, in the freeze, and doesn't.
- **Lupe's "para los novios."** Lupe gives free horchata to couples; she gives Jack and Lena two; they say "We're friends" at the
  same time; "Claro."
- **Thomas the crab** (E08): a *Pagurus* hermit crab on loan from the Marine Lab touch tank, in a Tupperware of seawater, named for
  the First Way. Back in the tank by noon Saturday.
- **Gloria's people-ratings, E08:** Becca, sight unseen, from Jack's description: **"Apple. That's the one you bring home to your
  mother."** Then: "What happened to the pecan?" "She has a boyfriend." "Hm."
- **Bishop Berkeley** (Hale's deaf greyhound, named for the idealist: *esse est percipi*) on page at last (E08, the Blessing); the
  frayed leash from Hale's office door.
- **Gloria's people-ratings, E09:** Becca in person — "Apple. Told you, hon."; Wes on sight — **"Peach."** (Peach was Lena's mother's
  crust in Malibu; nobody says so.)
- **Theo's expeditions** (E09): itineraries on Meridian Pictures letterhead; "Landfall" at the Madonna Inn (pink everything; the
  champagne cake; Grandmother Ashby took him every summer and called it vulgar and loved it).
- **Leif Erikson Day** (Oct 9): Margot observes it instead of Columbus Day, on the whiteboard, every year.
- **The air mattress in 412** (E09): an Aerobed Theo bought Friday "for guests"; Wes made it with hospital corners.
- **Wes's flip phone:** scuffed, black, a grainy camera; the photo of Mémère's ring (🔒 Jack knows about the ring when Wes ends it (S1E13),
  and tells her only on Fat Tuesday in New Orleans (S2E10); the ring itself — #78).
- **Wes's green Tulane sweatshirt** (E09 dawn; left behind): on Lena all of E10, under the oatmeal cardigan; once, in the tower, under Jack's
  Carhartt (one image; never glossed).
- **The Ferrer bells** (E10): the 5 a.m. Saints; the flat bell ("That's not flat. That's *New Orleans*."); the six o'clock chime; registry #71.
- **The basement piano** (Delgado, the dead F): Lena is the one who plays it and doesn't admit it — "Who do you think plays the piano in the
  basement?" (E10). Two years of piano at the Rosary.
- **The paperback, E10:** Walker Percy, ***The Moviegoer*** again — the pilot's copy out of the milk crate for the heart paper (Binx's "search");

# PART V — THE GAME IN STORY TERMS

## 27. Resolve (hidden; 0–10; both default 7)

Resolve is not willpower in the abstract. It's **the strength to choose the good thing when the easy thing is close.** It
is fed by grace and good company and drained by exhaustion, loneliness, booze and near-misses.

**Jack's resolve — raised by (+1 typical, +2 big):** going to Mass (+1); confession (+2); real prayer chosen by the player
(+1); a night of sleep after a crisis (+1); a good, sober night with friends — Kevin, Margot, Osei's chess (+1); calling
home and it going well (+1); telling the truth when it costs (+1); turning down a drink/drug/cigarette when it's offered
(+1, only when the refusal is a real choice); helping someone (carrying Laney home) (+1).
**Lowered by:** each real drink after the first (−1); cigarettes (−0 alone, −1 with drinking); drugs (−2); loneliness — a
night alone after bad news (−1); a fight with Lena (−1) or with Theo (−1); a charged near-miss with anyone (−1); lying to
someone who trusts him (−1); skipping Mass (−1); bad news from home (−1); sleeping on a couch after being sexiled (−1, a
joke with teeth).
**Hard rule in mechanics:** with anyone but Lena, no option ever leads past the near-miss, at any resolve. Low resolve
with Becca or Skye (or Lena with Julian) makes the scene closer, longer and costlier (−1 to −2, a confession owed), and the
line still holds — an exit is always on the menu, and if the player won't take it, the other person or the world does.

**Lena's resolve (writer-set).** Writers set it via scene `set` at the top of key scenes, based on her canon life: her
prayer life (high baseline), Wes (a slow drain S1), Laney (draining), her grief and secrets (deep drain when stirred —
the Times article, All Souls, the anniversary), exhaustion (finals), alcohol (she drinks moderately; when she drinks to
forget, it's a signal). Track her value in `continuity.md` at the end of every episode.
